function_by_symbol.CHD3: CHD3 encodes chromodomain helicase DNA binding protein 3. It is an ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor that binds and distorts nucleosomal DNA. It functions as a component of the histone deacetylase NuRD complex which participates in the remodeling of chromatin. It participates in transcriptional repression as part of the NuRD complex.
function_by_symbol.CHD4: CHD4 encodes ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler CHD4. Based in part on similarity, it is an ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor that binds and distorts nucleosomal DNA. It functions as a component of the histone deacetylase NuRD complex which participates in the remodeling of chromatin. It localizes to acetylated damaged chromatin in a ZMYND8-dependent manner, to promote transcriptional repression and double-strand break repair by homologous recombination.
function_by_symbol.CHEK1: CHEK1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase Chk1. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine-protein kinase which is required for checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest and activation of DNA repair in response to the presence of DNA damage or unreplicated DNA. It may also negatively regulate cell cycle progression during unperturbed cell cycles. This regulation is achieved by a number of mechanisms that together help to preserve the integrity of the genome.
function_by_symbol.CHIC2: CHIC2 encodes a protein containing a cysteine-rich hydrophobic CHIC motif. The protein has been localized to vesicular structures and the plasma membrane. These observations establish features of its cellular distribution, while its detailed molecular activity remains less well defined than that of a characterized receptor or enzyme.
function_by_symbol.CHIT1: CHIT1 encodes chitinase 1. It degrades chitin, chitotriose and chitobiose. It may participate in the defense against nematodes and other pathogens.
function_by_symbol.CHST12: CHST12 encodes carbohydrate sulfotransferase 12. It catalyzes the transfer of sulfate to position 4 of the N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residue of chondroitin and desulfated dermatan sulfate. It does not form 4, 6-di-O-sulfated GalNAc when chondroitin sulfate C is used as an acceptor.
function_by_symbol.CIITA: CIITA encodes MHC class II transactivator. It may act in a coactivator-like fashion through protein-protein interactions by contacting factors binding to the proximal MHC class II promoter, to elements of the transcription machinery, or both. Alternatively it may activate HLA class II transcription by modifying proteins that bind to the MHC class II promoter. It exhibits intrinsic GTP-stimulated acetyltransferase activity.
function_by_symbol.CITED2: CITED2 encodes cbp/p300-interacting transactivator 2. It functions as a bridge, linking TFAP2 transcription factors and the p300/CBP transcriptional coactivator complex in order to stimulate TFAP2-mediated transcriptional activation. It positively regulates TGF-beta signaling through its association with the SMAD/p300/CBP-mediated transcriptional coactivator complex. It stimulates the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors PPARA transcriptional activity.
function_by_symbol.CKS1B: CKS1B encodes cyclin-dependent kinases regulatory subunit 1. It forms part of the substrate-specific subunit in cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes. The E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase activity is regulated by the COP9 signalosome (CSN), which restores the ligase to its inactive state and resets the ligase for substrate recognition by reversing the activating neddylation on the cullin. It binds to the catalytic subunit of the cyclin dependent kinases and is essential for their biological function.
function_by_symbol.CLDN18: CLDN18 encodes claudin-18. Based in part on similarity, it participates in alveolar fluid homeostasis via regulation of alveolar epithelial tight junction composition and therefore ion transport and solute permeability, potentially via downstream regulation of the actin cytoskeleton organization and beta-2-adrenergic signaling. It is required for lung alveolarization and maintenance of the paracellular alveolar epithelial barrier. It acts to maintain epithelial progenitor cell proliferation and organ size, via regulation of YAP1 localization away from the nucleus and thereby restriction of YAP1 target gene transcription.
function_by_symbol.CLEC14A: CLEC14A encodes a C-type lectin-like protein involved in endothelial cell adhesion and blood-vessel formation. Its functions include filopodia formation, cell migration, and tube formation. These activities connect interactions at the cell surface with the structural changes required for angiogenesis; expression in endothelium is distinct from evidence that a particular sequence variant drives a tumor.
function_by_symbol.CLECL1: CLECL1 encodes C-type lectin like 1. It functions in mediating immune cell-cell interactions. It functions as a T-cell costimulatory molecule, enhancing anti-CD3-induced proliferation. May play a role in the interaction of dendritic cells with T-cells and the cells of the adaptive immune response.
function_by_symbol.CLIP1: CLIP1 encodes CAP-Gly domain-containing linker protein 1. It binds to the plus end of microtubules and regulates the dynamics of the microtubule cytoskeleton. It promotes microtubule growth and microtubule bundling. It links cytoplasmic vesicles to microtubules and thereby plays an important role in intracellular vesicle trafficking.
function_by_symbol.CLTC: CLTC encodes clathrin heavy chain 1. Based in part on similarity, clathrin is the major protein of the polyhedral coat of coated pits and vesicles. It functions as a component of the TACC3/ch-TOG/clathrin complex proposed to contribute to stabilization of kinetochore fibers of the mitotic spindle by acting as inter-microtubule bridge. The TACC3/ch-TOG/clathrin complex is required for the maintenance of kinetochore fiber tension.
function_by_symbol.CMTR2: CMTR2 encodes cap-specific mRNA (nucleoside-2'-O-)-methyltransferase 2. It methylates the ribose of the second nucleotide of a m(7)GpppG-capped mRNA and small nuclear RNA (snRNA) (cap0) to produce m(7)GpppRmpNm (cap2). It recognizes a guanosine cap on RNA independently of its N(7) methylation status. It displays a preference for cap1 RNAs.
function_by_symbol.CNOT9: CNOT9 encodes CCR4-NOT transcription complex subunit 9. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation and general transcription regulation. Additional complex functions may be a consequence of its influence on mRNA expression. It participates in down-regulation of MYB- and JUN-dependent transcription.
function_by_symbol.COBL: COBL encodes cordon-bleu WH2 repeat protein. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton. It regulates neuron morphogenesis and increases branching of axons and dendrites. It regulates dendrite branching in Purkinje cells.
function_by_symbol.COL21A1: COL21A1 encodes the alpha chain of type XXI collagen, a fibril-associated collagen with interrupted helices. It occurs in tissues containing type I collagen and contributes to extracellular-matrix integrity. Its normal role therefore concerns organization and support of the matrix surrounding cells rather than intracellular signal transduction or direct control of DNA repair.
function_by_symbol.COP1: COP1 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase COP1. It is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins. E3 ubiquitin ligases accept ubiquitin from an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme in the form of a thioester and then directly transfers the ubiquitin to targeted substrates. It participates in JUN ubiquitination and degradation.
function_by_symbol.CR1: CR1 encodes complement C3b/C4b receptor 1 (Knops blood group). It mediates the binding by these cells of particles and immune complexes that have activated complement to eliminate them from the circulation. It also acts in the inhibition of spontaneous complement activation by impairing the formation and function of the alternative and classical pathway C3/C5 convertases, and by serving as a cofactor for the cleavage by factor I of C3b to iC3b, C3c and C3d,g, and of C4b to C4c and C4d.
function_by_symbol.CRB1: CRB1 encodes crumbs cell polarity complex component 1. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to photoreceptor morphogenesis in the retina. It may maintain cell polarization and adhesion.
function_by_symbol.CRBN: CRBN encodes protein cereblon. Based in part on similarity, it is a substrate recognition component of a DCX (DDB1-CUL4-X-box) E3 protein ligase complex that mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins, such as MEIS2, ILF2, GLUL, IKZF1 and CSNK1A1. It maintains presynaptic glutamate release and consequently cognitive functions, such as memory and learning, by negatively regulating large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channels in excitatory neurons. It likely to function by regulating the assembly and neuronal surface expression of BK channels via its interaction with KCNT1.
function_by_symbol.CREB1: CREB1 encodes cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, transcription activation is enhanced by the TORC coactivators which act independently of Ser-119 phosphorylation. It participates in different cellular processes including the synchronization of circadian rhythmicity and the differentiation of adipose cells. It regulates the expression of apoptotic and inflammatory response factors in cardiomyocytes in response to ERFE-mediated activation of AKT signaling.
function_by_symbol.CREB3L1: CREB3L1 encodes cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 3-like protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it binds the DNA consensus sequence 5'-GTGXGCXGC-3'. It contributes to bone formation through the transcription of COL1A1, and possibly COL1A2, and the secretion of bone matrix proteins. It directly binds to the UPR element (UPRE)-like sequence in an osteoblast-specific COL1A1 promoter region and induces its transcription.
function_by_symbol.CREB3L2: CREB3L2 encodes cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 3-like protein 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor involved in unfolded protein response (UPR). The released N-terminal cytosolic domain is translocated to the nucleus to effect transcription of specific target genes. It contributes to chondrogenesis by activating the transcription of SEC23A, which promotes the transport and secretion of cartilage matrix proteins, and possibly that of ER biogenesis-related genes.
function_by_symbol.CREBBP: CREBBP encodes the CBP transcriptional coactivator and acetyltransferase, which modifies histones and other proteins to regulate gene expression. It acetylates histones, giving a specific tag for transcriptional activation. It mediates acetylation of histone H3 at 'Lys-18' and 'Lys-27' (H3K18ac and H3K27ac, respectively). It also acetylates non-histone proteins, like DDX21, FBL, IRF2, MAFG, NCOA3, POLR1E/PAF53 and FOXO1.
function_by_symbol.CRKL: CRKL encodes an adaptor protein containing SH2 and SH3 interaction domains. It participates in intracellular signal transmission through protein interactions, including pathways linked to RAS and JUN kinases. These domains organize signaling assemblies; they do not make CRKL itself an independently acting protein kinase.
function_by_symbol.CRLF2: CRLF2 encodes cytokine receptor-like factor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor for thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP). It forms a functional complex with TSLP and IL7R which is capable of stimulating cell proliferation through activation of STAT3 and STAT5. It also activates JAK2.
function_by_symbol.CRTC1: CRTC1 encodes CREB-regulated transcription coactivator 1. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a coactivator, in the SIK/TORC signaling pathway, being active when dephosphorylated and acts independently of CREB1 'Ser-133' phosphorylation. It enhances the interaction of CREB1 with TAF4. It regulates the expression of specific CREB-activated genes such as the steroidogenic gene, StAR.
function_by_symbol.CRTC3: CRTC3 encodes CREB-regulated transcription coactivator 3. It functions as a coactivator, in the SIK/TORC signaling pathway, being active when dephosphorylated and acts independently of CREB1 'Ser-133' phosphorylation. It enhances the interaction of CREB1 with TAF4. It regulates the expression of specific CREB-activated genes such as the steroidogenic gene, StAR.
function_by_symbol.CSF1: CSF1 encodes macrophage colony-stimulating factor 1. It promotes the release of pro-inflammatory chemokines, and thereby plays an important role in innate immunity and in inflammatory processes. It contributes to the regulation of osteoclast proliferation and differentiation, the regulation of bone resorption, and is required for normal bone development.
function_by_symbol.CSF1R: CSF1R encodes macrophage colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for CSF1 and IL34 and plays an essential role in the regulation of survival, proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic precursor cells, especially mononuclear phagocytes, such as macrophages and monocytes. It promotes the release of pro-inflammatory chemokines in response to IL34 and CSF1, and thereby plays an important role in innate immunity and in inflammatory processes. It contributes to the regulation of osteoclast proliferation and differentiation, the regulation of bone resorption, and is required for normal bone and tooth development.
function_by_symbol.CTCF: CTCF encodes transcriptional repressor CTCF. Based in part on similarity, it is a chromatin binding factor that binds to DNA sequence specific sites and regulates the 3D structure of chromatin. It binds together strands of DNA, thus forming chromatin loops, and anchors DNA to cellular structures, such as the nuclear lamina. It defines the boundaries between active and heterochromatic DNA via binding to chromatin insulators, thereby preventing interaction between promoter and nearby enhancers and silencers.
function_by_symbol.CTLA4: CTLA4 encodes cytotoxic T-lymphocyte protein 4. It functions as a decoy receptor: the affinity of CTLA4 for its natural B7 family ligands, CD80 and CD86, is considerably stronger than the affinity of their cognate stimulatory coreceptor CD28.
function_by_symbol.CTNNA1: CTNNA1 encodes catenin alpha-1. Based in part on similarity, it associates with the cytoplasmic domain of a variety of cadherins. The association of catenins to cadherins produces a complex which is linked to the actin filament network, and which seems to be of primary importance for cadherins cell-adhesion properties. It can associate with both E- and N-cadherins.
function_by_symbol.CTR9: CTR9 encodes RNA polymerase-associated protein CTR9 homolog. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the PAF1 complex (PAF1C) which has multiple functions during transcription by RNA polymerase II and is implicated in regulation of development and maintenance of embryonic stem cell pluripotency. PAF1C associates with RNA polymerase II through interaction with POLR2A CTD non-phosphorylated and 'Ser-2'- and 'Ser-5'-phosphorylated forms and is involved in transcriptional elongation, acting both independently and synergistically with TCEA1 and in cooperation with the DSIF complex and HTATSF1. PAF1C is required for transcription of Hox and Wnt target genes.
function_by_symbol.CUL3: CUL3 encodes cullin-3. It is a core component of multiple cullin-RING-based BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes which mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins. The E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase activity of the complex is dependent on the neddylation of the cullin subunit and is inhibited by the association of the deneddylated cullin subunit with TIP120A/CAND1. The functional specificity of the BCR complex depends on the BTB domain-containing protein as the substrate recognition component.
function_by_symbol.CXCR4: CXCR4 encodes C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor for the C-X-C chemokine CXCL12/SDF-1 that transduces a signal by increasing intracellular calcium ion levels and enhancing MAPK1/MAPK3 activation. CXCR4 is coupled to G(i) G alpha proteins and mediates inhibition of adenylate cyclase. It participates in the AKT signaling cascade.
function_by_symbol.CXXC5: CXXC5 encodes CXXC-type zinc finger protein 5. Based in part on similarity, it may indirectly participate in activation of the NF-kappa-B and MAPK pathways. It functions as a mediator of BMP4-mediated modulation of canonical Wnt signaling activity in neural stem cells. It is required for DNA damage-induced ATM phosphorylation, p53 activation and cell cycle arrest.
function_by_symbol.CYLD: CYLD encodes ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase CYLD. Based in part on similarity, it negatively regulates NF-kappa-B activation by deubiquitinating upstream signaling factors, thereby preventing recruitment of TAB2 and TAB3. It contributes to the regulation of cell survival, inflammation and innate immune response, via its effects on NF-kappa-B. RIPK1 deubiquitination regulates the kinase activity of RIPK1, promotes assembly of death-inducing complexes and TNF-induced apoptosis and necroptosis.
function_by_symbol.CYP19A1: CYP19A1 encodes aromatase. It catalyzes three successive oxidations of C19 androgens: two conventional oxidations at C19 yielding 19-hydroxy and 19-oxo/19-aldehyde derivatives, followed by a third oxidative aromatization step that involves C1-beta hydrogen abstraction combined with cleavage of the C10-C19 bond to yield a phenolic A ring and formic acid. It converts dihydrotestosterone to delta1,10-dehydro 19-nordihydrotestosterone and may play a role in homeostasis of this potent androgen. It also displays 2-hydroxylase activity toward estrone.
function_by_symbol.CYP2C8: CYP2C8 encodes cytochrome P450 family 2 subfamily C member 8. It catalyzes the hydroxylation of carbon-hydrogen bonds. It metabolizes all trans-retinoic acid toward its 4-hydroxylated form. It displays 16-alpha hydroxylase activity toward estrogen steroid hormones, 17beta-estradiol (E2) and estrone (E1).
function_by_symbol.CYP4A11: CYP4A11 encodes cytochrome P450 family 4 subfamily A member 11. It catalyzes predominantly the oxidation of the terminal carbon (omega-oxidation) of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids, the catalytic efficiency decreasing in the following order: dodecanoic > tetradecanoic > (9Z)-octadecenoic > (9Z,12Z)-octadecadienoic > hexadecanoic acid. It functions as a major omega-hydroxylase for dodecanoic (lauric) acid in liver. It participates in omega-hydroxylation of (5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z)-eicosatetraenoic acid (arachidonate) to 20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (20-HETE), a signaling molecule acting both as vasoconstrictive and natriuretic with overall effect on arterial blood pressure.
function_by_symbol.CYP7B1: CYP7B1 encodes cytochrome P450 family 7 subfamily B member 1. Based in part on similarity, it catalyzes the hydroxylation of carbon hydrogen bonds of steroids with a preference for 7-alpha position. It hydroxylates oxysterols, including 25-hydroxycholesterol and (25R)-cholest-5-ene-3beta,26-diol toward 7-alpha hydroxy derivatives, which may be transported to the liver and converted to bile acids. It metabolizes androstanoids toward 6- or 7-alpha hydroxy derivatives.
function_by_symbol.DAXX: DAXX encodes a histone chaperone and regulatory protein that participates with ATRX in histone H3.3 deposition and chromatin maintenance. It is a transcription corepressor known to repress transcriptional potential of several sumoylated transcription factors. Its transcription repressor activity is modulated by recruiting it to subnuclear compartments like the nucleolus or PML/POD/ND10 nuclear bodies through interactions with MCSR1 and PML, respectively. It seems to regulate transcription in PML/POD/ND10 nuclear bodies together with PML and may influence TNFRSF6-dependent apoptosis thereby.
function_by_symbol.DCAF13: DCAF13 encodes DDB1 and CUL4 associated factor 13. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit. It functions as a maternal factor that regulates oocyte and zygotic chromatin tightness during maternal to zygotic transition. It is also involved in the transformation of the endometrium into the decidua, known as decidualization, providing a solid foundation for implantation of blastocysts.
function_by_symbol.DCLRE1C: DCLRE1C encodes protein artemis. It is required for V(D)J recombination, the process by which exons encoding the antigen-binding domains of immunoglobulins and T-cell receptor proteins are assembled from individual V, (D), and J gene segments. V(D)J recombination is initiated by the lymphoid specific RAG endonuclease complex, which generates site specific DNA double strand breaks (DSBs). These ends are independently repaired by the non homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway to form coding and signal joints respectively.
function_by_symbol.DCTN1: DCTN1 encodes dynactin subunit 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. It contributes to dynein-mediated retrograde transport of vesicles and organelles along microtubules by recruiting and tethering dynein to microtubules. It binds to both dynein and microtubules providing a link between specific cargos, microtubules and dynein.
function_by_symbol.DCUN1D1: DCUN1D1 encodes DCN1-like protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex for neddylation. It promotes neddylation of cullin components of E3 cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase complexes. It acts by binding to cullin-RBX1 complexes in the cytoplasm and promoting their nuclear translocation, enhancing recruitment of E2-NEDD8 (UBE2M-NEDD8) thioester to the complex, and optimizing the orientation of proteins in the complex to allow efficient transfer of NEDD8 from the E2 to the cullin substrates.
function_by_symbol.DDB1: DDB1 encodes DNA damage-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in DNA repair and protein ubiquitination, as part of the UV-DDB complex and DCX (DDB1-CUL4-X-box) complexes, respectively. It is a core component of the UV-DDB complex (UV-damaged DNA-binding protein complex), a complex that recognizes UV-induced DNA damage and recruits proteins of the nucleotide excision repair pathway (the NER pathway) to initiate DNA repair. The UV-DDB complex preferentially binds to cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPD), 6-4 photoproducts (6-4 PP), apurinic sites and short mismatches.
function_by_symbol.DDB2: DDB2 encodes DNA damage-binding protein 2. It is a protein, which is both involved in DNA repair and protein ubiquitination, as part of the UV-DDB complex and DCX (DDB1-CUL4-X-box) complexes, respectively. It is a core component of the UV-DDB complex (UV-damaged DNA-binding protein complex), a complex that recognizes UV-induced DNA damage and recruit proteins of the nucleotide excision repair pathway (the NER pathway) to initiate DNA repair. The UV-DDB complex preferentially binds to cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPD), 6-4 photoproducts (6-4 PP), apurinic sites and short mismatches.
function_by_symbol.DDIT3: DDIT3 encodes CHOP, a C/EBP-family transcription factor activated during endoplasmic-reticulum stress. It can form heterodimers with other C/EBP proteins and inhibit their DNA-binding activity. The protein participates in adipocyte and erythroid differentiation and can promote apoptosis, connecting a cellular stress response with changes in transcription and cell fate.
function_by_symbol.DDR2: DDR2 encodes discoidin domain-containing receptor 2. It is a tyrosine kinase involved in the regulation of tissues remodeling. It is required for normal bone development. It regulates osteoblast differentiation and chondrocyte maturation via a signaling pathway that involves MAP kinases and leads to the activation of the transcription factor RUNX2.
function_by_symbol.DDX28: DDX28 encodes DEAD-box helicase 28. It contributes to facilitating the proper assembly of the mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit and its helicase activity is essential for this function. It may participate in RNA processing or transport. It has RNA and Mg(2+)-dependent ATPase activity.
function_by_symbol.DDX3X: DDX3X encodes ATP-dependent RNA helicase DDX3X. Based in part on similarity, the ATPase activity can be stimulated by various ribo-and deoxynucleic acids indicative for a relaxed substrate specificity. It binds RNA G-quadruplex (rG4s) structures, including those located in the 5'-UTR of NRAS mRNA. It positively regulates CDKN1A/WAF1/CIP1 transcription in an SP1-dependent manner, hence inhibits cell growth.
function_by_symbol.DDX41: DDX41 encodes a DEAD-box helicase-family protein implicated in RNA processing and cellular nucleic-acid sensing. Based in part on similarity, it plays pivotal roles in innate immune sensing and hematopoietic homeostasis. It modulates the homeostasis of dsDNA through its ATP-dependent DNA-unwinding activity and ATP-independent strand-annealing activity. It selectively modulates the transcription of certain immunity-associated genes by regulating their alternative splicing.
function_by_symbol.DES: DES encodes desmin. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to maintaining the structure of sarcomeres, inter-connecting the Z-disks and forming the myofibrils, linking them not only to the sarcolemmal cytoskeleton, but also to the nucleus and mitochondria, thus providing strength for the muscle fiber during activity. It is required for nuclear membrane integrity, via anchoring at the cell tip and nuclear envelope, resulting in maintenance of microtubule-derived intracellular mechanical forces. It contributes to the transcriptional regulation of the NKX2-5 gene in cardiac progenitor cells during a short period of cardiomyogenesis and in cardiac side population stem cells in the adult.
function_by_symbol.DHRS4: DHRS4 encodes dehydrogenase/reductase 4. It displays low activity toward all-trans-retinal and no activity toward 9-cis-retinal as compared to non-primate mammals. It participates in the metabolism of 3beta-hydroxysteroids, isatin and xenobiotic carbonyl compounds.
function_by_symbol.DHX15: DHX15 encodes ATP-dependent RNA helicase DHX15. Based in part on similarity, it is an RNA helicase involved in mRNA processing and antiviral innate immunity. It contributes to antiviral innate immunity by promoting both MAVS-dependent signaling and NLRP6 inflammasome. The NLRP6 inflammasome acts by promoting maturation and secretion of IL18 in the extracellular milieu.
function_by_symbol.DIS3: DIS3 encodes exosome complex exonuclease RRP44. The RNA exosome may be involved in Ig class switch recombination (CSR) and/or Ig variable region somatic hypermutation (SHM) by targeting AICDA deamination activity to transcribed dsDNA substrates. DIS3 has both 3'-5' exonuclease and endonuclease activities.
function_by_symbol.DIS3L2: DIS3L2 encodes DIS3-like exonuclease 2. It forms part of an exosome-independent RNA degradation pathway that mediates degradation of both mRNAs and miRNAs that have been polyuridylated by a terminal uridylyltransferase, such as ZCCHC11/TUT4. It mediates degradation of cytoplasmic mRNAs that have been deadenylated and subsequently uridylated at their 3'. It mediates degradation of uridylated pre-let-7 miRNAs, contributing to the maintenance of embryonic stem (ES) cells.
function_by_symbol.DKC1: DKC1 encodes H/ACA ribonucleoprotein complex subunit DKC1. This involves the isomerization of uridine such that the ribose is subsequently attached to C5, instead of the normal N1. Each rRNA can contain up to 100 pseudouridine ('psi') residues, which may serve to stabilize the conformation of rRNAs. It is required for ribosome biogenesis and telomere maintenance.
function_by_symbol.DMC1: DMC1 encodes meiotic recombination protein DMC1 homolog. It specifically required for meiotic recombination, facilitating the search and repair of DNA using the homolog rather than the sister chromatid, and can tolerate mismatches in heteroduplex DNA, unlike the higher-fidelity RAD51.
function_by_symbol.DMRT1: DMRT1 encodes doublesex- and mab-3-related transcription factor 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that plays a key role in male sex determination and differentiation by controlling testis development and male germ cell proliferation. It plays a central role in spermatogonia by inhibiting meiosis in undifferentiated spermatogonia and promoting mitosis, leading to spermatogonial development and allowing abundant and continuous production of sperm. It acts both as a transcription repressor and activator: prevents meiosis by restricting retinoic acid (RA)-dependent transcription and repressing STRA8 expression and promotes spermatogonial development by activating spermatogonial differentiation genes, such as SOHLH1.
function_by_symbol.DNAH11: DNAH11 encodes dynein axonemal heavy chain 11. Based in part on similarity, it produces force towards the minus ends of microtubules. It is a key component of dynein, a family of motor proteins essential for movement along microtubules. It is required for structural and functional integrity of cilia.
function_by_symbol.DNAH9: DNAH9 encodes dynein axonemal heavy chain 9. Based in part on similarity, it produces force towards the minus ends of microtubules. It is a key component of dynein, a family of motor proteins essential for movement along microtubules. It is required for structural and functional integrity of cilia.
function_by_symbol.DNAJB1: DNAJB1 encodes dnaJ homolog subfamily B member 1. It interacts with HSP70 and can stimulate its ATPase activity. It acts also with TTC1 as a chaperone adapter that regulates HSP70-dependent folding process by interacting with the HSP70 amino terminal region. It stimulates the association between HSC70 and HIP.
function_by_symbol.DNAJC21: DNAJC21 encodes dnaJ homolog subfamily C member 21. It may act as a co-chaperone for HSP70. May play a role in ribosomal RNA (rRNA) biogenesis, possibly in the maturation of the 60S subunit. It binds the precursor 45S rRNA.
function_by_symbol.DNMT1: DNMT1 encodes DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase 1. It is a DNA methyltransferase that methylates CpG residues. It associates with DNA replication sites in S phase maintaining the methylation pattern in the newly synthesized strand, that is essential for epigenetic inheritance. It associates with chromatin during G2 and M phases to maintain DNA methylation independently of replication.
function_by_symbol.DNMT3B: DNMT3B encodes DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase 3B. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase that mediates genome-wide de novo methylation and which is essential for the establishment of DNA methylation patterns during development. It modifies DNA at CpG sites with selectivity for residues flanking the target CpG site at positions -1 and +1, and strong preference for a guanine (G) immediately following the CpG sites. It methylates DNA in a non-cooperative processive manner, allowing the enzyme to diffuse along DNA and methylate multiple sites before dissociation.
function_by_symbol.DOCK8: DOCK8 encodes dedicator of cytokinesis protein 8. Based in part on similarity, it is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) which specifically activates small GTPase CDC42 by exchanging bound GDP for free GTP. It is required for CD4(+) T-cell migration in response to chemokine stimulation by promoting CDC42 activation at T cell leading edge membrane. It is involved in NK cell cytotoxicity by controlling polarization of microtubule-organizing center (MTOC), and possibly regulating CCDC88B-mediated lytic granule transport to MTOC during cell killing.
function_by_symbol.DTD2: DTD2 encodes D-aminoacyl-tRNA deacylase 2. Based in part on similarity, it deacylates mischarged D-aminoacyl-tRNAs. It also deacylates mischarged glycyl-tRNA(Ala), protecting cells against glycine mischarging by AlaRS. It probably acts by rejecting L-amino acids from its binding site rather than specific recognition of D-amino acids.
function_by_symbol.DTX1: DTX1 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase DTX1. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of MEKK1, thereby modulating signaling pathways involved in cell fate determination. It regulates the Notch signaling pathway, acting predominantly as a positive regulator but functioning as a context-dependent negative regulator in specific developmental or cellular settings. It mediates the antineural activity of Notch signaling, likely by inhibiting transcriptional activation mediated by MATCH1.
function_by_symbol.DUSP22: DUSP22 encodes dual specificity protein phosphatase 22. Based in part on similarity, it activates the JNK signaling pathway. It inhibits T-cell receptor signaling and T-cell mediated immune responses, acting, at least in part, by inducing degradation of E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR2. It dephosphorylates and thereby induces 'Lys-48'-linked ubiquitination of UBR2, leading to proteasomal degradation of UBR2.
function_by_symbol.DUX4: DUX4 encodes double homeobox protein 4. It binds to double-stranded DNA elements with the consensus sequence 5'-TAATCTAATCA-3'. It binds to chromatin containing histone H3 acetylated at 'Lys-27' (H3K27ac) and promotes deacetylation of H3K27ac. It participates in transcriptional regulation of numerous genes, primarily as transcriptional activator, but also mediates repression of a set of target genes.
function_by_symbol.E2F3: E2F3 encodes transcription factor E2F3. Based in part on similarity, the DRTF1/E2F complex functions in the control of cell-cycle progression from G1 to S phase. E2F3 binds specifically to RB1 in a cell-cycle dependent manner. It inhibits adipogenesis, probably through the repression of CEBPA binding to its target gene promoters.
function_by_symbol.EBF2: EBF2 encodes EBF transcription factor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that, in osteoblasts, activates the decoy receptor for RANKL, TNFRSF11B, which in turn regulates osteoclast differentiation. It acts in synergy with the Wnt-responsive LEF1/CTNNB1 pathway. It recognizes variations of the palindromic sequence 5'-ATTCCCNNGGGAATT-3'.
function_by_symbol.EED: EED encodes polycomb protein EED. It forms part of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, which methylates 'Lys-9' and 'Lys-27' of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It also recognizes 'Lys-26' trimethylated histone H1 with the effect of inhibiting PRC2 complex methyltransferase activity on nucleosomal histone H3 'Lys-27', whereas H3 'Lys-27' recognition has the opposite effect, enabling the propagation of this repressive mark. The PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex may also serve as a recruiting platform for DNA methyltransferases, thereby linking two epigenetic repression systems.
function_by_symbol.EGLN1: EGLN1 encodes egl nine homolog 1. It hydroxylates a specific proline found in each of the oxygen-dependent degradation (ODD) domains (N-terminal, NODD, and C-terminal, CODD) of HIF1A. It has a preference for the CODD site for both HIF1A and HIF1B. Hydroxylated HIFs are then targeted for proteasomal degradation via the von Hippel-Lindau ubiquitination complex.
function_by_symbol.EGR1: EGR1 encodes early growth response protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it recognizes and binds to the DNA sequence 5'-GCG(T/G)GGGCG-3'(EGR-site) in the promoter region of target genes. It binds double-stranded target DNA, irrespective of the cytosine methylation status. It regulates the transcription of numerous target genes, and thereby plays an important role in regulating the response to growth factors, DNA damage, and ischemia.
function_by_symbol.EGR2: EGR2 encodes E3 SUMO-protein ligase EGR2. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to hindbrain segmentation by regulating the expression of a subset of homeobox containing genes and in Schwann cell myelination by regulating the expression of genes involved in the formation and maintenance of myelin. It binds to two EGR2-consensus sites EGR2A (5'-CTGTAGGAG-3') and EGR2B (5'-ATGTAGGTG-3') in the HOXB3 enhancer and promotes HOXB3 transcriptional activation. It binds to specific DNA sites located in the promoter region of HOXA4, HOXB2 and ERBB2.
function_by_symbol.EHMT1: EHMT1 encodes euchromatic histone lysine methyltransferase 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that specifically mono-, di- and trimethylates 'Lys-9' of histone H3 (H3K9me1, H3K9me2 and H3K9me3, respectively) in euchromatin. H3K9me represents a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression by recruiting HP1 proteins to methylated histones. It also weakly methylates 'Lys-27' of histone H3 (H3K27me).
function_by_symbol.EIF1AX: EIF1AX encodes eukaryotic translation initiation factor 1A, X-chromosomal. It forms part of the 43S pre-initiation complex (43S PIC), which binds to the mRNA cap-proximal region, scans mRNA 5'-untranslated region, and locates the initiation codon. This protein enhances formation of the cap-proximal complex. It is released after 80S initiation complex formation, just after GTP hydrolysis by EIF5B, and before release of EIF5B.
function_by_symbol.EIF4E: EIF4E encodes eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E. Based in part on similarity, it acts in the cytoplasm to initiate and regulate protein synthesis and is required in the nucleus for export of a subset of mRNAs from the nucleus to the cytoplasm which promotes processes such as RNA capping, processing and splicing. It forms part of the protein complex eIF4F, which is involved in the recognition of the mRNA cap, ATP-dependent unwinding of 5'-terminal secondary structure and recruitment of mRNA to the ribosome. This protein recognizes and binds the 7-methylguanosine (m7G)-containing mRNA cap during an early step in the initiation of protein synthesis and facilitates ribosome binding by inducing the unwinding of the mRNAs secondary structures.
function_by_symbol.ELANE: ELANE encodes neutrophil elastase. It is a serine protease that modifies the functions of natural killer cells, monocytes and granulocytes. It shows microbicidal activity in neutrophils by mediating cleavage and degradation of bacterial proteins. NETs are mainly composed of DNA fibers and are released by neutrophils to trap pathogens during inflammation.
function_by_symbol.ELF3: ELF3 encodes ETS-related transcription factor Elf-3. Based in part on similarity, it acts synergistically with POU2F3 to transactivate the SPRR2A promoter and with RUNX1 to transactivate the ANGPT1 promoter. It also transactivates collagenase, CCL20, CLND7, FLG, KRT8, NOS2, PTGS2, SPRR2B, TGFBR2 and TGM3 promoters. It participates in mediating vascular inflammation.
function_by_symbol.ELL: ELL encodes RNA polymerase II elongation factor ELL. It specifically required for stimulating the elongation step of RNA polymerase II- and III-dependent snRNA gene transcription. ELL also plays an early role before its assembly into in the SEC complex by stabilizing RNA polymerase II recruitment/initiation and entry into the pause site.
function_by_symbol.ELP1: ELP1 encodes a scaffold component of the Elongator complex. Its molecular role concerns organization of a multiprotein assembly involved in RNA modification and regulation of gene expression. A scaffold contribution is distinct from assigning the catalytic activities of every Elongator subunit directly to ELP1.
function_by_symbol.EMILIN2: EMILIN2 encodes EMILIN-2. May be responsible for anchoring smooth muscle cells to elastic fibers, and may be involved not only in the formation of the elastic fiber, but also in the processes that regulate vessel assembly.
function_by_symbol.EML4: EML4 encodes echinoderm microtubule-associated protein-like 4. It is essential for the formation and stability of microtubules (MTs). It is required for the organization of the mitotic spindle and for the proper attachment of kinetochores to MTs. It promotes the recruitment of NUDC to the mitotic spindle for mitotic progression.
function_by_symbol.EMSY: EMSY encodes BRCA2-interacting transcriptional repressor EMSY. It is a regulator which is able to repress transcription, possibly via its interaction with a multiprotein chromatin remodeling complex that modifies the chromatin. It mediates ligand-dependent transcriptional activation by nuclear hormone receptors.
function_by_symbol.ENG: ENG encodes endoglin. Based in part on similarity, it is required for normal structure and integrity of adult vasculature. It regulates the migration of vascular endothelial cells.
function_by_symbol.EP300: EP300 encodes the p300 transcriptional coactivator and acetyltransferase, which regulates transcription through histone acetylation and interactions with transcription factors. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a histone acetyltransferase and regulates transcription via chromatin remodeling. It acetylates all four core histones in nucleosomes. It is a histone acetylation gives an epigenetic tag for transcriptional activation.
function_by_symbol.EP400: EP400 encodes E1A-binding protein p400. It forms part of the NuA4 histone acetyltransferase complex which is involved in transcriptional activation of select genes principally by acetylation of nucleosomal histones H4 and H2A. This modification may both alter nucleosome - DNA interactions and promote interaction of the modified histones with other proteins which positively regulate transcription. It may be required for transcriptional activation of E2F1 and MYC target genes during cellular proliferation.
function_by_symbol.EPAS1: EPAS1 encodes endothelial PAS domain-containing protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor involved in the induction of oxygen regulated genes. It regulates the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression and seems to be implicated in the development of blood vessels and the tubular system of lung. May also play a role in the formation of the endothelium that gives rise to the blood brain barrier.
function_by_symbol.EPC1: EPC1 encodes enhancer of polycomb homolog 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the NuA4 histone acetyltransferase (HAT) complex, a multiprotein complex involved in transcriptional activation of select genes principally by acetylation of nucleosomal histones H4 and H2A. The NuA4 complex plays a direct role in repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) by promoting homologous recombination (HR). The NuA4 complex is also required for spermatid development by promoting acetylation of histones: histone acetylation is required for histone replacement during the transition from round to elongating spermatids.
function_by_symbol.EPHA3: EPHA3 encodes ephrin type-A receptor 3. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase which binds promiscuously membrane-bound ephrin family ligands residing on adjacent cells, leading to contact-dependent bidirectional signaling into neighboring cells. The signaling pathway downstream of the receptor is referred to as forward signaling while the signaling pathway downstream of the ephrin ligand is referred to as reverse signaling. It also activated by EFNA1, inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition of cardiac cells and playing a role in heart development.
function_by_symbol.EPHA5: EPHA5 encodes ephrin type-A receptor 5. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase which binds promiscuously GPI-anchored ephrin-A family ligands residing on adjacent cells, leading to contact-dependent bidirectional signaling into neighboring cells. The signaling pathway downstream of the receptor is referred to as forward signaling while the signaling pathway downstream of the ephrin ligand is referred to as reverse signaling. It acts as an axon guidance molecule during development and may be involved in the development of the retinotectal, entorhino-hippocampal and hippocamposeptal pathways.
function_by_symbol.EPHA7: EPHA7 encodes ephrin type-A receptor 7. It is a receptor tyrosine kinase which binds promiscuously GPI-anchored ephrin-A family ligands residing on adjacent cells, leading to contact-dependent bidirectional signaling into neighboring cells. The signaling pathway downstream of the receptor is referred to as forward signaling while the signaling pathway downstream of the ephrin ligand is referred to as reverse signaling.
function_by_symbol.EPHB1: EPHB1 encodes ephrin type-B receptor 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase which binds promiscuously transmembrane ephrin-B family ligands residing on adjacent cells, leading to contact-dependent bidirectional signaling into neighboring cells. The signaling pathway downstream of the receptor is referred to as forward signaling while the signaling pathway downstream of the ephrin ligand is referred to as reverse signaling. This probably requires repulsive interaction with EFNB2.
function_by_symbol.ERBB3: ERBB3 encodes receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-3. Based in part on similarity, it is a tyrosine kinase receptor that, despite substitutions of key catalytic residues in the kinase domain, retains residual catalytic activity enabling autophosphorylation. It functions primarily as a heterodimer, preferentially partnering with ERBB2/HER2, which phosphorylates ERBB3 on specific tyrosine residues and provides the kinase activity required for downstream signaling. It binds neuregulins NRG1 and NRG2 through its extracellular domain, which induces conformational change from a tethered autoinhibited state to an extended conformation competent for dimerization.
function_by_symbol.ERBB4: ERBB4 encodes receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-4. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that plays an essential role as cell surface receptor for neuregulins and EGF family members and regulates development of the heart, the central nervous system and the mammary gland, gene transcription, cell proliferation, differentiation, migration and apoptosis. It is required for normal cardiac muscle differentiation during embryonic development, and for postnatal cardiomyocyte proliferation. It is required for normal development of the embryonic central nervous system, especially for normal neural crest cell migration and normal axon guidance.
function_by_symbol.ERCC3: ERCC3 encodes general transcription and DNA repair factor IIH helicase/translocase subunit XPB. It binds dsDNA rather than ssDNA, unzipping it in a translocase rather than classical helicase activity. It forms part of the general transcription and DNA repair factor IIH (TFIIH) core complex. The ATP-dependent helicase activity of XPB/ERCC3 is required for promoter opening and promoter escape.
function_by_symbol.ERCC4: ERCC4 encodes DNA repair endonuclease XPF. It is the catalytic component of a structure-specific DNA repair endonuclease responsible for the 5-prime incision during DNA repair, and which is essential for nucleotide excision repair (NER) and interstrand cross-link (ICL) repair.
function_by_symbol.ERCC5: ERCC5 encodes DNA excision repair protein ERCC-5. It is a single-stranded structure-specific DNA endonuclease involved in DNA excision repair. It makes the 3'incision in DNA nucleotide excision repair (NER). It binds and bends DNA repair bubble substrate and breaks base stacking at the single-strand/double-strand DNA junction of the DNA bubble.
function_by_symbol.ERCC6: ERCC6 encodes CSB, a DNA-binding ATPase important in transcription-coupled excision repair. It interacts with transcription and repair proteins and may help assemble repair machinery at damaged DNA. Its role links repair with the transcriptional apparatus, rather than treating all damaged genomic regions as equivalent repair substrates.
function_by_symbol.ERG: ERG encodes an ETS-family transcriptional regulator. It may influence gene expression through recruitment of the SETDB1 histone methyltransferase and consequent changes in local chromatin organization. This connects sequence-specific transcriptional regulation with recruitment of chromatin-modifying machinery.
function_by_symbol.ERRFI1: ERRFI1 encodes ERBB receptor feedback inhibitor 1. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a negative regulator for several EGFR family members, including ERBB2, ERBB3 and ERBB4. It inhibits EGFR catalytic activity by interfering with its dimerization. It inhibits autophosphorylation of EGFR, ERBB2 and ERBB4.
function_by_symbol.ESR1: ESR1 encodes estrogen receptor. Based in part on similarity, the steroid hormones and their receptors are involved in the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression and affect cellular proliferation and differentiation in target tissues. It decreases NF-kappa-B DNA-binding activity and inhibits NF-kappa-B-mediated transcription from the IL6 promoter and displace RELA/p65 and associated coregulators from the promoter. It can activate the transcriptional activity of TFF1.
function_by_symbol.ETV4: ETV4 encodes ETS translocation variant 4. Based in part on similarity, it regulates the positioning of motor neurons within the lateral medial column of the spinal cord and controls the terminal arborization of specific motor neuron axons within their target muscles. It is required for the expression of CDH8 and SEMA3E in ETV4-expressing motor neurons and for the exclusion of CDH7 expression from these neurons. May play a role in keratinocyte differentiation.
function_by_symbol.EVPL: EVPL encodes envoplakin. It forms part of the cornified envelope of keratinocytes. It may link the cornified envelope to desmosomes and intermediate filaments.
function_by_symbol.EWSR1: EWSR1 encodes RNA-binding protein EWS. It binds to ssRNA containing the consensus sequence 5'-AGGUAA-3'. EWS-fusion-proteins (EFPS) may play a role in the tumorigenic process. They may disturb gene expression by mimicking, or interfering with the normal function of CTD-POLII within the transcription initiation complex.
function_by_symbol.EXO1: EXO1 encodes exonuclease 1. It functions in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) to excise mismatch-containing DNA tracts directed by strand breaks located either 5' or 3' to the mismatch. It also exhibits endonuclease activity against 5'-overhanging flap structures similar to those generated by displacement synthesis when DNA polymerase encounters the 5'-end of a downstream Okazaki fragment.
function_by_symbol.EXOSC6: EXOSC6 encodes exosome complex component MTR3. The RNA exosome may be involved in Ig class switch recombination (CSR) and/or Ig variable region somatic hypermutation (SHM) by targeting AICDA deamination activity to transcribed dsDNA substrates. The catalytic inactive RNA exosome core complex of 9 subunits (Exo-9) is proposed to play a pivotal role in the binding and presentation of RNA for ribonucleolysis, and to serve as a scaffold for the association with catalytic subunits and accessory proteins or complexes.
function_by_symbol.EYA4: EYA4 encodes EYA transcriptional coactivator and phosphatase 4. Based in part on similarity, it is a tyrosine phosphatase that specifically dephosphorylates 'Tyr-142' of histone H2AX (H2AXY142ph). 'Tyr-142' phosphorylation of histone H2AX plays a central role in DNA repair and acts as a mark that distinguishes between apoptotic and repair responses to genotoxic stress. It promotes efficient DNA repair by dephosphorylating H2AX, promoting the recruitment of DNA repair complexes containing MDC1.
function_by_symbol.EZH1: EZH1 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase EZH1. It is a catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH1 complex, which methylates 'Lys-27' of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It is required for embryonic stem cell derivation and self-renewal, suggesting that it is involved in safeguarding embryonic stem cell identity. Compared to EZH2-containing complexes, it is less abundant in embryonic stem cells, has weak methyltransferase activity and plays a less critical role in forming H3K27me3, which is required for embryonic stem cell identity and proper differentiation.
function_by_symbol.EZH2: EZH2 encodes the catalytic methyltransferase component of polycomb repressive complex 2, which methylates histone H3 lysine 27 to regulate transcriptional repression. Based in part on similarity, it is a catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, a Polycomb group (PcG) complex that methylates 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27me) of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It displays a preference for substrates with less methylation, loses activity when progressively more methyl groups are incorporated into H3K27, H3K27me0 > H3K27me1 > H3K27me2. Compared to EZH1-containing complexes, it is more abundant in embryonic stem cells and plays a major role in forming H3K27me3, which is required for embryonic stem cell identity and proper differentiation.
function_by_symbol.EZHIP: EZHIP encodes EZH inhibitory protein. Based in part on similarity, it inhibits PRC2/EED-EZH1 and PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex function by inhibiting EZH1/EZH2 methyltransferase activity, thereby causing down-regulation of histone H3 trimethylation on 'Lys-27' (H3K27me3). It probably inhibits methyltransferase activity by limiting the stimulatory effect of cofactors such as AEBP2 and JARID2. It inhibits H3K27me3 deposition during spermatogenesis and oogenesis.
function_by_symbol.FAAP100: FAAP100 encodes Fanconi anemia core complex-associated protein 100. It contributes to Fanconi anemia-associated DNA damage response network. It regulates FANCD2 monoubiquitination and the stability of the FA core complex. It induces chromosomal instability as well as hypersensitivity to DNA cross-linking agents, when repressed.
function_by_symbol.FAAP20: FAAP20 encodes Fanconi anemia core complex-associated protein 20. It forms part of the Fanconi anemia (FA) complex required to recruit the FA complex to DNA interstrand cross-links (ICLs) and promote ICLs repair. It promotes translesion synthesis via interaction with REV1.
function_by_symbol.FAAP24: FAAP24 encodes Fanconi anemia core complex-associated protein 24. It contributes to DNA repair through recruitment of the FA core complex to damaged DNA. It regulates FANCD2 monoubiquitination upon DNA damage. It induces chromosomal instability as well as hypersensitivity to DNA cross-linking agents, when repressed.
function_by_symbol.FAN1: FAN1 encodes Fanconi-associated nuclease 1. It specifically involved in repair of ICL-induced DNA breaks by being required for efficient homologous recombination, probably in the resolution of homologous recombination intermediates. It functions as a 5'-3' exonuclease that anchors at a cut end of DNA and cleaves DNA successively at every third nucleotide, allowing to excise an ICL from one strand through flanking incisions. It probably keeps excising with 3'-flap annealing until it reaches and unhooks the ICL.
function_by_symbol.FANCA: FANCA encodes Fanconi anemia group A protein. It is a DNA repair protein that may operate in a postreplication repair or a cell cycle checkpoint function. It may participate in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability.
function_by_symbol.FANCC: FANCC encodes Fanconi anemia group C protein. It is a DNA repair protein that may operate in a postreplication repair or a cell cycle checkpoint function. It may be implicated in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability.
function_by_symbol.FANCD2: FANCD2 encodes Fanconi anemia group D2 protein. Based in part on similarity, it is required for maintenance of chromosomal stability. It promotes accurate and efficient pairing of homologs during meiosis. It participates in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks, both by homologous recombination and single-strand annealing.
function_by_symbol.FANCE: FANCE encodes Fanconi anemia group E protein. It is required for the nuclear accumulation of FANCC and provides a critical bridge between the FA complex and FANCD2.
function_by_symbol.FANCF: FANCF encodes Fanconi anemia group F protein. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA repair protein that may operate in a postreplication repair or a cell cycle checkpoint function. It may be implicated in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability.
function_by_symbol.FANCG: FANCG encodes Fanconi anemia group G protein. It is a DNA repair protein that may operate in a postreplication repair or a cell cycle checkpoint function. It may be implicated in interstrand DNA cross-link repair and in the maintenance of normal chromosome stability.
function_by_symbol.FANCI: FANCI encodes Fanconi anemia group I protein. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination and in the repair of interstrand DNA cross-links (ICLs) by promoting FANCD2 monoubiquitination by FANCL and participating in recruitment to DNA repair sites. It participates in S phase and G2 phase checkpoint activation upon DNA damage.
function_by_symbol.FANCL: FANCL encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase FANCL. It is an ubiquitin ligase protein that mediates monoubiquitination of FANCD2 in the presence of UBE2T, a key step in the DNA damage pathway. It also mediates monoubiquitination of FANCI. It may stimulate the ubiquitin release from UBE2W.
function_by_symbol.FANCM: FANCM encodes Fanconi anemia group M protein. It is a DNA-dependent ATPase component of the Fanconi anemia (FA) core complex. Its ATP-dependent DNA branch migration activity can process branched DNA structures such as a movable replication fork. This activity is strongly stimulated in the presence of CENPS and CENPX.
function_by_symbol.FAS: FAS encodes tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 6. The adapter molecule FADD recruits caspase CASP8 to the activated receptor. The resulting death-inducing signaling complex (DISC) performs CASP8 proteolytic activation which initiates the subsequent cascade of caspases (aspartate-specific cysteine proteases) mediating apoptosis. FAS-mediated apoptosis may have a role in the induction of peripheral tolerance, in the antigen-stimulated suicide of mature T-cells, or both.
function_by_symbol.FBXO11: FBXO11 encodes f-box only protein 11. It is a substrate recognition component of a SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins, such as DTL/CDT2, BCL6, SNAI1 and PRDM1/BLIMP1. The SCF(FBXO11) complex mediates ubiquitination and degradation of BCL6, thereby playing a role in the germinal center B-cells terminal differentiation toward memory B-cells and plasma cells. The SCF(FBXO11) complex also mediates ubiquitination and degradation of DTL, an important step for the regulation of TGF-beta signaling, cell migration and the timing of the cell-cycle progression and exit.
function_by_symbol.FBXW7: FBXW7 encodes f-box/WD repeat-containing protein 7. It is a substrate recognition component of a SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins. It recognizes and binds phosphorylated sites/phosphodegrons within target proteins and thereafter brings them to the SCF complex for ubiquitination. It functions as a negative regulator of JNK signaling by binding to phosphorylated JUN and promoting its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation.
function_by_symbol.FGF1: FGF1 encodes fibroblast growth factor 1. It contributes to the regulation of cell survival, cell division, angiogenesis, cell differentiation and cell migration. It functions as a ligand for FGFR1 and integrins. It binds to FGFR1 in the presence of heparin leading to FGFR1 dimerization and activation via sequential autophosphorylation on tyrosine residues which act as docking sites for interacting proteins, leading to the activation of several signaling cascades.
function_by_symbol.FGF2: FGF2 encodes fibroblast growth factor 2. It functions as a ligand for FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3 and FGFR4. It also acts as an integrin ligand which is required for FGF2 signaling. It contributes to the regulation of cell survival, cell division, cell differentiation and cell migration.
function_by_symbol.FGF4: FGF4 encodes fibroblast growth factor 4. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, and cell differentiation. It is required for normal limb and cardiac valve development during embryogenesis. May play a role in embryonic molar tooth bud development via inducing the expression of MSX1, MSX2 and MSX1-mediated expression of SDC1 in dental mesenchyme cells.
function_by_symbol.FGF5: FGF5 encodes fibroblast growth factor 5. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the regulation of cell proliferation and cell differentiation. It is required for normal regulation of the hair growth cycle. It acts as an inhibitor of hair elongation by promoting progression from anagen, the growth phase of the hair follicle, into catagen the apoptosis-induced regression phase.
function_by_symbol.FGF8: FGF8 encodes fibroblast growth factor 8. It contributes to the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, cell differentiation and cell migration. It is required for normal brain, eye, ear and limb development during embryogenesis. It is required for normal development of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neuronal system.
function_by_symbol.FGFR2: FGFR2 encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor 2. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation, migration and apoptosis, and in the regulation of embryonic development. It is required for normal embryonic patterning, trophoblast function, limb bud development, lung morphogenesis, osteogenesis and skin development. It contributes to the regulation of osteoblast differentiation, proliferation and apoptosis, and is required for normal skeleton development.
function_by_symbol.FGFR3: FGFR3 encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor 3. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation and apoptosis. It contributes to the regulation of chondrocyte differentiation, proliferation and apoptosis, and is required for normal skeleton development. It regulates both osteogenesis and postnatal bone mineralization by osteoblasts.
function_by_symbol.FGFR4: FGFR4 encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor 4. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays a role in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation and migration, and in regulation of lipid metabolism, bile acid biosynthesis, glucose uptake, vitamin D metabolism and phosphate homeostasis. It is required for normal down-regulation of the expression of CYP7A1, the rate-limiting enzyme in bile acid synthesis, in response to FGF19. It promotes SRC-dependent phosphorylation of the matrix protease MMP14 and its lysosomal degradation.
function_by_symbol.FHL2: FHL2 encodes four and a half LIM domains protein 2. It may function as a molecular transmitter linking various signaling pathways to transcriptional regulation. It negatively regulates the transcriptional repressor E4F1 and may function in cell growth. It inhibits the transcriptional activity of FOXO1 and its apoptotic function by enhancing the interaction of FOXO1 with SIRT1 and FOXO1 deacetylation.
function_by_symbol.FIP1L1: FIP1L1 encodes pre-mRNA 3'-end-processing factor FIP1. It forms part of the cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor (CPSF) complex that plays a key role in pre-mRNA 3'-end formation, recognizing the AAUAAA signal sequence and interacting with poly(A) polymerase and other factors to bring about cleavage and poly(A) addition. It binds to U-rich RNA sequence elements surrounding the poly(A) site. It may act to tether poly(A) polymerase to the CPSF complex.
function_by_symbol.FLCN: FLCN encodes folliculin. Based in part on similarity, it is a GTPase-activating protein that plays a key role in the cellular response to amino acid availability through regulation of the non-canonical mTORC1 signaling cascade controlling the MiT/TFE factors TFEB and TFE3. It activates mTORC1 by acting as a GTPase-activating protein: specifically stimulates GTP hydrolysis by RagC/RRAGC or RagD/RRAGD, promoting the conversion to the GDP-bound state of RagC/RRAGC or RagD/RRAGD, and thereby activating the kinase activity of mTORC1. The GTPase-activating activity is inhibited during starvation and activated in presence of nutrients.
function_by_symbol.FLT1: FLT1 encodes vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a positive regulator of postnatal retinal hyaloid vessel regression. May play an essential role as a negative regulator of embryonic angiogenesis by inhibiting excessive proliferation of endothelial cells. It can promote endothelial cell proliferation, survival and angiogenesis in adulthood.
function_by_symbol.FLT3: FLT3 encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed in hematopoietic progenitors. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for the cytokine FLT3LG and regulates differentiation, proliferation and survival of hematopoietic progenitor cells and of dendritic cells. It promotes phosphorylation of SHC1 and AKT1, and activation of the downstream effector MTOR. It promotes activation of RAS signaling and phosphorylation of downstream kinases, including MAPK1/ERK2 and/or MAPK3/ERK1.
function_by_symbol.FLT4: FLT4 encodes vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 3. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for VEGFC and VEGFD, and plays an essential role in adult lymphangiogenesis and in the development of the vascular network and the cardiovascular system during embryonic development. It promotes proliferation, survival and migration of endothelial cells, and regulates angiogenic sprouting. It modulates KDR signaling by forming heterodimers.
function_by_symbol.FN1: FN1 encodes fibronectin. Based in part on similarity, fibronectins are involved in cell adhesion, cell motility, opsonization, wound healing, and maintenance of cell shape. It participates in osteoblast compaction through the fibronectin fibrillogenesis cell-mediated matrix assembly process, essential for osteoblast mineralization.
function_by_symbol.FOLR1: FOLR1 encodes folate receptor alpha. Based in part on similarity, it binds to folate and reduced folic acid derivatives and mediates delivery of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate and folate analogs into the interior of cells. It has high affinity for folate and folic acid analogs at neutral pH. It is required for normal embryonic development and normal cell proliferation.
function_by_symbol.FOS: FOS encodes protein c-Fos. It is a nuclear phosphoprotein which forms a tight but non-covalently linked complex with the JUN/AP-1 transcription factor. On TGF-beta activation, forms a multimeric SMAD3/SMAD4/JUN/FOS complex at the AP1/SMAD-binding site to regulate TGF-beta-mediated signaling. It has a critical function in regulating the development of cells destined to form and maintain the skeleton.
function_by_symbol.FOSB: FOSB encodes protein FosB. Based in part on similarity, it participates in the display of nurturing behavior towards newborns. May play a role in neurogenesis in the hippocampus and in learning and memory-related tasks by regulating the expression of various genes involved in neurogenesis, depression and epilepsy. It may participate in the regulation of neurogenesis in the hippocampus.
function_by_symbol.FOSL1: FOSL1 encodes a leucine-zipper transcriptional regulator in the FOS family. FOS-family proteins pair with JUN-family partners to form AP-1 transcription-factor complexes. This partnership links FOSL1 to regulation of proliferation, differentiation, and cellular transformation through changes in target-gene expression rather than a direct enzymatic reaction on DNA.
function_by_symbol.FOXA1: FOXA1 encodes hepatocyte nuclear factor 3-alpha. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that is involved in embryonic development, establishment of tissue-specific gene expression and regulation of gene expression in differentiated tissues. It is thought to act as a 'pioneer' factor opening the compacted chromatin for other proteins through interactions with nucleosomal core histones and thereby replacing linker histones at target enhancer and/or promoter sites. Proposed to play a role in translating the epigenetic signatures into cell type-specific enhancer-driven transcriptional programs.
function_by_symbol.FOXI1: FOXI1 encodes forkhead box protein I1. Based in part on similarity, it is required for the expression of SLC26A4/PDS, JAG1 and COCH in a subset of epithelial cells and the development of the endolymphatic system in the inner ear. It is also required for the expression of SLC4A1/AE1, SLC4A9/AE4, ATP6V1B1 and the differentiation of intercalated cells in the epithelium of distal renal tubules.
function_by_symbol.FOXO1: FOXO1 encodes forkhead box protein O1. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that is the main target of insulin signaling and regulates metabolic homeostasis in response to oxidative stress. It orchestrates the endocrine function of the skeleton in regulating glucose metabolism. It also acts as a key regulator of chondrogenic commitment of skeletal progenitor cells in response to lipid availability: when lipids levels are low, translocates to the nucleus and promotes expression of SOX9, which induces chondrogenic commitment and suppresses fatty acid oxidation.
function_by_symbol.FOXO3: FOXO3 encodes forkhead box protein O3. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a positive regulator of autophagy in skeletal muscle: in starved cells, enters the nucleus following dephosphorylation and binds the promoters of autophagy genes, such as GABARAP1L, MAP1LC3B and ATG12, thereby activating their expression, resulting in proteolysis of skeletal muscle proteins. It triggers apoptosis in the absence of survival factors, including neuronal cell death upon oxidative stress. It participates in post-transcriptional regulation of MYC: following phosphorylation by MAPKAPK5, promotes induction of miR-34b and miR-34c expression, 2 post-transcriptional regulators of MYC that bind to the 3'UTR of MYC transcript and prevent its translation.
function_by_symbol.FRMD4B: FRMD4B encodes FERM domain containing 4B. Based in part on similarity, it may function as a scaffolding protein that regulates epithelial cell polarity by connecting ARF6 activation with the PAR3 complex. It plays a redundant role with FRMD4A in epithelial polarization.
function_by_symbol.FRS2: FRS2 encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor substrate 2. It is an adapter protein that links activated FGR and NGF receptors to downstream signaling pathways. It contributes to the activation of MAP kinases and in the phosphorylation of PIK3R1, the regulatory subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase, in response to ligand-mediated activation of FGFR1. It modulates signaling via SHC1 by competing for a common binding site on NTRK1.
function_by_symbol.FURIN: FURIN encodes furin. Based in part on similarity, it mediates processing of TGFB1, an essential step in TGF-beta-1 activation. It converts through proteolytic cleavage the non-functional Brain natriuretic factor prohormone into its active hormone BNP(1-32).
function_by_symbol.FUS: FUS encodes RNA-binding protein FUS. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA/RNA-binding protein that plays a role in various cellular processes such as transcription regulation, RNA splicing, RNA transport, DNA repair and damage response. It binds to ssRNA containing the consensus sequence 5'-AGGUAA-3'. It binds to nascent pre-mRNAs and acts as a molecular mediator between RNA polymerase II and U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein thereby coupling transcription and splicing.
function_by_symbol.FYN: FYN encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Fyn. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays a role in many biological processes including regulation of cell growth and survival, cell adhesion, integrin-mediated signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell motility, immune response and axon guidance. Inactive FYN is phosphorylated on its C-terminal tail within the catalytic domain. It participates in the regulation of cell adhesion and motility through phosphorylation of CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) and CTNND1 (delta-catenin).
function_by_symbol.FZD10: FZD10 encodes frizzled class receptor 10. Based in part on similarity, it functions in the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. The canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway leads to the activation of disheveled proteins, inhibition of GSK-3 kinase, nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin and activation of Wnt target genes.
function_by_symbol.GAB1: GAB1 encodes GRB2-associated-binding protein 1. It is an adapter protein that plays a role in intracellular signaling cascades triggered by activated receptor-type kinases. It contributes to FGFR1 signaling. It is probably involved in signaling by the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and the insulin receptor (INSR).
function_by_symbol.GAB2: GAB2 encodes GRB2-associated-binding protein 2. It is an adapter protein which acts downstream of several membrane receptors including cytokine, antigen, hormone, cell matrix and growth factor receptors to regulate multiple signaling pathways. It regulates osteoclast differentiation mediating the TNFRSF11A/RANK signaling. It is also involved in the regulation of cell proliferation and hematopoiesis.
function_by_symbol.GALNT12: GALNT12 encodes polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 12. It catalyzes the initial reaction in O-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis, the transfer of an N-acetyl-D-galactosamine residue to a serine or threonine residue on the protein receptor. It has activity toward non-glycosylated peptides such as Muc5AC, Muc1a and EA2, and no detectable activity with Muc2 and Muc7. It displays enzymatic activity toward the Gal-NAc-Muc5AC glycopeptide, but no detectable activity to mono-GalNAc-glycosylated Muc1a, Muc2, Muc7 and EA2.
function_by_symbol.GATA2: GATA2 encodes a zinc-finger transcription factor important for hematopoietic stem and progenitor-cell maintenance and development of several blood-cell lineages. It binds to the consensus sequence 5'-AGATAG-3'.
function_by_symbol.GATA3: GATA3 encodes trans-acting T-cell-specific transcription factor GATA-3. Based in part on similarity, it binds to the consensus sequence 5'-AGATAG-3'. It is required for the T-helper 2 (Th2) differentiation process following immune and inflammatory responses.
function_by_symbol.GATA4: GATA4 encodes transcription factor GATA-4. Based in part on similarity, it participates in bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)-mediated induction of cardiac-specific gene expression. It binds to BMP response element (BMPRE) DNA sequences within cardiac activating regions.
function_by_symbol.GBA1: GBA1 encodes lysosomal acid glucosylceramidase. It plays a central role in the degradation of complex lipids and the turnover of cellular membranes. It catalyzes the glucosylation of cholesterol, through a transglucosylation reaction where glucose is transferred from GlcCer to cholesterol. It can also hydrolyze cholesteryl 3-beta-D-glucoside producing glucose and cholesterol.
function_by_symbol.GEN1: GEN1 encodes flap endonuclease GEN homolog 1. It cleaves HJs by a nick and counter-nick mechanism involving dual coordinated incisions that lead to the formation of ligatable nicked duplex products. Cleavage of the first strand is rate limiting, while second strand cleavage is rapid. It exhibits a weak sequence preference for incision between two G residues that reside in a T-rich region of DNA.
function_by_symbol.GFI1: GFI1 encodes zinc finger protein Gfi-1. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription repressor essential for hematopoiesis. It functions in a cell-context and development-specific manner. It forms part of several complexes, including the EHMT2-GFI1-HDAC1, AJUBA-GFI1-HDAC1 and RCOR-GFI-KDM1A-HDAC complexes, that suppress, via histone deacetylase (HDAC) recruitment, a number of genes implicated in multilineage blood cell development.
function_by_symbol.GFI1B: GFI1B encodes zinc finger protein Gfi-1b. It forms part of a RCOR-GFI-KDM1A-HDAC complex that suppresses, via histone deacetylase (HDAC) recruitment, a number of genes implicated in multilineage blood cell development and controls hematopoietic differentiation. It inhibits down-regulation of MYC and MYB as well as the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor CDKN1A/P21WAF1 in IL6-treated myelomonocytic cells. It suppresses GATA1-mediated stimulation of GFI1B promoter through protein interaction.
function_by_symbol.GID4: GID4 encodes a substrate-recognition component of the CTLH ubiquitin-ligase complex. It recognizes proteins with particular amino-terminal proline-containing degradation signals, helping select substrates for ubiquitination and subsequent turnover. Substrate recognition is its role within the assembly, rather than the entire catalytic activity of the ligase complex being assigned to GID4 alone.
function_by_symbol.GLI1: GLI1 encodes transcription activator GLI1. It is a transcription activator that acts as a key effector of the smoothened signaling pathway, and which plays a role in craniofacial development and digital development, as well as development of the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract. It binds to the DNA consensus sequence 5'-GACCACCCA-3'.
function_by_symbol.GLI2: GLI2 encodes transcription activator GLI2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that acts as a key effector of the smoothened signaling pathway, and which plays a role in skeleton development. It specifically binds to the minimal GLI-consensus sequence 5'-GACCACCCA-3' to activate or repress the expression of target genes. It functions both as a transcriptional activator and repressor: the full-length GLI2 form (Transcription activator GLI2) acts as a transcription activator following smoothened activation, while the Transcription repressor GLI2R, which is generated in absence of smoothened, acts as a transcription repressor.
function_by_symbol.GNA11: GNA11 encodes G protein subunit alpha 11. Based in part on similarity, it is a guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G proteins) function as transducers downstream of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in numerous signaling cascades. The alpha chain contains the guanine nucleotide binding site and alternates between an active, GTP-bound state and an inactive, GDP-bound state.
