The alpha subunit has a low GTPase activity that converts bound GTP to GDP, thereby terminating the signal.
function_by_symbol.GNA12: GNA12 encodes guanine nucleotide-binding protein subunit alpha-12. Based in part on similarity, guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G proteins) are involved as modulators or transducers in various transmembrane signaling systems. It activates effector molecule RhoA by binding and activating RhoGEFs (ARHGEF12/LARG). GNA12-dependent Rho signaling subsequently regulates transcription factor AP-1 (activating protein-1).
function_by_symbol.GNA13: GNA13 encodes guanine nucleotide-binding protein subunit alpha-13. Based in part on similarity, guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G proteins) are involved as modulators or transducers in various transmembrane signaling systems. It activates effector molecule RhoA by binding and activating RhoGEFs (ARHGEF1/p115RhoGEF, ARHGEF11/PDZ-RhoGEF and ARHGEF12/LARG). GNA13-dependent Rho signaling subsequently regulates transcription factor AP-1 (activating protein-1).
function_by_symbol.GNAQ: GNAQ encodes guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(q) subunit alpha. Based in part on similarity, it is a guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G proteins) function as transducers downstream of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in numerous signaling cascades. The alpha chain contains the guanine nucleotide binding site and alternates between an active, GTP-bound state and an inactive, GDP-bound state. The alpha subunit has a low GTPase activity that converts bound GTP to GDP, thereby terminating the signal.
function_by_symbol.GNAS: GNAS is a complex imprinted locus with maternally, paternally, and biallelically expressed transcripts. Alternative promoters and first exons generate distinct products, including noncoding RNAs and forms of the stimulatory G-protein alpha subunit. The latter couples receptor activation to adenylyl cyclase. Parent-of-origin expression and transcript structure are therefore central features of the locus, rather than all transcripts representing one uniformly expressed protein.
function_by_symbol.GNB1: GNB1 encodes guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(T) subunit beta-1. Based in part on similarity, the beta-gamma dimer stabilizes the GDP-bound inactive alpha subunit by inhibiting spontaneous GDP dissociation. It participates in bitter and sweet taste transduction as well as in umami (monosodium glutamate, monopotassium glutamate, and inosine monophosphate) taste transduction.
function_by_symbol.GOPC: GOPC encodes golgi-associated PDZ and coiled-coil motif-containing protein. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to intracellular protein trafficking and degradation. It may regulate CFTR chloride currents and acid-induced ASIC3 currents by modulating cell surface expression of both channels. It may also regulate the intracellular trafficking of the ADR1B receptor.
function_by_symbol.GPC3: GPC3 encodes glypican-3. Based in part on similarity, it negatively regulates the hedgehog signaling pathway when attached via the GPI-anchor to the cell surface by competing with the hedgehog receptor PTC1 for binding to hedgehog proteins. It positively regulates the canonical Wnt signaling pathway by binding to the Wnt receptor Frizzled and stimulating the binding of the Frizzled receptor to Wnt ligands. It positively regulates the non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.GPS2: GPS2 encodes g protein pathway suppressor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a key regulator of inflammation, lipid metabolism and mitochondrion homeostasis that acts by inhibiting the activity of the ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2N/Ubc13, thereby inhibiting 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitination. It functions as a transcription coactivator in adipocytes by promoting the recruitment of PPARG to promoters: acts by inhibiting the activity of the ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2N/Ubc13, leading to stabilization of KDM4A and subsequent histone H3 'Lys-9' (H3K9) demethylation. It promotes cholesterol efflux by acting as a transcription coactivator.
function_by_symbol.GREM1: GREM1 encodes gremlin-1. Based in part on similarity, it functions as inhibitor of monocyte chemotaxis.
function_by_symbol.GRIN2A: GRIN2A encodes glutamate receptor ionotropic, NMDA 2A. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (NMDARs) that function as heterotetrameric, ligand-gated cation channels with high calcium permeability and voltage-dependent block by Mg(2+). It participates in the synaptic plasticity regulation through activation by the L-glutamate releaseed by BEST1, into the synaptic cleft, upon F2R/PAR-1 activation in astrocyte.
function_by_symbol.GRIPAP1: GRIPAP1 encodes GRIP1-associated protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it regulates the endosomal recycling back to the neuronal plasma membrane, possibly by connecting early and late recycling endosomal domains and promoting segregation of recycling endosomes from early endosomal membranes. It participates in the localization of recycling endosomes to dendritic spines, thereby playing a role in the maintenance of dendritic spine morphology.
function_by_symbol.GRM1: GRM1 encodes metabotropic glutamate receptor 1. Based in part on similarity, it may participate in the central action of glutamate in the CNS, such as long-term potentiation in the hippocampus and long-term depression in the cerebellum. It may function in the light response in the retina. It induces GRID1 and GRID2 cation-channel activation via GNAQ-PLC-PKC pathway in dopaminergic neurons and cerebellar Purkinje cell, respectively.
function_by_symbol.GSK3B: GSK3B encodes glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta. Based in part on similarity, it requires primed phosphorylation of the majority of its substrates. It regulates protein synthesis by controlling the activity of initiation factor 2B (EIF2BE/EIF2B5) in the same manner as glycogen synthase. It phosphorylates JUN at sites proximal to its DNA-binding domain, thereby reducing its affinity for DNA.
function_by_symbol.GTF2I: GTF2I encodes general transcription factor II-I. It interacts with the basal transcription machinery by coordinating the formation of a multiprotein complex at the C-FOS promoter, and linking specific signal responsive activator complexes. It promotes the formation of stable high-order complexes of SRF and PHOX1 and interacts cooperatively with PHOX1 to promote serum-inducible transcription of a reporter gene deriven by the C-FOS serum response element (SRE). It functions as a coregulator for USF1 by binding independently two promoter elements, a pyrimidine-rich initiator (Inr) and an upstream E-box.
function_by_symbol.GTF3C2: GTF3C2 encodes general transcription factor 3C polypeptide 2. It is required for RNA polymerase III-mediated transcription. It forms part of TFIIIC that initiates transcription complex assembly on tRNA and is required for transcription of 5S rRNA and other stable nuclear and cytoplasmic RNAs. May play a direct role in stabilizing interactions of TFIIIC2 with TFIIIC1.
function_by_symbol.H1-2: H1-2 encodes histone H1.2. Histone H1 protein binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber. Histone H1-2 is required for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers. Histone H1-2 also acts as a histone reader: specifically recognizes and binds histone H3 trimethylated at 'lys-27' (H3K27me3).
function_by_symbol.H1-3: H1-3 encodes histone H1.3. Based in part on similarity, histone H1 protein binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber. Histones H1 are necessary for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers and promote formation of the H3K27me3 mark by the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex. It also acts as a regulator of individual gene transcription through chromatin remodeling, nucleosome spacing and DNA methylation.
function_by_symbol.H1-4: H1-4 encodes histone H1.4. Histone H1 protein binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber. Histones H1 are necessary for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers and promote formation of the H3K27me3 mark by the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex. It also acts as a regulator of individual gene transcription through chromatin remodeling, nucleosome spacing and DNA methylation.
function_by_symbol.H1-5: H1-5 encodes histone H1.5. Based in part on similarity, histone H1 protein binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber. Histones H1 are necessary for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers and promote formation of the H3K27me3 mark by the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex. It also acts as a regulator of individual gene transcription through chromatin remodeling, nucleosome spacing and DNA methylation.
function_by_symbol.H2AC11: H2AC11 encodes histone H2A type 1. Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin, limiting DNA accessibility to the cellular machineries which require DNA as a template. Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.

Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.

Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.

Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.
function_by_symbol.H2BC11: H2BC11 encodes histone H2B type 1-J. Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin, limiting DNA accessibility to the cellular machineries which require DNA as a template. Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. It may contribute to the formation of the functional antimicrobial barrier of the colonic epithelium, and to the bactericidal activity of amniotic fluid.

DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.

Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.

Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. It may contribute to the formation of the functional antimicrobial barrier of the colonic epithelium, and to the bactericidal activity of amniotic fluid.
function_by_symbol.H3-3A: H3-3A encodes the histone variant H3.3, which is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA replication and contributes to regulation of chromatin structure and transcription. It constitutes the predominant form of histone H3 in non-dividing cells and is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA synthesis. Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin, limiting DNA accessibility to the cellular machineries which require DNA as a template. Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability.
function_by_symbol.H3-3B: H3-3B encodes the histone variant H3.3, which participates in replication-independent nucleosome assembly and regulation of chromatin organization. It constitutes the predominant form of histone H3 in non-dividing cells and is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA synthesis. Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin, limiting DNA accessibility to the cellular machineries which require DNA as a template. Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability.

Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.

DNA accessibility is regulated via a complex set of post-translational modifications of histones, also called histone code, and nucleosome remodeling.
function_by_symbol.HAVCR2: HAVCR2 encodes hepatitis A virus cellular receptor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a cell surface receptor implicated in modulating innate and adaptive immune responses. Generally accepted to have an inhibiting function. It reports on stimulating functions suggest that the activity may be influenced by the cellular context and/or the respective ligand.
function_by_symbol.HDAC1: HDAC1 encodes histone deacetylase 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone deacetylase that catalyzes the deacetylation of lysine residues on the N-terminal part of the core histones (H2A, H2B, H3 and H4). Histone deacetylation gives a tag for epigenetic repression and plays an important role in transcriptional regulation, cell cycle progression and developmental events. It is a histone deacetylases act via the formation of large multiprotein complexes.
function_by_symbol.HDAC4: HDAC4 encodes histone deacetylase 4. Histone deacetylation gives a tag for epigenetic repression and plays an important role in transcriptional regulation, cell cycle progression and developmental events. It is a histone deacetylases act via the formation of large multiprotein complexes. It participates in muscle maturation via its interaction with the myocyte enhancer factors such as MEF2A, MEF2C and MEF2D.
function_by_symbol.HDAC7: HDAC7 encodes histone deacetylase 7. Based in part on similarity, histone deacetylation gives a tag for epigenetic repression and plays an important role in transcriptional regulation, cell cycle progression and developmental events. It is a histone deacetylases act via the formation of large multiprotein complexes. It participates in muscle maturation by repressing transcription of myocyte enhancer factors such as MEF2A, MEF2B and MEF2C.
function_by_symbol.HELQ: HELQ encodes helicase POLQ-like. It is a single-stranded 3'-5' DNA helicase that plays a key role in homology-driven double-strand break (DSB) repair. It participates in different DSB repair mechanisms that are guided by annealing of extensive stretches of complementary bases at break ends, such as microhomology-mediated end-joining (MMEJ), single-strand annealing (SSA) or synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA). It possesses both DNA unwinding and annealing activities.
function_by_symbol.HEY1: HEY1 encodes hairy/enhancer-of-split related with YRPW motif protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it specifically required for the Notch-induced endocardial epithelial to mesenchymal transition, which is itself criticial for cardiac valve and septum development. It may be required in conjunction with HEY2 to specify arterial cell fate or identity.
function_by_symbol.HIF1A: HIF1A encodes hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a master transcriptional regulator of the adaptive response to hypoxia. Activity is enhanced by interaction with NCOA1 and/or NCOA2. It participates in the axonal distribution and transport of mitochondria in neurons during hypoxia.
function_by_symbol.HLA-A: HLA-A encodes HLA class I histocompatibility antigen, A alpha chain. May also present self-peptides derived from the signal sequence of secreted or membrane proteins, although T cells specific for these peptides are usually inactivated to prevent autoreactivity. It typically presents intracellular peptide antigens of 8 to 13 amino acids that arise from cytosolic proteolysis via IFNG-induced immunoproteasome or via endopeptidase IDE/insulin-degrading enzyme.
function_by_symbol.HLA-B: HLA-B encodes HLA class I histocompatibility antigen, B alpha chain. May also present self-peptides derived from the signal sequence of secreted or membrane proteins, although T cells specific for these peptides are usually inactivated to prevent autoreactivity. It typically presents intracellular peptide antigens of 8 to 13 amino acids that arise from cytosolic proteolysis via constitutive proteasome and IFNG-induced immunoproteasome. It presents an EBV/HHV-4 epitope derived from BZLF1 (SELEIKRY).
function_by_symbol.HLA-C: HLA-C encodes HLA class I histocompatibility antigen, C alpha chain. Based in part on similarity, it typically presents intracellular peptide antigens of 9 amino acids that arise from cytosolic proteolysis via proteasome. It can bind different peptides containing allele-specific binding motifs, which are mainly defined by anchor residues at position 2 and 9. The low affinity peptides compete with the high affinity peptides impeding KIR-mediated inhibition and favoring lysis of infected cells.
function_by_symbol.HMBS: HMBS encodes porphobilinogen deaminase. The covalently linked cofactor acts as a primer, around which the tetrapyrrole product is assembled.
function_by_symbol.HMGA1: HMGA1 encodes high mobility group AT-hook 1. It is suggested that these proteins could function in nucleosome phasing and in the 3'-end processing of mRNA transcripts. They are also involved in the transcription regulation of genes containing, or in close proximity to A+T-rich regions.
function_by_symbol.HNRNPK: HNRNPK encodes heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K. It binds tenaciously to poly(C) sequences. It likely to play a role in the nuclear metabolism of hnRNAs, particularly for pre-mRNAs that contain cytidine-rich sequences. It can also bind poly(C) single-stranded DNA.
function_by_symbol.HOOK1: HOOK1 encodes protein Hook homolog 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the FTS/Hook/FHIP complex (FHF complex). The FHF complex may function to promote vesicle trafficking and/or fusion via the homotypic vesicular protein sorting complex (the HOPS complex). It is probably involved in the positioning of the microtubules of the manchette and the flagellum in relation to the membrane skeleton.
function_by_symbol.HOOK2: HOOK2 encodes hook microtubule tethering protein 2. It forms part of the FTS/Hook/FHIP complex (FHF complex). The FHF complex may function to promote vesicle trafficking and/or fusion via the homotypic vesicular protein sorting complex (the HOPS complex). It contributes to the establishment and maintenance of centrosome function.
function_by_symbol.HOXA9: HOXA9 encodes homeobox protein Hox-A9. Based in part on similarity, it is a sequence-specific transcription factor which is part of a developmental regulatory system that provides cells with specific positional identities on the anterior-posterior axis. It is required for induction of SELE/E-selectin and VCAM1 on the endothelial cells surface at sites of inflammation. It positively regulates EIF4E-mediated mRNA nuclear export and also increases the translation efficiency of ODC mRNA in the cytoplasm by competing with factors which repress EIF4E activity such as PRH.
function_by_symbol.HSD11B1: HSD11B1 encodes an NADP(H)-dependent enzyme that interconverts active and inactive glucocorticoids. Although the reaction can run in both directions in vitro, the enzyme predominantly acts as a reductase in vivo, converting cortisone to cortisol and increasing local active-glucocorticoid availability. This directional distinction connects its enzymatic role with regulation of glucocorticoid action.
function_by_symbol.HSP90AA1: HSP90AA1 encodes heat shock protein HSP 90-alpha. It undergoes a functional cycle that is linked to its ATPase activity which is essential for its chaperone activity. This cycle probably induces conformational changes in the client proteins, thereby causing their activation. It interacts dynamically with various co-chaperones that modulate its substrate recognition, ATPase cycle and chaperone function.
function_by_symbol.HTRA1: HTRA1 encodes serine protease HTRA1. It is a serine protease with a variety of targets, including extracellular matrix proteins such as fibronectin. It may also degrade proteoglycans, such as aggrecan, decorin and fibromodulin. It regulates the availability of insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) by cleaving IGF-binding proteins.
function_by_symbol.ICOS: ICOS encodes inducible T-cell costimulator. Based in part on similarity, it is an essential both for efficient interaction between T and B-cells and for normal antibody responses to T-cell dependent antigens. It prevents the apoptosis of pre-activated T-cells. It contributes to CD40-mediated class switching of immunoglobin isotypes.
function_by_symbol.ICOSLG: ICOSLG encodes ICOS ligand. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a costimulatory signal for T-cell proliferation and cytokine secretion. It also induces B-cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells. Could play an important role in mediating local tissue responses to inflammatory conditions, as well as in modulating the secondary immune response by co-stimulating memory T-cell function.
function_by_symbol.ID3: ID3 encodes DNA-binding protein inhibitor ID-3. It participates in myogenesis by inhibiting skeletal muscle and cardiac myocyte differentiation and promoting muscle precursor cells proliferation. It inhibits the binding of E2A-containing protein complexes to muscle creatine kinase E-box enhancer. It regulates the circadian clock by repressing the transcriptional activator activity of the CLOCK-BMAL1 heterodimer.
function_by_symbol.IFNGR1: IFNGR1 encodes interferon gamma receptor 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor subunit for interferon gamma/INFG that plays crucial roles in antimicrobial, antiviral, and antitumor responses by activating effector immune cells and enhancing antigen presentation. It associates with transmembrane accessory factor IFNGR2 to form a functional receptor. STAT3 can also be activated in a similar manner although activation seems weaker.
function_by_symbol.IGF1: IGF1 encodes insulin-like growth factor 1. Based in part on similarity, the insulin-like growth factors, isolated from plasma, are structurally and functionally related to insulin but have a much higher growth-promoting activity. It stimulates glucose transport in bone-derived osteoblastic (PyMS) cells and is effective at much lower concentrations than insulin, not only regarding glycogen and DNA synthesis but also with regard to enhancing glucose uptake. May play a role in synapse maturation.
function_by_symbol.IGF1R: IGF1R encodes insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor. It is a receptor tyrosine kinase which mediates actions of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1). It binds IGF1 with high affinity and IGF2 and insulin (INS) with a lower affinity. The activated IGF1R is involved in cell growth and survival control.
function_by_symbol.IGH: IGH is the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus, containing variable, diversity, joining, and constant segments. During B-cell development, DNA rearrangement assembles a variable region by joining diversity and joining segments and then a variable segment. Subsequent class switching changes the constant-region context. Segment recombination, junctional diversity, and somatic hypermutation contribute to the range of antigen recognition without each antibody specificity corresponding to a separate inherited gene.
function_by_symbol.IGHV4-34: IGHV4-34 encodes immunoglobulin heavy variable 4-34. Immunoglobulins, also known as antibodies, are membrane-bound or secreted glycoproteins produced by B lymphocytes. The antigen binding site is formed by the variable domain of one heavy chain, together with that of its associated light chain. Thus, each immunoglobulin has two antigen binding sites with remarkable affinity for a particular antigen.
function_by_symbol.IGL: IGL is the immunoglobulin lambda light-chain locus. In developing B cells, a variable segment joins a joining segment at the DNA level, and the constant segment is incorporated by RNA splicing. Use of different segments, junctional diversity, and somatic hypermutation contribute to antibody diversity. The locus contains both functional segments and pseudogenes, so its organization differs from that of a conventional single protein-coding gene.
function_by_symbol.IGLL5: IGLL5 encodes an immunoglobulin lambda-like polypeptide within the lambda locus. Unlike conventional rearranging immunoglobulin genes, its expression does not require somatic rearrangement. Its first exon is unrelated to immunoglobulin variable segments, whereas later exons correspond to lambda joining and constant segments. This organization distinguishes IGLL5 from an ordinary rearranged antibody light-chain gene.
function_by_symbol.IKBKE: IKBKE encodes inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa-B kinase subunit epsilon. Based in part on similarity, it is also involved in TNFA and inflammatory cytokines, like Interleukin-1, signaling. This activity allows subsequent homodimerization and nuclear translocation of the IRF3 leading to transcriptional activation of pro-inflammatory and antiviral genes including IFNB. It activates NF-kappa-B by mediating phosphorylation and inactivation of CYLD.
function_by_symbol.IKZF3: IKZF3 encodes zinc finger protein Aiolos. It is a transcription factor that plays an important role in the regulation of lymphocyte differentiation. It contributes to regulation of B-cell differentiation, proliferation and maturation to an effector state. It participates in regulating BCL2 expression and controlling apoptosis in T-cells in an IL2-dependent manner.
function_by_symbol.IL10: IL10 encodes interleukin-10. Based in part on similarity, it is a major immune regulatory cytokine that acts on many cells of the immune system where it has profound anti-inflammatory functions, limiting excessive tissue disruption caused by inflammation. Mechanistically, IL10 binds to its heterotetrameric receptor comprising IL10RA and IL10RB leading to JAK1 and STAT2-mediated phosphorylation of STAT3. It targets antigen-presenting cells (APCs) such as macrophages and monocytes and inhibits their release of pro-inflammatory cytokines including granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor /GM-CSF, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor/G-CSF, IL-1 alpha, IL-1 beta, IL-6, IL-8 and TNF.
function_by_symbol.IL3: IL3 encodes interleukin-3. Based in part on similarity, it also stimulates mature basophils, eosinophils, and monocytes to become functionally activated. It participates as well in bone homeostasis and inhibits osteoclast differentiation by preventing NF-kappa-B nuclear translocation and activation. Receptor stimulation results in the rapid activation of JAK2 kinase activity leading to STAT5-mediated transcriptional program.
function_by_symbol.IL6ST: IL6ST encodes interleukin-6 receptor subunit beta. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a shared signal-transducing subunit not only for IL6 but also for other cytokine receptor complexes, including IL6, LIF, OSM, CNTF, IL11, CTF1, BSF3, MT-RNR2/humanin, CLCF1 and the heterodimeric complex CRLF1-CLCF1. It engages site 2 of CNTF, CLCF1, LIF, and IL-6, and site 3 of IL27 and IL6. It initiates signal transmission through three mechanisms.
function_by_symbol.INHA: INHA encodes inhibin alpha chain. Based in part on similarity, inhibins/activins are involved in regulating a number of diverse functions such as hypothalamic and pituitary hormone secretion, gonadal hormone secretion, germ cell development and maturation, erythroid differentiation, insulin secretion, nerve cell survival, embryonic axial development or bone growth, depending on their subunit composition. It inhibits the secretion of FSH from the anterior pituitary gland by acting on pituitary gonadotrope cells.
function_by_symbol.INHBA: INHBA encodes inhibin beta A chain. It signals through type I (such as ACVR1B or ACVR1C) and type II receptors (such as ACVR2A, ACVR2B or BMPR2) which, upon ligand binding, phosphorylate SMAD2 and SMAD3 intracellular signaling mediators that form a complex with SMAD4, translocate to the nucleus and modulate gene expression. It can also activate alternative non-canonical intracellular signaling pathways including the p38 MAPK, extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2 (ERK1/2) and c-Jun N-terminal kinases (JNKs) to modulate cell migration and differentiation. It inhibits the secretion of FSH from the anterior pituitary gland by acting on pituitary gonadotrope cells.
function_by_symbol.INHBE: INHBE encodes inhibin beta E chain. Based in part on similarity, inhibins/activins are involved in regulating a number of diverse functions such as hypothalamic and pituitary hormone secretion, gonadal hormone secretion, germ cell development and maturation, erythroid differentiation, insulin secretion, nerve cell survival, embryonic axial development or bone growth, depending on their subunit composition. It plays a central role in the regulation of adipose tissue lipolysis by preventing the influx of fatty acids from adipose tissue into the liver.
function_by_symbol.INMT: INMT encodes indolethylamine N-methyltransferase. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a thioether S-methyltransferase and is active with a variety of thioethers and the corresponding selenium and tellurium compounds, including 3-methylthiopropionaldehyde, dimethyl selenide, dimethyl telluride, 2-methylthioethylamine, 2-methylthioethanol, methyl-n-propyl sulfide and diethyl sulfide. It contributes to the detoxification of selenium compounds. It catalyzes the N-methylation of tryptamine and structurally related compounds.
function_by_symbol.INPP4A: INPP4A encodes inositol polyphosphate-4-phosphatase type I A. Based in part on similarity, it catalyzes the hydrolysis of the 4-position phosphate of phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate (PtdIns(3,4)P2). It also catalyzes inositol 1,3,4-trisphosphate and inositol 1,4-bisphosphate. It antagonizes the PI3K-AKT/PKB signaling pathway by dephosphorylating phosphoinositides and thereby modulating cell cycle progression and cell survival.
function_by_symbol.INPP4B: INPP4B encodes inositol polyphosphate 4-phosphatase type II. It catalyzes the hydrolysis of the 4-position phosphate of phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate, inositol 1,3,4-trisphosphate and inositol 3,4-trisphosphate. It contributes to the late stages of macropinocytosis by dephosphorylating phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate in membrane ruffles. It antagonizes the PI3K-AKT/PKB signaling pathway by dephosphorylating phosphoinositides and thereby modulating cell cycle progression and cell survival.
function_by_symbol.INPPL1: INPPL1 encodes phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 5-phosphatase 2. Based in part on similarity, it is required for correct mitotic spindle orientation and therefore progression of mitosis. It plays a central role in regulation of PI3K-dependent insulin signaling, although the precise molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways remain unclear. It forms part of a signaling pathway that regulates actin cytoskeleton remodeling.
function_by_symbol.INSR: INSR encodes insulin receptor. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase which mediates the pleiotropic actions of insulin. Each of these phosphorylated proteins serve as docking proteins for other signaling proteins that contain Src-homology-2 domains (SH2 domain) that specifically recognize different phosphotyrosine residues, including the p85 regulatory subunit of PI3K and SHP2. The net effect of this pathway is to produce a translocation of the glucose transporter SLC2A4/GLUT4 from cytoplasmic vesicles to the cell membrane to facilitate glucose transport.
function_by_symbol.INTS12: INTS12 encodes integrator complex subunit 12. It forms part of the integrator complex, a multiprotein complex that terminates RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription in the promoter-proximal region of genes. The integrator complex is also involved in terminating the synthesis of non-coding Pol II transcripts, such as enhancer RNAs (eRNAs), small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs), telomerase RNAs and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). It mediates recruitment of cytoplasmic dynein to the nuclear envelope, probably as component of the integrator complex.
function_by_symbol.IRF1: IRF1 encodes interferon regulatory factor 1. It stimulates both innate and acquired immune responses through the activation of specific target genes and can act as a transcriptional activator and repressor regulating target genes by binding to an interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE) in their promoters. It has an essential role in IFNG-dependent immunity to mycobacteria. It competes with the transcriptional repressor ZBED2 for binding to a common consensus sequence in gene promoters.
function_by_symbol.IRF2: IRF2 encodes interferon regulatory factor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA-binding transcription factor that specifically binds to the upstream regulatory region of type I interferon (IFN) and IFN-inducible genes and regulates their expression. It also acts as an activator for several genes including H4 and IL7. Constitutively binds to the ISRE promoter to activate IL7.
function_by_symbol.IRS1: IRS1 encodes insulin receptor substrate 1. Based in part on similarity, it plays therefore an important role in development, growth, glucose homeostasis as well as lipid metabolism. Activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway is responsible for most of insulin metabolic effects in the cell, and the Ras/Raf/MEK/MAPK is involved in the regulation of gene expression and in cooperation with the PI3K pathway regulates cell growth and differentiation. It acts a positive regulator of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway through suppression of DVL2 autophagy-mediated degradation leading to cell proliferation.
function_by_symbol.IRS2: IRS2 encodes insulin receptor substrate 2. Based in part on similarity, it plays therefore an important role in development, growth, glucose homeostasis as well as lipid metabolism. Activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway is responsible for most of insulin metabolic effects in the cell, and the Ras/Raf/MEK/MAPK is involved in the regulation of gene expression and in cooperation with the PI3K pathway regulates cell growth and differentiation. It acts a positive regulator of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway through suppression of DVL2 autophagy-mediated degradation leading to cell proliferation.
function_by_symbol.IRS4: IRS4 encodes insulin receptor substrate 4. It functions as an interface between multiple growth factor receptors possessing tyrosine kinase activity, such as insulin receptor, IGF1R and FGFR1, and a complex network of intracellular signaling molecules containing SH2 domains. It participates in the IGF1R mitogenic signaling pathway. It promotes the AKT1 signaling pathway and BAD phosphorylation during insulin stimulation without activation of RPS6KB1 or the inhibition of apoptosis.
function_by_symbol.ITK: ITK encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ITK/TSK. Based in part on similarity, it is a tyrosine kinase that plays an essential role in regulation of the adaptive immune response. It regulates the development, function and differentiation of conventional T-cells and nonconventional NKT-cells. It phosphorylates 2 essential adapter proteins: the linker for activation of T-cells/LAT protein and LCP2.
function_by_symbol.JAK1: JAK1 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase JAK1. Functionally, is involved in the IFN-alpha/beta/gamma signal pathway. It directly phosphorylates STAT proteins but also activates STAT signaling through the transactivation of other JAK kinases associated with signaling receptors. It participates in the MT-RNR2/humanin-mediated signaling pathway leading to STAT3 phosphorylation.
function_by_symbol.JAK2: JAK2 encodes a nonreceptor tyrosine kinase that associates with cytokine receptors and transmits signals through STAT proteins and other downstream pathways in hematopoietic cells. Functionally, plays a pivotal role in signal transduction and is involved in various processes such as cell growth, development, differentiation or histone modifications. It mediates essential signaling events in both innate and adaptive immunity. Phosphorylated STATs then form homodimer or heterodimers and translocate to the nucleus to activate gene transcription.
function_by_symbol.JAK3: JAK3 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase JAK3. It is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase involved in various processes such as cell growth, development, or differentiation. It mediates essential signaling events in both innate and adaptive immunity and plays a crucial role in hematopoiesis during T-cells development. Phosphorylated STATs then form homodimer or heterodimers and translocate to the nucleus to activate gene transcription.
function_by_symbol.JARID2: JARID2 encodes protein Jumonji. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone reader that acts as a regulator of histone methyltransferase complexes, thereby playing an essential role in embryonic development, including heart and liver development, neural tube fusion process and hematopoiesis. It specifically recognizes and binds histone H2A ubiquitinated at 'Lys-119' (H2AK119Ub). It functions as an accessory subunit for the core PRC2 (Polycomb repressive complex 2) complex, which mediates histone H3K27 (H3K27me3) trimethylation on chromatin.
function_by_symbol.JAZF1: JAZF1 encodes juxtaposed with another zinc finger protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a transcriptional corepressor of orphan nuclear receptor NR2C2. It inhibits expression of the gluconeogenesis enzyme PCK2 through inhibition of NR2C2 activity. It is also involved in transcriptional activation of NAMPT by promoting expression of PPARA and PPARD.
function_by_symbol.JUNB: JUNB encodes transcription factor JunB. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor involved in regulating gene activity following the primary growth factor response. It heterodimerizes with proteins of the FOS family to form an AP-1 transcription complex, thereby enhancing its DNA binding activity to an AP-1 consensus sequence and its transcriptional activity.
function_by_symbol.KAT6A: KAT6A encodes histone acetyltransferase KAT6A. It forms part of the MOZ/MORF complex which has a histone H3 acetyltransferase activity. It may act as a transcriptional coactivator for RUNX1 and RUNX2. It acetylates p53/TP53 at 'Lys-120' and 'Lys-382' and controls its transcriptional activity via association with PML.
function_by_symbol.KAT8: KAT8 encodes lysine acetyltransferase 8. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone acetyltransferase that catalyzes histone H4 acetylation at 'Lys-5'- and 'Lys-8' (H4K5ac and H4K8ac) or 'Lys-16' (H4K16ac), depending on the context. It is the catalytic component of the MSL histone acetyltransferase complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates the majority of histone H4 acetylation at 'Lys-16' (H4K16ac), an epigenetic mark that prevents chromatin compaction. The MSL complex is required for chromosome stability and genome integrity by maintaining homeostatic levels of H4K16ac.
function_by_symbol.KBTBD4: KBTBD4 encodes kelch repeat and BTB domain-containing protein 4. It is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex which targets CoREST corepressor complex components RCOR1, KDM1A/LSD1 and HDAC2 for proteasomal degradation. RCOR1 is likely to be the primary target while degradation of KDM1A and HDAC2 is likely due to their association with RCOR1. It also targets RCOR3, MIER2 and MIER3 for proteasomal degradation as well as associated proteins ZNF217 and RREB1.
function_by_symbol.KCNH5: KCNH5 encodes potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily H member 5. The kinetic is characterized by a slow activation time course and a small voltage dependence of the activation time constants, therefore, starts to open at more negative voltages. The activation kinetics depend on the prepulse potential and external divalent cation concentration. The time course of activation is biphasic with a fast and a slowly activating current component.
function_by_symbol.KCNJ12: KCNJ12 encodes potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 12. It probably participates in establishing action potential waveform and excitability of neuronal and muscle tissues. Inward rectifier potassium channels are characterized by a greater tendency to allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it. The inward rectification is mainly due to the blockage of outward current by internal magnesium.
function_by_symbol.KCNJ8: KCNJ8 encodes potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 8. Based in part on similarity, inward rectifier potassium channels are characterized by a greater tendency to allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it. The inward rectification is mainly due to the blockage of outward current by internal magnesium. This channel is activated by internal ATP and can be blocked by external barium.
function_by_symbol.KCNQ1: KCNQ1 encodes potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily KQT member 1. Based in part on similarity, it associates with KCNE beta subunits that modulates current kinetics. It induces a voltage-dependent current by rapidly activating and slowly deactivating potassium-selective outward current. It also promotes a delayed voltage activated potassium current showing outward rectification characteristic.
function_by_symbol.KCNQ5: KCNQ5 encodes potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 5. It associates with KCNQ3/Kv7.3 pore-forming subunit to form a potassium channel which contributes to M-type current, a slowly activating and deactivating potassium conductance which plays a critical role in determining the subthreshold electrical excitability of neurons. It also forms a functional channel with KCNQ1/Kv7.1 subunit that may contribute to vasoconstriction and hypertension.
function_by_symbol.KDM5A: KDM5A encodes lysine demethylase 5A. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-4' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code. It does not demethylate histone H3 'Lys-9', H3 'Lys-27', H3 'Lys-36', H3 'Lys-79' or H4 'Lys-20'. It regulates specific gene transcription through DNA-binding on 5'-CCGCCC-3' motif.
function_by_symbol.KDM5C: KDM5C encodes lysine demethylase 5C. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-4' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code. It does not demethylate histone H3 'Lys-9', H3 'Lys-27', H3 'Lys-36', H3 'Lys-79' or H4 'Lys-20'. It participates in transcriptional repression of neuronal genes by recruiting histone deacetylases and REST at neuron-restrictive silencer elements.
function_by_symbol.KDM6A: KDM6A encodes lysine demethylase 6A. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates 'Lys-27' of histone H3, thereby playing a central role in histone code. It plays a central role in regulation of posterior development, by regulating HOX gene expression. It plays a demethylase-independent role in chromatin remodeling to regulate T-box family member-dependent gene expression.
function_by_symbol.KEAP1: KEAP1 encodes kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1. It is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that regulates the response to oxidative stress by targeting NFE2L2/NRF2 for ubiquitination. The BCR(KEAP1) complex also mediates ubiquitination of SQSTM1/p62, increasing SQSTM1/p62 sequestering activity and degradation. The BCR(KEAP1) complex also targets BPTF and PGAM5 for ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome.
function_by_symbol.KHDRBS2: KHDRBS2 encodes KH domain-containing, RNA-binding, signal transduction-associated protein 2. Based in part on similarity, it is an RNA-binding protein that plays a role in the regulation of alternative splicing and influences mRNA splice site selection and exon inclusion. It binds both poly(A) and poly(U) homopolymers. It induces an increased concentration-dependent incorporation of exon in CD44 pre-mRNA by direct binding to purine-rich exonic enhancer.
function_by_symbol.KIF26B: KIF26B encodes kinesin family member 26B. Based in part on similarity, it is essential for embryonic kidney development. It contributes to the compact adhesion between mesenchymal cells adjacent to the ureteric buds, possibly by interacting with MYH10. This could lead to the establishment of the basolateral integrity of the mesenchyme and the polarized expression of ITGA8, which maintains the GDNF expression required for further ureteric bud attraction.
function_by_symbol.KIF5B: KIF5B encodes kinesin-1 heavy chain. Based in part on similarity, it can induce formation of neurite-like membrane protrusions in non-neuronal cells in a ZFYVE27-dependent manner. It regulates centrosome and nuclear positioning during mitotic entry. It is required for anterograde axonal transportation of MAPK8IP3/JIP3 which is essential for MAPK8IP3/JIP3 function in axon elongation.
function_by_symbol.KLF17: KLF17 encodes krueppel-like factor 17. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription repressor that binds to the promoter of target genes and prevents their expression. It may be a germ cell-specific transcription factor that plays important roles in spermatid differentiation and oocyte development.
function_by_symbol.KLHL6: KLHL6 encodes kelch-like protein 6. It is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that acts as a multifunctional regulator of B-cell receptor (BCR) signaling, germinal center formation, and T-cell function. It functions by mediating polyubiquitination of target proteins, leading to their proteasomal degradation. It targets the BCR signaling subunits CD79A and CD79B for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, thereby controlling surface BCR homeostasis.
function_by_symbol.KLLN: KLLN encodes killin. It is a DNA-binding protein involved in S phase checkpoint control-coupled apoptosis by mediating p53/TP53-induced apoptosis. It has the ability to inhibit DNA synthesis and S phase arrest coupled to apoptosis. It has affinity to both double- and single-stranded DNA.
function_by_symbol.KMT2A: KMT2A encodes a histone methyltransferase that helps establish H3K4 methylation and regulate transcriptional programs important for development and hematopoiesis. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that plays an essential role in early development and hematopoiesis. It is a catalytic subunit of the MLL1/MLL complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates both methylation of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4me) complex and acetylation of 'Lys-16' of histone H4 (H4K16ac). It catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism.
function_by_symbol.KMT2B: KMT2B encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase 2B. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism. It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery predominantly forms H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It likely plays a redundant role with KMT2C in enriching H3K4me1 marks on primed and active enhancer elements.
function_by_symbol.KMT2C: KMT2C encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase 2C. It is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4). It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery predominantly forms H3K4me1 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It likely plays a redundant role with KMT2D in enriching H3K4me1 mark on primed and active enhancer elements.
function_by_symbol.KMT2D: KMT2D encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase 2D. It is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4). It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery predominantly forms H3K4me1 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It functions as a coactivator for estrogen receptor by being recruited by ESR1, thereby activating transcription.
function_by_symbol.KNSTRN: KNSTRN encodes small kinetochore-associated protein. It is an essential component of the mitotic spindle required for faithful chromosome segregation and progression into anaphase. It promotes the metaphase-to-anaphase transition and is required for chromosome alignment, normal timing of sister chromatid segregation, and maintenance of spindle pole architecture. The astrin (SPAG5)-kinastrin (SKAP) complex promotes stable microtubule-kinetochore attachments.
function_by_symbol.LAMP1: LAMP1 encodes lysosome-associated membrane glycoprotein 1. It functions as an important regulator of lysosomal lumen pH regulation by acting as a direct inhibitor of the proton channel TMEM175, facilitating lysosomal acidification for optimal hydrolase activity. It also plays an important role in NK-cells cytotoxicity.
function_by_symbol.LATS1: LATS1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase LATS1. The core of this pathway is composed of a kinase cascade wherein STK3/MST2 and STK4/MST1, in complex with its regulatory protein SAV1, phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2 in complex with its regulatory protein MOB1, which in turn phosphorylates and inactivates YAP1 oncoprotein and WWTR1/TAZ. It negatively regulates G2/M transition by down-regulating CDK1 kinase activity. It participates in the control of p53 expression.
function_by_symbol.LATS2: LATS2 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase LATS2. The core of this pathway is composed of a kinase cascade wherein STK3/MST2 and STK4/MST1, in complex with its regulatory protein SAV1, phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2 in complex with its regulatory protein MOB1, which in turn phosphorylates and inactivates YAP1 oncoprotein and WWTR1/TAZ. It also phosphorylates YAP1 in response to cell contact inhibition-driven WWP1 ubiquitination of AMOTL2, which results in LATS2 activation. It negatively regulates G1/S transition by down-regulating cyclin E/CDK2 kinase activity.
function_by_symbol.LCK: LCK encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Lck. It is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays an essential role in the selection and maturation of developing T-cells in the thymus and in the function of mature T-cells. It contributes to T-cell antigen receptor (TCR)-linked signal transduction pathways. It associates directly with the cytoplasmic tail of CD2, which leads to hyperphosphorylation and activation of LCK.
function_by_symbol.LIG4: LIG4 encodes DNA ligase 4. It catalyzes the NHEJ ligation step of the broken DNA during DSB repair by resealing the DNA breaks after the gap filling is completed. It joins single-strand breaks in a double-stranded polydeoxynucleotide in an ATP-dependent reaction. LIG4 is mechanistically flexible: it can ligate nicks as well as compatible DNA overhangs alone, while in the presence of XRCC4, it can ligate ends with 2-nucleotides (nt) microhomology and 1-nt gaps.
function_by_symbol.LMNA: LMNA encodes prelamin-A/C. The structural integrity of the lamina is strictly controlled by the cell cycle, as seen by the disintegration and formation of the nuclear envelope in prophase and telophase, respectively. Lamin A and C are present in equal amounts in the lamina of mammals.
function_by_symbol.LPL: LPL encodes lipoprotein lipase. It is a key enzyme in triglyceride metabolism. It catalyzes the hydrolysis of triglycerides from circulating chylomicrons and very low density lipoproteins (VLDL), and thereby plays an important role in lipid clearance from the blood stream, lipid utilization and storage. Although it has both phospholipase and triglyceride lipase activities it is primarily a triglyceride lipase with low but detectable phospholipase activity.
function_by_symbol.LRP1: LRP1 encodes LDL receptor related protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it is required for early embryonic development. It participates in cellular lipid homeostasis. It participates in the plasma clearance of chylomicron remnants and activated LRPAP1 (alpha 2-macroglobulin), as well as the local metabolism of complexes between plasminogen activators and their endogenous inhibitors.
function_by_symbol.LRP5: LRP5 encodes LDL receptor related protein 5. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a coreceptor with members of the frizzled family of seven-transmembrane spanning receptors to transduce signal by Wnt proteins. It activates the canonical Wnt signaling pathway that controls cell fate determination and self-renewal during embryonic development and adult tissue regeneration. It functions as a coreceptor for non-Wnt proteins, such as norrin/NDP.
function_by_symbol.LSM14A: LSM14A encodes LSM14A mRNA processing body assembly factor. It is essential for formation of P-bodies, cytoplasmic structures that provide storage sites for translationally inactive mRNAs and protect them from degradation. It functions as a repressor of mRNA translation. May play a role in mitotic spindle assembly.
function_by_symbol.LTK: LTK encodes leukocyte tyrosine kinase receptor. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor with a tyrosine-protein kinase activity. It phosphorylates almost exclusively at the first tyrosine of the Y-x-x-x-Y-Y motif. It participates in regulation of the secretory pathway involving endoplasmic reticulum (ER) export sites (ERESs) and ER to Golgi transport.
function_by_symbol.LTN1: LTN1 encodes listerin E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase component of the ribosome quality control complex (RQC), a ribosome-associated complex that mediates ubiquitination and extraction of incompletely synthesized nascent chains for proteasomal degradation.
function_by_symbol.LYN: LYN encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Lyn. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that transmits signals from cell surface receptors and plays an important role in the regulation of innate and adaptive immune responses, hematopoiesis, responses to growth factors and cytokines, integrin signaling, but also responses to DNA damage and genotoxic agents. It functions primarily as negative regulator, but can also function as activator, depending on the context. It is required for the initiation of the B-cell response, but also for its down-regulation and termination.
function_by_symbol.LYST: LYST encodes lysosomal-trafficking regulator. Based in part on similarity, it is an adapter protein that regulates and/or fission of intracellular vesicles such as lysosomes.
function_by_symbol.LZTR1: LZTR1 encodes leucine-zipper-like transcriptional regulator 1. It is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex that mediates ubiquitination of Ras GTPases (M-Ras/MRAS, K-Ras/KRAS, N-Ras/NRAS and H-Ras/HRAS) and Ras-like protein RIT1. It functions as a negative regulator of RAS-MAPK signaling by controlling Ras levels and decreasing Ras association with membranes.
function_by_symbol.MAD2L2: MAD2L2 encodes mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint protein MAD2B. It is an adapter protein able to interact with different proteins and involved in different biological processes. It mediates the interaction between the error-prone DNA polymerase zeta catalytic subunit REV3L and the inserter polymerase REV1, thereby mediating the second polymerase switching in translesion DNA synthesis. It forms part of the shieldin complex, which plays an important role in repair of DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs).
function_by_symbol.MAF: MAF encodes transcription factor Maf. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a transcriptional activator or repressor. It participates in embryonic lens fiber cell development. It recruits the transcriptional coactivators CREBBP and/or EP300 to crystallin promoters leading to up-regulation of crystallin gene during lens fiber cell differentiation.
function_by_symbol.MAFB: MAFB encodes transcription factor MafB. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a transcriptional activator or repressor. It plays a pivotal role in regulating lineage-specific hematopoiesis by repressing ETS1-mediated transcription of erythroid-specific genes in myeloid cells. It is required for monocytic, macrophage, osteoclast, podocyte and islet beta cell differentiation.
function_by_symbol.MAGEC1: MAGEC1 encodes a member of the MAGE antigen family, whose protein-derived antigens can be recognized by cytotoxic T lymphocytes. The protein contains an extended region of short repeats preceding its MAGE-homology region. Its normal molecular description therefore includes a distinctive repeat architecture and an antigenic role.
function_by_symbol.MAGI2: MAGI2 encodes membrane-associated guanylate kinase, WW and PDZ domain-containing protein 2. Based in part on similarity, it seems to act as a scaffold molecule at synaptic junctions by assembling neurotransmitter receptors and cell adhesion proteins. It contributes to nerve growth factor (NGF)-induced recruitment of RAPGEF2 to late endosomes and neurite outgrowth. May play a role in regulating activin-mediated signaling in neuronal cells.
function_by_symbol.MAGOH: MAGOH encodes mago homolog, exon junction complex subunit. It is required for pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome. It plays a redundant role with MAGOHB as core component of the exon junction complex (EJC) and in the nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) pathway. The EJC is a dynamic structure consisting of core proteins and several peripheral nuclear and cytoplasmic associated factors that join the complex only transiently either during EJC assembly or during subsequent mRNA metabolism.
function_by_symbol.MALAT1: MALAT1 produces a nuclear long noncoding RNA from a precursor that also yields the small mascRNA product through RNase P cleavage. The mature long RNA lacks a conventional poly(A) tail and is stabilized by a triple-helical structure at its 3' end. It is thought to act as a scaffold for ribonucleoprotein assemblies and participates in regulation of gene expression and the cell cycle.
function_by_symbol.MALT1: MALT1 encodes mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it mediates BCL10 cleavage: MALT1-dependent BCL10 cleavage plays an important role in T-cell antigen receptor-induced integrin adhesion. It participates in the induction of T helper 17 cells (Th17) differentiation. It cleaves RC3H1 and ZC3H12A in response to T-cell receptor (TCR) stimulation which releases their cooperatively repressed targets to promote Th17 cell differentiation.
function_by_symbol.MAMLD1: MAMLD1 encodes mastermind-like domain-containing protein 1. It transactivates the HES3 promoter independently of NOTCH proteins. HES3 is a non-canonical NOTCH target gene which lacks binding sites for RBPJ.
function_by_symbol.MAP2K1: MAP2K1 encodes dual specificity mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 1. MAP2K1/MEK1 has been shown to export PPARG from the nucleus. The MAPK/ERK cascade is also involved in the regulation of endosomal dynamics, including lysosome processing and endosome cycling through the perinuclear recycling compartment (PNRC), as well as in the fragmentation of the Golgi apparatus during mitosis.
function_by_symbol.MAP2K4: MAP2K4 encodes dual specificity mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 4. It is an essential component of the stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinase (SAP/JNK) signaling pathway. With MAP2K7/MKK7, is the one of the only known kinase to directly activate the stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinases MAPK8/JNK1, MAPK9/JNK2 and MAPK10/JNK3. The phosphorylation of the Thr residue by MAP2K7/MKK7 seems to be the prerequisite for JNK activation at least in response to pro-inflammatory cytokines, while other stimuli activate both MAP2K4/MKK4 and MAP2K7/MKK7 which synergistically phosphorylate JNKs.
function_by_symbol.MAP3K13: MAP3K13 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 13. It activates the JUN N-terminal pathway through activation of the MAP kinase kinase MAP2K7. It acts synergistically with PRDX3 to regulate the activation of NF-kappa-B in the cytosol. This activation is kinase-dependent and involves activating the IKK complex, the IKBKB-containing complex that phosphorylates inhibitors of NF-kappa-B.
function_by_symbol.MAP3K14: MAP3K14 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 14. It phosphorylates CHUK/IKKA, thereby promoting proteolytic processing of NFKB2/P100, which leads to NF-kappa-B activation via the non-canonical pathway. It has an essential role in the non-canonical NF-kappa-B signaling that regulates genes encoding molecules involved in B-cell survival, lymphoid organogenesis, and immune response.
function_by_symbol.MAP3K7: MAP3K7 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 7. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine kinase which acts as an essential component of the MAP kinase signal transduction pathway. It contributes to the cascades of cellular responses evoked by changes in the environment. It promotes TRIM5 capsid-specific restriction activity.
function_by_symbol.MAP3K8: MAP3K8 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 8. It is required for lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced, TLR4-mediated activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway in macrophages, thus being critical for production of the pro-inflammatory cytokine TNF (TNF) during immune responses. It participates in the regulation of T-helper cell differentiation and IFNG expression in T-cells. It transduces CD40 and TNFRSF1A signals that activate ERK in B-cells and macrophages, and thus may play a role in the regulation of immunoglobulin production.
function_by_symbol.MAPK1: MAPK1 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine kinase which acts as an essential component of the MAP kinase signal transduction pathway. MAPK1/ERK2 and MAPK3/ERK1 are the 2 MAPKs which play an important role in the MAPK/ERK cascade. The MAPK/ERK cascade also plays a role in initiation and regulation of meiosis, mitosis, and postmitotic functions in differentiated cells by phosphorylating a number of transcription factors.
function_by_symbol.MAPK3: MAPK3 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase 3. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine kinase which acts as an essential component of the MAP kinase signal transduction pathway. MAPK1/ERK2 and MAPK3/ERK1 are the 2 MAPKs which play an important role in the MAPK/ERK cascade. The MAPK/ERK cascade also plays a role in initiation and regulation of meiosis, mitosis, and postmitotic functions in differentiated cells by phosphorylating a number of transcription factors.
function_by_symbol.MAPK7: MAPK7 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase 7. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to various cellular processes such as proliferation, differentiation and cell survival. The upstream activator of MAPK7 is the MAPK kinase MAP2K5. May have a role in muscle cell differentiation.
function_by_symbol.MAPKAP1: MAPKAP1 encodes target of rapamycin complex 2 subunit MAPKAP1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), which transduces signals from growth factors to pathways involved in proliferation, cytoskeletal organization, lipogenesis and anabolic output. The mTORC2 complex also phosphorylates various proteins involved in insulin signaling, such as FBXW8 and IGF2BP1 . mTORC2 acts upstream of Rho GTPases to regulate the actin cytoskeleton, probably by activating one or more Rho-type guanine nucleotide exchange factors . mTORC2 promotes the serum-induced formation of stress-fibers or F-actin. It inhibits HRAS and KRAS independently of mTORC2 complex.
function_by_symbol.MARCHF10: MARCHF10 encodes membrane associated ring-CH-type finger 10. E3 ubiquitin ligases accept ubiquitin from an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme in the form of a thioester and then directly transfer the ubiquitin to targeted substrates.
function_by_symbol.MBD4: MBD4 encodes methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 4. It has thymine glycosylase activity and is specific for G:T mismatches within methylated and unmethylated CpG sites. It can also remove uracil or 5-fluorouracil in G:U mismatches. It was first identified as methyl-CpG-binding protein.
function_by_symbol.MCM8: MCM8 encodes DNA helicase MCM8. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the MCM8-MCM9 complex, which is involved in the repair of double-stranded DNA breaks (DBSs) and DNA interstrand cross-links (ICLs) by homologous recombination (HR). The MCM8-MCM9 complex is a 3'-5' DNA helicase and single-stranded (ss)DNA-stimulated ATPase which binds ssDNA in the presence of nucleoside triphosphates. It is required for DNA resection by the MRE11-RAD50-NBN/NBS1 (MRN) complex by recruiting the MRN complex to the repair site and by promoting the complex nuclease activity.
function_by_symbol.MDC1: MDC1 encodes mediator of DNA damage checkpoint protein 1. It is a histone reader protein required for checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest in response to DNA damage within both the S phase and G2/M phases of the cell cycle. It specifically recognizes and binds histone H2AX phosphorylated at 'Ser-139', a marker of DNA damage, serving as a scaffold for the recruitment of DNA repair and signal transduction proteins to discrete foci of DNA damage sites. It is also required for downstream events subsequent to the recruitment of these proteins.
function_by_symbol.MDM2: MDM2 encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase and negative regulator of p53, helping control p53 stability and activity. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination of p53/TP53, leading to its degradation by the proteasome. It inhibits p53/TP53- and p73/TP73-mediated cell cycle arrest and apoptosis by binding its transcriptional activation domain. It also acts as a ubiquitin ligase E3 toward itself and ARRB1.
function_by_symbol.MEAF6: MEAF6 encodes chromatin modification-related protein MEAF6. It forms part of the NuA4 histone acetyltransferase complex which is involved in transcriptional activation of select genes principally by acetylation of nucleosomal histone H4 and H2A. This modification may both alter nucleosome - DNA interactions and promote interaction of the modified histones with other proteins which positively regulate transcription. It forms part of HBO1 complexes, which specifically mediate acetylation of histone H3 at 'Lys-14' (H3K14ac), and have reduced activity toward histone H4.
function_by_symbol.MECOM: MECOM encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase MECOM. Based in part on similarity, may also play a role in apoptosis through regulation of the JNK and TGF-beta signaling. It probably catalyzes the monomethylation of free histone H3 in the cytoplasm which is then transported to the nucleus and incorporated into nucleosomes where SUV39H methyltransferases use it as a substrate to catalyze histone H3 'Lys-9' trimethylation. It likely to be one of the primary histone methyltransferases along with PRDM16 that direct cytoplasmic H3K9me1 methylation.
function_by_symbol.MED12: MED12 encodes mediator of RNA polymerase II transcription subunit 12. It forms part of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in the regulated transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes. Mediator is recruited to promoters by direct interactions with regulatory proteins and serves as a scaffold for the assembly of a functional pre-initiation complex with RNA polymerase II and the general transcription factors. This subunit may specifically regulate transcription of targets of the Wnt signaling pathway and SHH signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.MED28: MED28 encodes mediator complex subunit 28. It forms part of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in the regulated transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes. Mediator is recruited to promoters by direct interactions with regulatory proteins and serves as a scaffold for the assembly of a functional pre-initiation complex with RNA polymerase II and the general transcription factors. It may be part of a complex containing NF2/merlin that participates in cellular signaling to the actin cytoskeleton downstream of tyrosine kinase signaling pathways.
function_by_symbol.MEF2A: MEF2A encodes myocyte enhancer factor 2A. It is also involved in the activation of numerous growth factor- and stress-induced genes. It mediates cellular functions not only in skeletal and cardiac muscle development, but also in neuronal differentiation and survival. It plays diverse roles in the control of cell growth, survival and apoptosis via p38 MAPK signaling in muscle-specific and/or growth factor-related transcription.
function_by_symbol.MEF2C: MEF2C encodes myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2C. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription activator which binds specifically to the MEF2 element present in the regulatory regions of many muscle-specific genes. It controls cardiac morphogenesis and myogenesis, and is also involved in vascular development. It enhances transcriptional activation mediated by SOX18.
function_by_symbol.MEF2D: MEF2D encodes myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2D. Based in part on similarity, it mediates cellular functions not only in skeletal and cardiac muscle development, but also in neuronal differentiation and survival. It plays diverse roles in the control of cell growth, survival and apoptosis via p38 MAPK signaling in muscle-specific and/or growth factor-related transcription. It contributes to the regulation of neuronal apoptosis.
function_by_symbol.METTL14: METTL14 encodes methyltransferase 14, N6-adenosine-methyltransferase non-catalytic subunit. Based in part on similarity, the METTL3-METTL14 heterodimer forms a N6-methyltransferase complex that methylates adenosine residues at the N(6) position of some mRNAs and regulates the circadian clock, differentiation of embryonic stem cells and cortical neurogenesis. M6A regulates spermatogonial differentiation and meiosis and is essential for male fertility and spermatogenesis. M6A also regulates cortical neurogenesis: m6A methylation of transcripts related to transcription factors, neural stem cells, the cell cycle and neuronal differentiation during brain development promotes their destabilization and decay, promoting differentiation of radial glial cells.
function_by_symbol.MGA: MGA encodes MAX gene-associated protein. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a dual-specificity transcription factor, regulating the expression of both MAX-network and T-box family target genes. It acts as a repressor or an activator. It binds to 5'-AATTTCACACCTAGGTGTGAAATT-3' core sequence and seems to regulate MYC-MAX target genes.
function_by_symbol.MGAM: MGAM encodes maltase-glucoamylase. It cleaves the non-reducing alpha-(1,4)-linked glucose residue in linear dextrins with retention of anomeric center stereochemistry. Can cleave alpha-(1,2), alpha-(1,3) and alpha-(1,6) glycosidic linkages with lower efficiency, whereas beta glycosidic linkages are usually not hydrolyzed.
function_by_symbol.MGMT: MGMT encodes methylated-DNA--protein-cysteine methyltransferase. It participates in the cellular defense against the biological effects of O6-methylguanine (O6-MeG) and O4-methylthymine (O4-MeT) in DNA. It repairs the methylated nucleobase in DNA by stoichiometrically transferring the methyl group to a cysteine residue in the enzyme. This is a suicide reaction: the enzyme is irreversibly inactivated.
function_by_symbol.MIB1: MIB1 encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes Delta-mediated NOTCH signaling. It ubiquitinates Delta-family ligands, facilitating their endocytosis and the signaling interaction with NOTCH. The distinction between ligand and receptor is important to this mechanism: the normal functional description concerns modification of the ligand-bearing signaling partner.
function_by_symbol.MIR143: MIR143 encodes a microRNA precursor rather than a protein. MicroRNA production involves sequential processing of a primary transcript by DROSHA and DICER, followed by incorporation of the mature small RNA into a silencing complex. Base pairing with target messenger RNAs can reduce their translation or stability. The RefSeq record represents the precursor stem-loop, distinguishing the genomic precursor from the mature regulatory RNA.
function_by_symbol.MIR17HG: MIR17HG is a noncoding host gene for the MIR17-92 cluster, which contains at least six microRNAs. These regulatory RNAs have roles in survival, proliferation, differentiation, and angiogenesis. Not all host-gene transcripts contain the complete cluster: the longer polycistronic transcript carries it, whereas another noncoding transcript does not. Transcript structure is therefore relevant to the gene's normal regulatory output.
function_by_symbol.MITF: MITF encodes microphthalmia-associated transcription factor. It is a transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of melanocyte survival and differentiation as well as melanosome biogenesis. It binds to M-boxes (5'-TCATGTG-3') and symmetrical DNA sequences (E-boxes) (5'-CACGTG-3') found in the promoter of pigmentation genes, such as tyrosinase (TYR). It participates in the cellular response to amino acid availability by acting downstream of MTOR: in the presence of nutrients, MITF phosphorylation by MTOR promotes its inactivation.
function_by_symbol.MKI67: MKI67 encodes proliferation marker protein Ki-67. Based in part on similarity, it is a protein that associates with the surface of mitotic chromosomes and acts both as a chromosome repellent during early mitosis and chromosome attractant during late mitosis. The MKI67 brush structure prevents chromosomes from collapsing into a single chromatin mass by forming a steric and electrostatic charge barrier: the protein has a high net electrical charge and acts as a surfactant, dispersing chromosomes and enabling independent chromosome motility. It binds DNA, with a preference for supercoiled DNA and AT-rich DNA.
function_by_symbol.MLLT1: MLLT1 encodes protein ENL. It is a chromatin reader component of the super elongation complex (SEC), a complex required to increase the catalytic rate of RNA polymerase II transcription by suppressing transient pausing by the polymerase at multiple sites along the DNA. It specifically recognizes and binds acetylated and crotonylated histones, with a preference for histones that are crotonylated. It has a slightly higher affinity for binding histone H3 crotonylated at 'Lys-27' (H3K27cr) than 'Lys-20' (H3K9cr20).
function_by_symbol.MLLT3: MLLT3 encodes protein AF-9. Based in part on similarity, it is a chromatin reader component of the super elongation complex (SEC), a complex required to increase the catalytic rate of RNA polymerase II transcription by suppressing transient pausing by the polymerase at multiple sites along the DNA. It specifically recognizes and binds acylated histone H3, with a preference for histone H3 that is crotonylated. It recognizes and binds histone H3 crotonylated at 'Lys-9' (H3K9cr), and with slightly lower affinity histone H3 crotonylated at 'Lys-18' (H3K18cr).
function_by_symbol.MN1: MN1 encodes transcriptional activator MN1. Based in part on similarity, it promotes maturation and normal function of calvarial osteoblasts, including expression of the osteoclastogenic cytokine TNFSF11/RANKL. It is necessary for normal development of the membranous bones of the skull.
function_by_symbol.MPEG1: MPEG1 encodes macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein. Based in part on similarity, it plays a central role in antigen cross-presentation in dendritic cells by forming a pore in antigen-containing compartments, thereby promoting delivery of antigens for cross-presentation. It acts by forming a pore in antigen-containing compartments, promoting the release of antigens into the cytosol, enabling generation of MHCI:peptide complexes and T-cell priming.
function_by_symbol.MPO: MPO encodes myeloperoxidase. It promotes NET formation by mediating chromatin disassembly: translocates to the nucleus and specifically binds to nucleosomes, both as monomer and homodimer, leading to nucleosome unstacking and initial chromatin decondensation.
function_by_symbol.MRE11: MRE11 encodes double-strand break repair protein MRE11. Based in part on similarity, it is a core component of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair, DNA recombination, maintenance of telomere integrity and meiosis. The MRN complex is involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR), an error-free mechanism which primarily occurs during S and G2 phases. The complex (1) mediates the end resection of damaged DNA, which generates proper single-stranded DNA, a key initial steps in HR, and is (2) required for the recruitment of other repair factors and efficient activation of ATM and ATR upon DNA damage.
function_by_symbol.MRTFA: MRTFA encodes myocardin-related transcription factor A. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription coactivator that associates with the serum response factor (SRF) transcription factor to control expression of genes regulating the cytoskeleton during development, morphogenesis and cell migration. The SRF-MRTFA complex activity responds to Rho GTPase-induced changes in cellular globular actin (G-actin) concentration, thereby coupling cytoskeletal gene expression to cytoskeletal dynamics. MRTFA binds G-actin via its RPEL repeats, regulating activity of the MRTFA-SRF complex.
function_by_symbol.MSH2: MSH2 encodes a DNA mismatch-recognition protein. It forms part of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR). It forms two different heterodimers: MutS alpha (MSH2-MSH6 heterodimer) and MutS beta (MSH2-MSH3 heterodimer) which binds to DNA mismatches thereby initiating DNA repair. It recruits DNA helicase MCM9 to chromatin which unwinds the mismatch containing DNA strand.
function_by_symbol.MSI1: MSI1 encodes RNA-binding protein Musashi homolog 1. Based in part on similarity, it is an RNA binding protein that regulates the expression of target mRNAs at the translation level. It regulates expression of the NOTCH1 antagonist NUMB. May play a role in the proliferation and maintenance of stem cells in the central nervous system.
function_by_symbol.MSI2: MSI2 encodes Musashi-2, an RNA-binding protein that regulates expression of target messenger RNAs at the level of translation. It may also contribute to proliferation and maintenance of nervous-system stem cells, an assignment supported in part by similarity.
