It is essential for efficient beta-selection and positive selection by promoting the ZAP70-dependent phosphorylation of the LAT signalosome during pre-TCR and TCR signaling. It plays critical roles in mast cell function by facilitating phosphorylation of SYK in Fc epsilon RI-mediated signal transduction.
function_by_symbol.RICTOR: RICTOR encodes rapamycin-insensitive companion of mTOR. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), which transduces signals from growth factors to pathways involved in proliferation, cytoskeletal organization, lipogenesis and anabolic output. The mTORC2 complex also phosphorylates various proteins involved in insulin signaling, such as FBXW8 and IGF2BP1 . mTORC2 acts upstream of Rho GTPases to regulate the actin cytoskeleton, probably by activating one or more Rho-type guanine nucleotide exchange factors . mTORC2 promotes the serum-induced formation of stress-fibers or F-actin.
function_by_symbol.RIF1: RIF1 encodes telomere-associated protein RIF1. Based in part on similarity, it is a key regulator of TP53BP1 that plays a key role in the repair of double-strand DNA breaks (DSBs) in response to DNA damage: acts by promoting non-homologous end joining (NHEJ)-mediated repair of DSBs. It is also required for immunoglobulin class-switch recombination (CSR) during antibody genesis, a process that involves the generation of DNA DSBs. It promotes NHEJ of dysfunctional telomeres.
function_by_symbol.RIMS1: RIMS1 encodes regulating synaptic membrane exocytosis 1. Based in part on similarity, it may act as scaffold protein that regulates neurotransmitter release at the active zone. It is essential for maintaining normal probability of neurotransmitter release and for regulating release during short-term synaptic plasticity. It contributes to dendrite formation by melanocytes.
function_by_symbol.RIT1: RIT1 encodes GTP-binding protein Rit1. It contributes to coupling nerve growth factor (NGF) stimulation to the activation of both EPHB2 and MAPK14 signaling pathways and in NGF-dependent neuronal differentiation. It participates in ELK1 transactivation through the Ras-MAPK signaling cascade that mediates a wide variety of cellular functions, including cell proliferation, survival, and differentiation.
function_by_symbol.RNF43: RNF43 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RNF43. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by mediating the ubiquitination, endocytosis and subsequent degradation of Wnt receptor complex components Frizzled. It acts on both canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.RNF8: RNF8 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RNF8. It is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that plays a key role in DNA damage signaling via 2 distinct roles: by mediating the 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitination of histones H2A and H2AX and promoting the recruitment of DNA repair proteins at double-strand breaks (DSBs) sites, and by catalyzing 'Lys-48'-linked ubiquitination to remove target proteins from DNA damage sites. It also controls the recruitment of UIMC1-BRCC3 (RAP80-BRCC36) and PAXIP1/PTIP to DNA damage sites. It promotes the recruitment of NBN to DNA damage sites by catalyzing 'Lys-6'-linked ubiquitination of NBN.
function_by_symbol.ROBO1: ROBO1 encodes roundabout homolog 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor for SLIT1 and SLIT2 that mediates cellular responses to molecular guidance cues in cellular migration, including axonal navigation at the ventral midline of the neural tube and projection of axons to different regions during neuronal development. It may be required for lung development.
function_by_symbol.ROS1: ROS1 encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase whose signaling can regulate cellular proliferation, survival, and differentiation. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) that plays a role in epithelial cell differentiation and regionalization of the proximal epididymal epithelium. NELL2 is an endogenous ligand for ROS1. It may activate several downstream signaling pathways related to cell differentiation, proliferation, growth and survival including the PI3 kinase-mTOR signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.RPA1: RPA1 encodes replication protein A 70 kDa DNA-binding subunit. Thereby, it plays an essential role both in DNA replication and the cellular response to DNA damage. It is required for the recruitment of the DNA double-strand break repair factors RAD51 and RAD52 to chromatin in response to DNA damage. It also recruits to sites of DNA damage proteins like XPA and XPG that are involved in nucleotide excision repair and is required for this mechanism of DNA repair.
function_by_symbol.RPL10L: RPL10L encodes ribosomal protein L10 like. Based in part on similarity, it compensates for the inactivated X-linked RPL10 paralog during spermatogenesis. The ribosome is a large ribonucleoprotein complex responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell. The male germ cell-specific ribosome displays a ribosomal polypeptide exit tunnel of distinct size and charge states compared with the classical ribosome.
function_by_symbol.RPS19: RPS19 encodes small ribosomal subunit protein eS19. It forms part of the small ribosomal subunit. The ribosome is a large ribonucleoprotein complex responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell. It is required for pre-rRNA processing and maturation of 40S ribosomal subunits.
function_by_symbol.RPS6KA4: RPS6KA4 encodes ribosomal protein S6 kinase alpha-4. It is a serine/threonine-protein kinase that is required for the mitogen or stress-induced phosphorylation of the transcription factors CREB1 and ATF1 and for the regulation of the transcription factor RELA, and that contributes to gene activation by histone phosphorylation and functions in the regulation of inflammatory genes. It phosphorylates CREB1 and ATF1 in response to mitogenic or stress stimuli such as UV-C irradiation, epidermal growth factor (EGF) and anisomycin. It contributes to the control of RELA transcriptional activity in response to TNF.
function_by_symbol.RPS6KB1: RPS6KB1 encodes ribosomal protein S6 kinase beta-1. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine-protein kinase that acts downstream of mTOR signaling in response to growth factors and nutrients to promote cell proliferation, cell growth and cell cycle progression. It regulates protein synthesis through phosphorylation of EIF4B, RPS6 and EEF2K, and contributes to cell survival by repressing the pro-apoptotic function of BAD. The active form then phosphorylates and activates several substrates in the pre-initiation complex, including the EIF2B complex and the cap-binding complex component EIF4B.
function_by_symbol.RPS6KB2: RPS6KB2 encodes ribosomal protein S6 kinase beta-2. It phosphorylates specifically ribosomal protein S6. It seems to act downstream of mTOR signaling in response to growth factors and nutrients to promote cell proliferation, cell growth and cell cycle progression in an alternative pathway regulated by MEAK7.
function_by_symbol.RPTOR: RPTOR encodes regulatory-associated protein of mTOR (p150 target of rapamycin (TOR)-scaffold protein). Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), an evolutionarily conserved central nutrient sensor that stimulates anabolic reactions and macromolecule biosynthesis to promote cellular biomass generation and growth. The mTORC1 complex is inhibited in response to starvation and amino acid depletion.
function_by_symbol.RRAGC: RRAGC encodes ras-related GTP-binding protein C. It is a guanine nucleotide-binding protein that plays a crucial role in the cellular response to amino acid availability through regulation of the mTORC1 signaling cascade. It forms heterodimeric Rag complexes with RagA/RRAGA or RagB/RRAGB and cycles between an inactive GTP-bound and an active GDP-bound form: RagC/RRAGC is in its active form when GDP-bound RagC/RRAGC forms a complex with GTP-bound RagA/RRAGA (or RagB/RRAGB) and in an inactive form when GTP-bound RagC/RRAGC heterodimerizes with GDP-bound RagA/RRAGA (or RagB/RRAGB). This is a crucial step in the activation of the MTOR signaling cascade by amino acids.
function_by_symbol.RSPO2: RSPO2 encodes r-spondin-2. It is an activator of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway by acting as a ligand for LGR4-6 receptors. It also regulates the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent pathway and non-canonical Wnt signaling by acting as an inhibitor of ZNRF3, an important regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.RSPO3: RSPO3 encodes r-spondin-3. Based in part on similarity, it is an activator of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway by acting as a ligand for LGR4-6 receptors, which acts as a key regulator of angiogenesis. It also regulates the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent pathway and non-canonical Wnt signaling by acting as an inhibitor of ZNRF3, an important regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway. It functions as a ligand for frizzled FZD8 and LRP6.
function_by_symbol.RTEL1: RTEL1 encodes regulator of telomere elongation helicase 1. It functions as an anti-recombinase to counteract toxic recombination and limit crossover during meiosis. It regulates meiotic recombination and crossover homeostasis by physically dissociating strand invasion events and thereby promotes noncrossover repair by meiotic synthesis dependent strand annealing (SDSA) as well as disassembly of D loop recombination intermediates. It also disassembles T loops and prevents telomere fragility by counteracting telomeric G4-DNA structures, which together ensure the dynamics and stability of the telomere.
function_by_symbol.RUNX1: RUNX1 encodes a DNA-binding transcription factor that forms the core-binding factor complex with CBFB and regulates hematopoietic development and differentiation. Based in part on similarity, it forms the heterodimeric complex core-binding factor (CBF) with CBFB. It is essential for the development of normal hematopoiesis. It acts synergistically with ELF4 to transactivate the IL-3 promoter and with ELF2 to transactivate the BLK promoter.
function_by_symbol.RXRA: RXRA encodes retinoic acid receptor RXR-alpha. It is a receptor for retinoic acid that acts as a transcription factor. It forms homo- or heterodimers with retinoic acid receptors (RARs) and binds to target response elements in response to their ligands, all-trans or 9-cis retinoic acid, to regulate gene expression in various biological processes. The RAR/RXR heterodimers bind to the retinoic acid response elements (RARE) composed of tandem 5'-AGGTCA-3' sites known as DR1-DR5 to regulate transcription.
function_by_symbol.RYBP: RYBP encodes RING1 and YY1-binding protein. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of a Polycomb group (PcG) multiprotein PRC1-like complex, a complex class required to maintain the transcriptionally repressive state of many genes, including Hox genes, throughout development. It forms part of a PRC1-like complex that mediates monoubiquitination of histone H2A 'Lys-119' on the X chromosome and is required for normal silencing of one copy of the X chromosome in XX females. It may stimulate ubiquitination of histone H2A 'Lys-119' by recruiting the complex to target sites.
function_by_symbol.S100A3: S100A3 encodes S100 calcium binding protein A3. It binds both calcium and zinc. It may participate in calcium-dependent cuticle cell differentiation, hair shaft and hair cuticular barrier formation.
function_by_symbol.S100A8: S100A8 encodes S100 calcium binding protein A8. S100A8 is a calcium- and zinc-binding protein which plays a prominent role in the regulation of inflammatory processes and immune response. It can induce neutrophil chemotaxis and adhesion. The intracellular functions include: facilitating leukocyte arachidonic acid trafficking and metabolism, modulation of the tubulin-dependent cytoskeleton during migration of phagocytes and activation of the neutrophilic NADPH-oxidase.
function_by_symbol.SAMD9: SAMD9 encodes sterile alpha motif domain-containing protein 9. It is a double-stranded nucleic acid binding that acts as an antiviral factor by playing an essential role in the formation of cytoplasmic antiviral granules. May play a role in the inflammatory response to tissue injury and the control of extra-osseous calcification, acting as a downstream target of TNF signaling. It participates in the regulation of EGR1, in coordination with RGL2.
function_by_symbol.SAMD9L: SAMD9L encodes a SAM-domain-containing protein implicated in regulation of cellular growth and hematopoietic homeostasis. Based in part on similarity, it may participate in endosome fusion. It mediates down-regulation of growth factor signaling via internalization of growth factor receptors.
function_by_symbol.SAMHD1: SAMHD1 encodes deoxynucleoside triphosphate triphosphohydrolase SAMHD1. Based in part on similarity, it functions during S phase at stalled DNA replication forks to promote the resection of gapped or reversed forks: acts by stimulating the exonuclease activity of MRE11, activating the ATR-CHK1 pathway and allowing the forks to restart replication. Its ability to promote degradation of nascent DNA at stalled replication forks is required to prevent induction of type I interferons, thereby preventing chronic inflammation.
function_by_symbol.SBDS: SBDS encodes ribosome maturation protein SBDS. It is required for the assembly of mature ribosomes and ribosome biogenesis. It is required for normal levels of protein synthesis. May play a role in cellular response to DNA damage.
function_by_symbol.SCG5: SCG5 encodes neuroendocrine protein 7B2. It functions as a molecular chaperone for PCSK2/PC2, preventing its premature activation in the regulated secretory pathway. It binds to inactive PCSK2 in the endoplasmic reticulum and facilitates its transport from there to later compartments of the secretory pathway where it is proteolytically matured and activated. It contributes to regulating pituitary hormone secretion.
function_by_symbol.SDHAF2: SDHAF2 encodes succinate dehydrogenase assembly factor 2, mitochondrial. It contributes to the assembly of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH), an enzyme complex (also referred to as respiratory complex II) that is a component of both the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and the mitochondrial electron transport chain, and which couples the oxidation of succinate to fumarate with the reduction of ubiquinone (coenzyme Q) to ubiquinol. It is required for flavinylation (covalent attachment of FAD) of the flavoprotein subunit SDHA of the SDH catalytic dimer.
function_by_symbol.SDHB: SDHB encodes succinate dehydrogenase complex iron sulfur subunit B. Based in part on similarity, it is an iron-sulfur protein (IP) subunit of the succinate dehydrogenase complex (mitochondrial respiratory chain complex II), responsible for transferring electrons from succinate to ubiquinone (coenzyme Q).
function_by_symbol.SEMA4B: SEMA4B encodes semaphorin 4B. Based in part on similarity, it inhibits axonal extension by providing local signals to specify territories inaccessible for growing axons.
function_by_symbol.SERP2: SERP2 encodes stress-associated endoplasmic reticulum protein 2. Based in part on similarity, it interacts with target proteins during their translocation into the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum. It protects unfolded target proteins against degradation during ER stress. It may facilitate glycosylation of target proteins after termination of ER stress.
function_by_symbol.SERPINA1: SERPINA1 encodes alpha-1-antitrypsin. Its primary target is elastase, but it also has a moderate affinity for plasmin and thrombin. Its major physiological function is the protection of the lower respiratory tract against proteolytic destruction by human leukocyte elastase (HLE).
function_by_symbol.SERPINE1: SERPINE1 encodes plasminogen activator inhibitor 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a primary inhibitor of tissue-type plasminogen activator (PLAT) and urokinase-type plasminogen activator (PLAU). It functions as a regulator of cell migration, independently of its role as protease inhibitor. It is required for stimulation of keratinocyte migration during cutaneous injury repair.
function_by_symbol.SESN1: SESN1 encodes sestrin-1. Based in part on similarity, it acts as an intracellular leucine sensor that negatively regulates the TORC1 signaling pathway through the GATOR complex. This stress-inducible metabolic regulator may also play a role in protection against oxidative and genotoxic stresses. It may positively regulate the transcription by NFE2L2 of genes involved in the response to oxidative stress by facilitating the SQSTM1-mediated autophagic degradation of KEAP1.
function_by_symbol.SESN2: SESN2 encodes sestrin-2. It acts as an intracellular leucine sensor that negatively regulates the mTORC1 signaling pathway through the GATOR complex. This stress-inducible metabolic regulator also plays a role in protection against oxidative and genotoxic stresses. It may negatively regulate protein translation in response to endoplasmic reticulum stress, via mTORC1.
function_by_symbol.SESN3: SESN3 encodes sestrin-3. Based in part on similarity, it may function as an intracellular leucine sensor that negatively regulates the TORC1 signaling pathway. It may also regulate the insulin-receptor signaling pathway through activation of TORC2. This metabolic regulator may also play a role in protection against oxidative and genotoxic stresses.
function_by_symbol.SETBP1: SETBP1 encodes a protein with a SET-binding region, a SKI-homology region, and nuclear-localization signals. It binds the SET protein, which participates in DNA replication. Its protein interactions and nuclear targeting provide functional context, while the cited description does not establish SETBP1 as an independently acting DNA-replication enzyme.
function_by_symbol.SETD1A: SETD1A encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD1A. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism. It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery, forms H3K4me1, H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It is required for H3K4me1 mark at stalled replication forks.
function_by_symbol.SETD1B: SETD1B encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD1B. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism. It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery, forms H3K4me1, H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It contributes to regulating the transcriptional programming of multipotent hematopoietic progenitor cells and lymphoid lineage specification during hematopoiesis.
function_by_symbol.SETD2: SETD2 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD2. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that specifically trimethylates 'Lys-36' of histone H3 (H3K36me3) using dimethylated 'Lys-36' (H3K36me2) as substrate. It represents the main enzyme generating H3K36me3, a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional activation. It contributes to chromatin structure modulation during elongation by coordinating recruitment of the FACT complex and by interacting with hyperphosphorylated POLR2A.
function_by_symbol.SETD3: SETD3 encodes actin-histidine N-methyltransferase. It is a protein-histidine N-methyltransferase that specifically mediates 3-methylhistidine (tele-methylhistidine) methylation of actin at 'His-73'. Histidine methylation of actin is required for smooth muscle contraction of the laboring uterus during delivery. It does not have protein-lysine N-methyltransferase activity and probably only catalyzes histidine methylation of actin.
function_by_symbol.SETD4: SETD4 encodes SET domain-containing protein 4. Based in part on similarity, it is a protein-lysine N-methyltransferase that methylates both histones and non-histone proteins. Via its catalytic activity, regulates many processes, including cell proliferation, cell differentiation, inflammatory response and apoptosis. It regulates the inflammatory response by mediating mono- and dimethylation of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4me1 and H3K4me2, respectively), leading to activate the transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNF.
function_by_symbol.SETD5: SETD5 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD5. Based in part on similarity, it is a chromatin regulator required for brain development: acts as a regulator of RNA elongation rate, thereby regulating neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and synaptic transmission. It may act by mediating trimethylation of 'Lys-36' of histone H3 (H3K36me3), which is essential to allow on-time RNA elongation dynamics.
function_by_symbol.SETD6: SETD6 encodes n-lysine methyltransferase SETD6. Based in part on similarity, it monomethylates 'Lys-310' of the RELA subunit of NF-kappa-B complex, leading to down-regulation of NF-kappa-B transcription factor activity. It monomethylates 'Lys-8' of H2AZ (H2AZK8me1). It is required for the maintenance of embryonic stem cell self-renewal.
function_by_symbol.SETD7: SETD7 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD7. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that specifically monomethylates 'Lys-4' of histone H3. H3 'Lys-4' methylation represents a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional activation. It plays a central role in the transcriptional activation of genes such as collagenase or insulin.
function_by_symbol.SETDB1: SETDB1 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETDB1. It is a histone methyltransferase that specifically trimethylates 'Lys-9' of histone H3 (H3K9me3). H3 'Lys-9' trimethylation represents a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression by recruiting HP1 (CBX1, CBX3 and/or CBX5) proteins to methylated histones. H3 'Lys-9' trimethylation is coordinated with DNA methylation.
function_by_symbol.SETDB2: SETDB2 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETDB2. It is a histone methyltransferase involved in left-right axis specification in early development and mitosis. It specifically trimethylates 'Lys-9' of histone H3 (H3K9me3). H3K9me3 is a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression that recruits HP1 (CBX1, CBX3 and/or CBX5) proteins to methylated histones.
function_by_symbol.SF3B1: SF3B1 encodes a component of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein complex that participates in branch-point recognition during pre-mRNA splicing. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the 17S U2 SnRNP complex of the spliceosome, a large ribonucleoprotein complex that removes introns from transcribed pre-mRNAs. The 17S U2 SnRNP complex (1) directly participates in early spliceosome assembly and (2) mediates recognition of the intron branch site during pre-mRNA splicing by promoting the selection of the pre-mRNA branch-site adenosine, the nucleophile for the first step of splicing. Sequence independent binding of SF3A and SF3B subcomplexes upstream of the branch site is essential, it may anchor U2 snRNP to the pre-mRNA.
function_by_symbol.SFPQ: SFPQ encodes splicing factor, proline- and glutamine-rich. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA- and RNA binding protein, involved in several nuclear processes. It is an essential pre-mRNA splicing factor required early in spliceosome formation and for splicing catalytic step II, probably as a heteromer with NONO. It binds to pre-mRNA in spliceosome C complex, and specifically binds to intronic polypyrimidine tracts.
function_by_symbol.SGK1: SGK1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase Sgk1. It is a serine/threonine-protein kinase which is involved in the regulation of a wide variety of ion channels, membrane transporters, cellular enzymes, transcription factors, neuronal excitability, cell growth, proliferation, survival, migration and apoptosis. It contributes to cellular stress response. It contributes to regulation of renal Na(+) retention, renal K(+) elimination, salt appetite, gastric acid secretion, intestinal Na(+)/H(+) exchange and nutrient transport, insulin-dependent salt sensitivity of blood pressure, salt sensitivity of peripheral glucose uptake, cardiac repolarization and memory consolidation.
function_by_symbol.SH2D1A: SH2D1A encodes SH2 domain-containing protein 1A. Based in part on similarity, it is a cytoplasmic adapter regulating receptors of the signaling lymphocytic activation molecule (SLAM) family such as SLAMF1, CD244, LY9, CD84, SLAMF6 and SLAMF7. Initially it has been proposed that association with SLAMF1 prevents SLAMF1 binding to inhibitory effectors including INPP5D/SHIP1 and PTPN11/SHP-2. It positively regulates CD244/2B4- and CD84-mediated natural killer (NK) cell functions.
function_by_symbol.SHB: SHB encodes SH2 domain containing adaptor protein B. It is an adapter protein which regulates several signal transduction cascades by linking activated receptors to downstream signaling components. May play a role in angiogenesis by regulating FGFR1, VEGFR2 and PDGFR signaling. May also play a role in T-cell antigen receptor/TCR signaling, interleukin-2 signaling, apoptosis and neuronal cells differentiation by mediating basic-FGF and NGF-induced signaling cascades.
function_by_symbol.SHH: SHH encodes sonic hedgehog protein. Based in part on similarity, the C-terminal part of the precursor displays an autoproteolysis and a cholesterol transferase activity, resulting (1) in the cleavage of the full-length protein into two parts, Sonic hedgehog protein N-product and C-product (ShhN and ShhC, respectively) and (2) covalent attachment of a cholesterol moiety to the C-terminus of the newly generated ShhN. It acts by binding to the patched receptor (PTCH1 or PTCH2), relieving smoothened (SMO) inhibition by patched, activating the smoothened signaling pathway and transcription of target genes. ShhN is widely expressed and plays a key role in the patterning of the central nervous system and limb development.
function_by_symbol.SHOC2: SHOC2 encodes leucine-rich repeat protein SHOC-2. It is a core component of the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1c (SMP) holophosphatase complex that regulates activation of the MAPK pathway. It functions as a scaffolding protein in the SMP complex. The SMP complex specifically dephosphorylates the inhibitory phosphorylation at 'Ser-259' of RAF1 kinase, 'Ser-365' of BRAF kinase and 'Ser-214' of ARAF kinase, stimulating their kinase activities.
function_by_symbol.SHQ1: SHQ1 encodes protein SHQ1 homolog. It is required for the quantitative accumulation of H/ACA ribonucleoproteins (RNPs), including telomerase, probably through the stabilization of DKC1, from the time of its synthesis until its association with NOP10, NHP2, and NAF1 at the nascent H/ACA RNA.
function_by_symbol.SIX1: SIX1 encodes homeobox protein SIX1. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that is involved in the regulation of cell proliferation, apoptosis and embryonic development. It contributes to the development of several organs, including kidney, muscle and inner ear. It lacks an activation domain, and requires interaction with EYA family members for transcription activation.
function_by_symbol.SIX2: SIX2 encodes homeobox protein SIX2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that plays an important role in the development of several organs, including kidney, skull and stomach. It acts through its interaction with TCF7L2 and OSR1 in a canonical Wnt signaling independent manner preventing transcription of differentiation genes in cap mesenchyme such as WNT4. It also acts independently of OSR1 to activate expression of many cap mesenchyme genes, including itself, GDNF and OSR1.
function_by_symbol.SLAMF1: SLAMF1 encodes signaling lymphocytic activation molecule. Based in part on similarity, activities are controlled by presence or absence of small cytoplasmic adapter proteins, SH2D1A/SAP and/or SH2D1B/EAT-2. SLAMF1-induced signal-transduction events in T-lymphocytes are different from those in B-cells. Initially it has been proposed that association with SH2D1A prevents binding to inhibitory effectors including INPP5D/SHIP1 and PTPN11/SHP-2.
function_by_symbol.SLC25A13: SLC25A13 encodes electrogenic aspartate/glutamate antiporter SLC25A13, mitochondrial. It is a mitochondrial electrogenic aspartate/glutamate antiporter that favors efflux of aspartate and entry of glutamate and proton within the mitochondria as part of the malate-aspartate shuttle. Substrate exchange across the membrane occurs consecutively with one substrate being transported first, then dissociating from the substrate binding site before the second substrate binds for transport in the opposite direction. It also mediates the uptake of L-cysteinesulfinate (3-sulfino-L-alanine) by mitochondria in exchange for L-glutamate and proton.
function_by_symbol.SLC27A5: SLC27A5 encodes solute carrier family 27 member 5. Based in part on similarity, it may mediate the import of long-chain fatty acids (LCFA) by facilitating their transport across cell membranes. It also catalyzes the ATP-dependent formation of fatty acyl-CoA using LCFA and very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFA) as substrates.
function_by_symbol.SLC3A2: SLC3A2 encodes amino acid transporter heavy chain SLC3A2. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a chaperone that facilitates biogenesis and trafficking of functional transporter heterodimers to the plasma membrane. It forms heterodimers with SLC7 family transporters (SLC7A5, SLC7A6, SLC7A7, SLC7A8, SLC7A10 and SLC7A11), a group of amino-acid antiporters.
function_by_symbol.SLC44A1: SLC44A1 encodes choline transporter-like protein 1. It also acts as a high-affinity ethanolamine/H+ antiporter, regulating the supply of extracellular ethanolamine (Etn) for the CDP-Etn pathway, redistribute intracellular Etn and balance the CDP-Cho and CDP-Etn arms of the Kennedy pathway. It participates in membrane synthesis and myelin production.
function_by_symbol.SLC4A11: SLC4A11 encodes solute carrier family 4 member 11. Based in part on similarity, it regulates the oxidative stress response in corneal endothelium by enhancing antioxidant defenses and protecting cells from reactive oxygen species.
function_by_symbol.SLFN11: SLFN11 encodes schlafen family member 11. It is an inhibitor of DNA replication that promotes cell death in response to DNA damage. It functions as a guardian of the genome by killing cells with defective replication. A single tRNA molecule is bound and cleaved by the SLFN11 dimer.
function_by_symbol.SLIT2: SLIT2 encodes slit homolog 2 protein. It may be implicated in spinal cord midline post-crossing axon repulsion. It seems to play a role in branching and arborization of CNS sensory axons, and in neuronal cell migration. It seems to be involved in regulating leukocyte migration.
function_by_symbol.SLMAP: SLMAP encodes sarcolemmal membrane-associated protein. Based in part on similarity, it associates with the striatin-interacting phosphatase and kinase (STRIPAK) core complex, forming the extended (SIKE1:SLMAP)STRIPAK complex. The (SIKE1:SLMAP)STRIPAK complex dephosphorylates STK3 leading to the inhibition of Hippo signaling and the control of cell growth. May play a role during myoblast fusion.
function_by_symbol.SLX1A: SLX1A encodes structure-specific endonuclease subunit SLX1. It is a catalytic subunit of the SLX1-SLX4 structure-specific endonuclease that resolves DNA secondary structures generated during DNA repair and recombination. It has endonuclease activity towards branched DNA substrates, introducing single-strand cuts in duplex DNA close to junctions with ss-DNA. It has a preference for 5'-flap structures, and promotes symmetrical cleavage of static and migrating Holliday junctions (HJs).
function_by_symbol.SLX1B: SLX1B encodes structure-specific endonuclease subunit SLX1. It is a catalytic subunit of the SLX1-SLX4 structure-specific endonuclease that resolves DNA secondary structures generated during DNA repair and recombination. It has endonuclease activity towards branched DNA substrates, introducing single-strand cuts in duplex DNA close to junctions with ss-DNA. It has a preference for 5'-flap structures, and promotes symmetrical cleavage of static and migrating Holliday junctions (HJs).
function_by_symbol.SLX4: SLX4 encodes structure-specific endonuclease subunit SLX4. It has several distinct roles in protecting genome stability by resolving diverse forms of deleterious DNA structures originating from replication and recombination intermediates and from DNA damage. It forms part of the SLX1-SLX4 structure-specific endonuclease that resolves DNA secondary structures generated during DNA repair and recombination. It has endonuclease activity towards branched DNA substrates, introducing single-strand cuts in duplex DNA close to junctions with ss-DNA.
function_by_symbol.SMAD2: SMAD2 encodes SMAD family member 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor-regulated SMAD (R-SMAD) that is an intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) and activin type 1 receptor kinases. It binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD2/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription. It promotes TGFB1-mediated transcription of odontoblastic differentiation genes in dental papilla cells.
function_by_symbol.SMAD3: SMAD3 encodes SMAD family member 3. It is a receptor-regulated SMAD (R-SMAD) that is an intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) and activin type 1 receptor kinases. It binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD3/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription. It also can form a SMAD3/SMAD4/JUN/FOS complex at the AP-1/SMAD site to regulate TGF-beta-mediated transcription.
function_by_symbol.SMARCA1: SMARCA1 encodes SWI/SNF-related matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily A member 1. ATPase activity is substrate-dependent, and is increased when nucleosomes are the substrate, but is also catalytically active when DNA alone is the substrate. It is a catalytic subunit of ISWI chromatin-remodeling complexes, which form ordered nucleosome arrays on chromatin and facilitate access to DNA during DNA-templated processes such as DNA replication, transcription, and repair. Catalytic activity and histone octamer sliding propensity is regulated and determined by components of the ISWI chromatin-remodeling complexes.
function_by_symbol.SMARCA2: SMARCA2 encodes SWI/SNF-related matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily A member 2. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes that carry out key enzymatic activities, changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner. It belongs to the neural progenitors-specific chromatin remodeling complex (npBAF complex) and the neuron-specific chromatin remodeling complex (nBAF complex). The transition from proliferating neural stem/progenitor cells to postmitotic neurons requires a switch in subunit composition of the npBAF and nBAF complexes.
function_by_symbol.SMARCC1: SMARCC1 encodes SWI/SNF complex subunit SMARCC1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology). It forms part of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes that carry out key enzymatic activities, changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner. It may stimulate the ATPase activity of the catalytic subunit of the complex.
function_by_symbol.SMARCC2: SMARCC2 encodes SWI/SNF complex subunit SMARCC2. Based in part on similarity, it participates in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology). It forms part of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes that carry out key enzymatic activities, changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner. It can stimulate the ATPase activity of the catalytic subunit of these complexes.
function_by_symbol.SMARCD1: SMARCD1 encodes SWI/SNF-related matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily D member 1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology). It forms part of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes that carry out key enzymatic activities, changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner. It belongs to the neural progenitors-specific chromatin remodeling complex (npBAF complex) and the neuron-specific chromatin remodeling complex (nBAF complex).
function_by_symbol.SMARCE1: SMARCE1 encodes SWI/SNF-related matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily E member 1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology). It forms part of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes that carry out key enzymatic activities, changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner. It belongs to the neural progenitors-specific chromatin remodeling complex (npBAF complex) and the neuron-specific chromatin remodeling complex (nBAF complex).
function_by_symbol.SMC1A: SMC1A encodes structural maintenance of chromosomes protein 1A. It participates in chromosome cohesion during cell cycle and in DNA repair. The cohesin complex is required for the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA replication. The cohesin complex apparently forms a large proteinaceous ring within which sister chromatids can be trapped.
function_by_symbol.SMC3: SMC3 encodes structural maintenance of chromosomes protein 3. The cohesin complex may form a large proteinaceous ring within which sister chromatids can be trapped. At anaphase, the complex is cleaved and dissociates from chromatin, allowing sister chromatids to segregate. Cohesion is coupled to DNA replication and is involved in DNA repair.
function_by_symbol.SMG1: SMG1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase SMG1. It is a serine/threonine protein kinase involved in both mRNA surveillance and genotoxic stress response pathways. It plays a central role in nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of mRNAs containing premature stop codons by phosphorylating UPF1/RENT1. It also acts as a genotoxic stress-activated protein kinase that displays some functional overlap with ATM.
function_by_symbol.SND1: SND1 encodes staphylococcal nuclease domain-containing protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a bridging factor between STAT6 and the basal transcription factor. It contributes to PIM1 regulation of MYB activity. It acts as a transcriptional coactivator for STAT5.
function_by_symbol.SNRPD3: SNRPD3 encodes small nuclear ribonucleoprotein D3 polypeptide. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to pre-mRNA splicing as a core component of the spliceosomal U1, U2, U4 and U5 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs), the building blocks of the spliceosome. It forms part of both the pre-catalytic spliceosome B complex and activated spliceosome C complexes.
function_by_symbol.SOCS2: SOCS2 encodes suppressor of cytokine signaling 2. It is a substrate-recognition component of a cullin-5-RING E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex (ECS complex, also named CRL5 complex), which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins, such as EPOR and GHR. It specifically recognizes and binds phosphorylated proteins via its SH2 domain, promoting their ubiquitination. The ECS(SOCS2) complex acts as a key regulator of growth hormone receptor (GHR) levels by mediating ubiquitination and degradation of GHR, following GHR phosphorylation by JAK2.
function_by_symbol.SOCS3: SOCS3 encodes suppressor of cytokine signaling 3. Based in part on similarity, SOCS family proteins form part of a classical negative feedback system that regulates cytokine signal transduction. SOCS3 is involved in negative regulation of cytokines that signal through the JAK/STAT pathway. It inhibits signal transduction by binding to transmembrane signaling receptors including IL6ST/gp130, LIFR, EPOR, INSR, IL12RB2, CSF3R/G-CSF-R and LEPR.
function_by_symbol.SOS1: SOS1 encodes a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor that promotes replacement of RAS-bound GDP with GTP. This exchange favors RAS activation and connects extracellular signaling with the MAPK pathway. SOS1 interacts with adaptor proteins such as GRB2, providing a route for coupling receptor-associated signaling assemblies to the nucleotide state of RAS.
function_by_symbol.SOX10: SOX10 encodes transcription factor SOX-10. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that plays a central role in developing and mature glia. It specifically activates expression of myelin genes, during oligodendrocyte (OL) maturation, such as DUSP15 and MYRF, thereby playing a central role in oligodendrocyte maturation and CNS myelination.
function_by_symbol.SOX11: SOX11 encodes transcription factor SOX-11. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that acts as a transcriptional activator. It binds cooperatively with POU3F2/BRN2 or POU3F1/OCT6 to gene promoters, which enhances transcriptional activation. It functions as a transcriptional activator of TEAD2 by binding to its gene promoter and first intron.
function_by_symbol.SOX2: SOX2 encodes transcription factor SOX-2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that forms a trimeric complex with OCT4 on DNA and controls the expression of a number of genes involved in embryonic development such as YES1, FGF4, UTF1 and ZFP206. It binds to the proximal enhancer region of NANOG. It keeps neural cells undifferentiated by counteracting the activity of proneural proteins and suppresses neuronal differentiation.
function_by_symbol.SOX9: SOX9 encodes transcription factor SOX-9. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that plays a key role in chondrocytes differentiation and skeletal development. It specifically binds the 5'-ACAAAG-3' DNA motif present in enhancers and super-enhancers and promotes expression of genes important for chondrogenesis, including cartilage matrix protein-coding genes COL2A1, COL4A2, COL9A1, COL11A2 and ACAN, SOX5 and SOX6. It also binds to some promoter regions.
function_by_symbol.SPEN: SPEN encodes msx2-interacting protein. Based in part on similarity, may serve as a nuclear matrix platform that organizes and integrates transcriptional responses. It has also been shown to be an essential corepressor protein, which probably regulates different key pathways such as the Notch pathway. It blocks the differentiation of precursor B-cells into marginal zone B-cells.
function_by_symbol.SPI1: SPI1 encodes transcription factor PU.1. Based in part on similarity, FCER1A transactivation is achieved in cooperation with GATA1.
function_by_symbol.SPRTN: SPRTN encodes DNA-dependent metalloprotease SPRTN. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA-dependent metalloendopeptidase that mediates the proteolytic cleavage of covalent DNA-protein cross-links (DPCs) during DNA synthesis and mitosis, thereby playing a key role in maintaining genomic integrity. DPCs are highly toxic DNA lesions that interfere with essential chromatin transactions, such as replication and transcription, and which are induced by reactive agents, such as UV light or formaldehyde. It associates with the DNA replication machinery and specifically removes DPCs during DNA synthesis.
function_by_symbol.SRC: SRC encodes proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase which is activated following engagement of many different classes of cellular receptors including immune response receptors, integrins and other adhesion receptors, receptor protein tyrosine kinases, G protein-coupled receptors as well as cytokine receptors. It participates in signaling pathways that control a diverse spectrum of biological activities including gene transcription, immune response, cell adhesion, cell cycle progression, apoptosis, migration, and transformation. Receptor clustering or dimerization leads to recruitment of SRC to the receptor complexes where it phosphorylates the tyrosine residues within the receptor cytoplasmic domains.
function_by_symbol.SRCAP: SRCAP encodes chromatin remodeling protein SRCAP. It acts both as a chromatin remodeler and transcription coregulator. It is the catalytic component of the SRCAP complex which mediates the ATP-dependent exchange of histone H2AZ/H2B dimers for nucleosomal H2A/H2B, leading to transcriptional regulation of selected genes expression through chromatin remodeling. It functions as a coactivator for CREB-mediated transcription, steroid receptor-mediated transcription, and Notch-mediated transcription.
function_by_symbol.SRF: SRF encodes serum response factor. Based in part on similarity, SRF is a transcription factor that binds to the serum response element (SRE), a short sequence of dyad symmetry located 300 bp to the 5' of the site of transcription initiation of some genes (such as FOS). The SRF-MRTFA complex activity responds to Rho GTPase-induced changes in cellular globular actin (G-actin) concentration, thereby coupling cytoskeletal gene expression to cytoskeletal dynamics. It is required for cardiac differentiation and maturation.
function_by_symbol.SRP19: SRP19 encodes signal recognition particle 19 kDa protein. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the signal recognition particle (SRP) complex, a ribonucleoprotein complex that mediates the cotranslational targeting of secretory and membrane proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). It binds directly to 7SL RNA. It mediates binding of SRP54 to the SRP complex.
function_by_symbol.SRP54: SRP54 encodes signal recognition particle subunit SRP54. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the signal recognition particle (SRP) complex, a ribonucleoprotein complex that mediates the cotranslational targeting of secretory and membrane proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). It binds to the signal sequence of presecretory proteins when they emerge from the ribosomes. It displays basal GTPase activity, and stimulates reciprocal GTPase activation of the SR subunit SRPRA.
function_by_symbol.SRP72: SRP72 encodes signal recognition particle subunit SRP72. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the signal recognition particle (SRP) complex, a ribonucleoprotein complex that mediates the cotranslational targeting of secretory and membrane proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The SRP complex interacts with the signal sequence in nascent secretory and membrane proteins and directs them to the membrane of the ER. The SRP complex targets the ribosome-nascent chain complex to the SRP receptor (SR), which is anchored in the ER, where SR compaction and GTPase rearrangement drive cotranslational protein translocation into the ER.
function_by_symbol.SRSF2: SRSF2 encodes a serine/arginine-rich RNA-binding splicing factor that regulates splice-site selection and processing of pre-mRNA. It is necessary for the splicing of pre-mRNA. It is required for formation of the earliest ATP-dependent splicing complex and interacts with spliceosomal components bound to both the 5'- and 3'-splice sites during spliceosome assembly. It also is required for ATP-dependent interactions of both U1 and U2 snRNPs with pre-mRNA.
function_by_symbol.SRY: SRY encodes sex-determining region Y protein. Based in part on similarity, it is necessary and sufficient for initiating male sex determination by directing the development of supporting cell precursors (pre-Sertoli cells) as Sertoli rather than granulosa cells. It participates in different aspects of gene regulation including promoter activation or repression.
function_by_symbol.SS18: SS18 encodes protein SSXT. It appears to function synergistically with RBM14 as a transcriptional coactivator. It forms part of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling subcomplex GBAF that carries out key enzymatic activities, changing chromatin structure by altering DNA-histone contacts within a nucleosome in an ATP-dependent manner.
function_by_symbol.SS18L1: SS18L1 encodes calcium-responsive transactivator. Based in part on similarity, it recruits CREB-binding protein (CREBBP) to nuclear bodies. It forms part of the CREST-BRG1 complex, a multiprotein complex that regulates promoter activation by orchestrating a calcium-dependent release of a repressor complex and a recruitment of an activator complex.
function_by_symbol.SSBP3: SSBP3 encodes single stranded DNA binding protein 3. Based in part on similarity, it may participate in transcription regulation of the alpha 2(I) collagen gene where it binds to the single-stranded polypyrimidine sequences in the promoter region.
function_by_symbol.STAG1: STAG1 encodes cohesin subunit SA-1. It forms part of cohesin complex, a complex required for the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA replication. The cohesin complex apparently forms a large proteinaceous ring within which sister chromatids can be trapped. At anaphase, the complex is cleaved and dissociates from chromatin, allowing sister chromatids to segregate.
function_by_symbol.STAG2: STAG2 encodes cohesin subunit SA-2. It forms part of cohesin complex, a complex required for the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA replication. The cohesin complex apparently forms a large proteinaceous ring within which sister chromatids can be trapped. At anaphase, the complex is cleaved and dissociates from chromatin, allowing sister chromatids to segregate.
function_by_symbol.STAT3: STAT3 encodes signal transducer and activator of transcription 3. Based in part on similarity, it may mediate cellular responses to activated FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3 and FGFR4. It functions as a regulator of inflammatory response by regulating differentiation of naive CD4(+) T-cells into T-helper Th17 or regulatory T-cells (Treg): acetylation promotes its transcription activity and cell differentiation while deacetylation and oxidation of lysine residues by LOXL3 inhibits differentiation. It participates in cell cycle regulation by inducing the expression of key genes for the progression from G1 to S phase, such as CCND1.
function_by_symbol.STAT4: STAT4 encodes signal transducer and activator of transcription 4. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the differentiation of T-helper 1 cells and the production of interferon-gamma. It also participates in multiple neutrophil functions including chemotaxis and production of the neutrophil extracellular traps. Transcription activation of IFN-gamma gene is mediated by interaction with JUN that forms a complex that efficiently interacts with the AP-1-related sequence of the IFN-gamma promoter.
function_by_symbol.STIL: STIL encodes SCL-interrupting locus protein. It plays a role as a positive regulator of the sonic hedgehog pathway, acting downstream of PTCH1. It contributes to the regulation of centriole duplication. It is required for the onset of procentriole formation and proper mitotic progression.
function_by_symbol.STRN: STRN encodes striatin. STRIPAK complexes have critical roles in protein (de)phosphorylation and are regulators of multiple signaling pathways including Hippo, MAPK, nuclear receptor and cytoskeleton remodeling.
function_by_symbol.SUFU: SUFU encodes suppressor of fused homolog. Based in part on similarity, it may also act as a negative regulator of beta-catenin signaling. It is required for normal embryonic development. It is required for the proper formation of hair follicles and the control of epidermal differentiation.
function_by_symbol.SUZ12: SUZ12 encodes polycomb protein SUZ12. It forms part of the PRC2 complex, which methylates 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27me) of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. The PRC2 complex may also serve as a recruiting platform for DNA methyltransferases, thereby linking two epigenetic repression systems.
function_by_symbol.SYK: SYK encodes tyrosine-protein kinase SYK. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase which mediates signal transduction downstream of a variety of transmembrane receptors including classical immunoreceptors like the B-cell receptor (BCR). It regulates several biological processes including innate and adaptive immunity, cell adhesion, osteoclast maturation, platelet activation and vascular development. It assembles into signaling complexes with activated receptors at the plasma membrane via interaction between its SH2 domains and the receptor tyrosine-phosphorylated ITAM domains.
function_by_symbol.TACC1: TACC1 encodes transforming acidic coiled-coil-containing protein 1. It participates in transcription regulation induced by nuclear receptors, including in T3 thyroid hormone and all-trans retinoic acid pathways. It likely involved in the processes that promote cell division prior to the formation of differentiated tissues.
function_by_symbol.TACC3: TACC3 encodes transforming acidic coiled-coil-containing protein 3. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the microtubule-dependent coupling of the nucleus and the centrosome. It participates in the processes that regulate centrosome-mediated interkinetic nuclear migration (INM) of neural progenitors. It functions as a component of the TACC3/ch-TOG/clathrin complex proposed to contribute to stabilization of kinetochore fibers of the mitotic spindle by acting as inter-microtubule bridge.
function_by_symbol.TAF1: TAF1 encodes TATA-box binding protein associated factor 1. The TFIID basal transcription factor complex plays a major role in the initiation of RNA polymerase II (Pol II)-dependent transcription. TFIID recognizes and binds promoters with or without a TATA box via its subunit TBP, a TATA-box-binding protein, and promotes assembly of the pre-initiation complex (PIC). The TFIID complex consists of TBP and TBP-associated factors (TAFs), including TAF1, TAF2, TAF3, TAF4, TAF5, TAF6, TAF7, TAF8, TAF9, TAF10, TAF11, TAF12 and TAF13.
function_by_symbol.TAF15: TAF15 encodes TATA-box binding protein associated factor 15. It is an RNA and ssDNA-binding protein that may play specific roles during transcription initiation at distinct promoters. It binds to ssRNA containing the consensus sequence 5'-AGGUAA-3'. It can enter the pre-initiation complex together with the RNA polymerase II (Pol II).
function_by_symbol.TAFAZZIN: TAFAZZIN encodes tafazzin. Based in part on similarity, its role in cellular physiology is to improve mitochondrial performance. CL is critical for the coassembly of lipids and proteins in mitochondrial membranes, for instance, remodeling of the acyl groups of CL in the mitochondrial inner membrane affects the assembly and stability of respiratory chain complex IV and its supercomplex forms. It catalyzes the transacylation between phospholipids and lysophospholipids, with the highest rate being between phosphatidylcholine (1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine or PC) and CL.
function_by_symbol.TAP1: TAP1 encodes antigen peptide transporter 1. It uses the chemical energy of ATP to export peptides against the concentration gradient. It typically transports intracellular peptide antigens of 8 to 13 amino acids that arise from cytosolic proteolysis via IFNG-induced immunoproteasome. It binds peptides with free N- and C-termini, the first three and the C-terminal residues being critical.
function_by_symbol.TAP2: TAP2 encodes antigen peptide transporter 2. It uses the chemical energy of ATP to export peptides against the concentration gradient. It typically transports intracellular peptide antigens of 8 to 13 amino acids that arise from cytosolic proteolysis via IFNG-induced immunoproteasome. It binds peptides with free N- and C-termini, the first three and the C-terminal residues being critical.
function_by_symbol.TARBP2: TARBP2 encodes TARBP2 subunit of RISC loading complex. Based in part on similarity, it is required for formation of the RNA induced silencing complex (RISC). It forms part of the RISC loading complex (RLC), also known as the micro-RNA (miRNA) loading complex (miRLC), which is composed of DICER1, AGO2 and TARBP2. May also play a role in the production of short interfering RNAs (siRNAs) from double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) by DICER1.
function_by_symbol.TBL1XR1: TBL1XR1 encodes f-box-like/WD repeat-containing protein TBL1XR1. It contributes to transcription activation mediated by nuclear receptors. It probably acts as integral component of the N-Cor corepressor complex that mediates the recruitment of the 19S proteasome complex, leading to the subsequent proteasomal degradation of N-Cor complex, thereby allowing cofactor exchange, and transcription activation.
function_by_symbol.TBX2: TBX2 encodes T-box transcription factor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor which acts as a transcriptional repressor. It may also function as a transcriptional activator. It binds to the palindromic T site 5'-TTCACACCTAGGTGTGAA-3' DNA sequence, or a half-site, which are present in the regulatory region of several genes.
function_by_symbol.TBX21: TBX21 encodes t-box transcription factor TBX21. Based in part on similarity, it activates transcription of a set of genes important for Th1 cell function, including those encoding IFN-gamma and the chemokine receptor CXCR3. It induces permissive chromatin accessibility and CpG methylation in IFNG. It activates IFNG and CXCR3 genes in part by recruiting chromatin remodeling complexes including KDM6B, a SMARCA4-containing SWI/SNF-complex, and an H3K4me2-methyltransferase complex to their promoters and all of these complexes serve to establish a more permissive chromatin state conducive with transcriptional activation.
function_by_symbol.TBX3: TBX3 encodes t-box transcription factor TBX3. Based in part on similarity, it binds to the palindromic T site 5'-TTCACACCTAGGTGTGAA-3' DNA sequence, or a half-site, which are present in the regulatory region of several genes. Probably plays a role in limb pattern formation. It is required for mammary placode induction, and maintenance of the mammary buds during development.
function_by_symbol.TBXT: TBXT encodes t-box transcription factor T. Based in part on similarity, it participates in the transcriptional regulation of genes required for mesoderm formation and differentiation. It binds to a palindromic T site 5'-TTCACACCTAGGTGTGAA-3' DNA sequence and activates gene transcription when bound to such a site.
function_by_symbol.TCF3: TCF3 encodes transcription factor E2-alpha. Based in part on similarity, heterodimers between TCF3 and tissue-specific basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) proteins play major roles in determining tissue-specific cell fate during embryogenesis, like muscle or early B-cell differentiation. It binds to the kappa-E2 site in the kappa immunoglobulin gene enhancer.
function_by_symbol.TCF7L2: TCF7L2 encodes transcription factor 7-like 2. It participates in the Wnt signaling pathway and modulates MYC expression by binding to its promoter in a sequence-specific manner. It functions as a repressor in the absence of CTNNB1, and as activator in its presence. It activates transcription from promoters with several copies of the Tcf motif 5'-CCTTTGATC-3' in the presence of CTNNB1.
function_by_symbol.TDG: TDG encodes G/T mismatch-specific thymine DNA glycosylase. It is a DNA glycosylase that plays a key role in active DNA demethylation: specifically recognizes and binds 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) in the context of CpG sites and mediates their excision through base-excision repair (BER) to install an unmethylated cytosine. It is also involved in DNA repair by acting as a thymine-DNA glycosylase that mediates correction of G/T mispairs to G/C pairs: in the DNA of higher eukaryotes, hydrolytic deamination of 5-methylcytosine to thymine leads to the formation of G/T mismatches. It is capable of hydrolyzing the carbon-nitrogen bond between the sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA and a mispaired thymine.
function_by_symbol.TEAD1: TEAD1 encodes transcriptional enhancer factor TEF-1. The core of this pathway is composed of a kinase cascade wherein MST1/MST2, in complex with its regulatory protein SAV1, phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2 in complex with its regulatory protein MOB1, which in turn phosphorylates and inactivates YAP1 oncoprotein and WWTR1/TAZ. It acts by mediating gene expression of YAP1 and WWTR1/TAZ, thereby regulating cell proliferation, migration and epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT) induction. The activation function appears to be mediated by a limiting cell-specific transcriptional intermediary factor (TIF).
function_by_symbol.TEK: TEK encodes angiopoietin-1 receptor. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for ANGPT1, ANGPT2 and ANGPT4 and regulates angiogenesis, endothelial cell survival, proliferation, migration, adhesion and cell spreading, reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton, but also maintenance of vascular quiescence. It has anti-inflammatory effects by preventing the leakage of pro-inflammatory plasma proteins and leukocytes from blood vessels. It is required for normal angiogenesis and heart development during embryogenesis.
function_by_symbol.TENT5C: TENT5C encodes terminal nucleotidyltransferase 5C. It catalyzes the transfer of one adenosine molecule from an ATP to an mRNA poly(A) tail bearing a 3'-OH terminal group and enhances mRNA stability and gene expression. It can also elongate RNA oligos ending with uridine molecule, provided that the sequence is adenosine-rich.
function_by_symbol.TENT5D: TENT5D encodes terminal nucleotidyltransferase 5D. It catalyzes the transfer of one adenosine molecule from an ATP to an mRNA poly(A) tail bearing a 3'-OH terminal group.
function_by_symbol.TERC: TERC produces the RNA template component of telomerase. The telomerase ribonucleoprotein combines this template with a reverse-transcriptase protein component to add TTAGGG repeats at chromosome ends. TERC therefore supplies sequence information for telomere extension rather than the catalytic protein itself. Regulation of telomerase activity is linked to telomere maintenance and cellular senescence.
function_by_symbol.TERT: TERT encodes the catalytic reverse-transcriptase component of telomerase. Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein enzyme essential for the replication of chromosome termini in most eukaryotes. It is the catalytic component of the teleromerase holoenzyme complex whose main activity is the elongation of telomeres by acting as a reverse transcriptase that adds simple sequence repeats to chromosome ends by copying a template sequence within the RNA component of the enzyme. It catalyzes the RNA-dependent extension of 3'-chromosomal termini with the 6-nucleotide telomeric repeat unit, 5'-TTAGGG-3'.
function_by_symbol.TET1: TET1 encodes methylcytosine dioxygenase TET1. Based in part on similarity, it plays therefore a role in many biological processes, including stem cell maintenance, T- and B-cell development, inflammation regulation, genomic imprinting, neural activity or DNA repair. It participates in the balance between pluripotency and lineage commitment of cells and plays a role in embryonic stem cells maintenance and inner cell mass cell specification.
function_by_symbol.TET3: TET3 encodes methylcytosine dioxygenase TET3. Based in part on similarity, it also mediates subsequent conversion of 5hmC into 5-formylcytosine (5fC), and conversion of 5fC to 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC). It selectively binds to the promoter region of target genes and contributes to regulate the expression of numerous developmental genes. It participates in DNA demethylation in the paternal pronucleus by mediating conversion of 5mC into 5hmC, 5fC and 5caC.
function_by_symbol.TEX12: TEX12 encodes testis-expressed protein 12. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the transverse central element of synaptonemal complexes (SCS), formed between homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase. It requires SYCP1 in order to be incorporated into the central element.
function_by_symbol.TFCP2: TFCP2 encodes alpha-globin transcription factor CP2. Based in part on similarity, it acts as part of the SSP (stage selector protein) complex. It facilitates the interaction of the gamma-globin genes with enhancer elements contained in the locus control region in fetal erythroid cells. It interacts by binding to the stage selector element (SSE) in the proximal gamma-globin promoter.
function_by_symbol.TFEB: TFEB encodes transcription factor EB. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, autophagy, lysosomal exocytosis, lipid catabolism, energy metabolism and immune response. It participates in the cellular response to amino acid availability by acting downstream of MTOR: in the presence of nutrients, TFEB phosphorylation by MTOR promotes its cytosolic retention and subsequent inactivation. It specifically recognizes and binds the CLEAR-box sequence (5'-GTCACGTGAC-3') present in the regulatory region of many lysosomal genes, leading to activate their expression, thereby playing a central role in expression of lysosomal genes.
function_by_symbol.TFG: TFG encodes protein TFG. It contributes to the normal dynamic function of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and its associated microtubules. It is required for secretory cargo traffic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus.
function_by_symbol.TFRC: TFRC encodes transferrin receptor protein 1. Based in part on similarity, the apotransferrin-receptor complex is then recycled to the cell surface with a return to neutral pH and the concomitant loss of affinity of apotransferrin for its receptor. Transferrin receptor is necessary for development of erythrocytes and the nervous system. It positively regulates T and B cell proliferation through iron uptake.
function_by_symbol.TGFBR1: TGFBR1 encodes TGF-beta receptor type-1. It transduces the TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and is thus regulating a plethora of physiological and pathological processes including cell cycle arrest in epithelial and hematopoietic cells, control of mesenchymal cell proliferation and differentiation, wound healing, extracellular matrix production, immunosuppression and carcinogenesis. The formation of the receptor complex composed of 2 TGFBR1 and 2 TGFBR2 molecules symmetrically bound to the cytokine dimer results in the phosphorylation and the activation of TGFBR1 by the constitutively active TGFBR2. The SMAD2-SMAD4 complex is subsequently translocated to the nucleus where it modulates the transcription of the TGF-beta-regulated genes.
function_by_symbol.TGFBR2: TGFBR2 encodes TGF-beta receptor type-2. It transduces the TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and thus regulates a plethora of physiological and pathological processes including cell cycle arrest in epithelial and hematopoietic cells, control of mesenchymal cell proliferation and differentiation, wound healing, extracellular matrix production, immunosuppression and carcinogenesis. The formation of the receptor complex composed of 2 TGFBR1 and 2 TGFBR2 molecules symmetrically bound to the cytokine dimer results in the phosphorylation and activation of TGFBR1 by the constitutively active TGFBR2. The SMAD2-SMAD4 complex is subsequently translocated to the nucleus where it modulates the transcription of the TGF-beta-regulated genes.
function_by_symbol.TGFBR3: TGFBR3 encodes transforming growth factor beta receptor type 3. Based in part on similarity, it is a cell surface receptor that regulates diverse cellular processes including cell proliferation, differentiation, migration, and apoptosis. It initiates BMP, inhibin, and TGF-beta signaling pathways by interacting with different ligands including TGFB1, BMP2, BMP5, BMP7 or GDF5. It promotes epithelial cell adhesion, focal adhesion formation and integrin signaling during epithelial cell spreading on fibronectin.
function_by_symbol.TGFBRAP1: TGFBRAP1 encodes transforming growth factor beta receptor associated protein 1. It contributes to the TGF-beta/activin signaling pathway. It associates with inactive heteromeric TGF-beta and activin receptor complexes, mainly through the type II receptor, and is released upon activation of signaling. The CORVET complex is proposed to function as a Rab5 effector to mediate early endosome fusion probably in specific endosome subpopulations.
function_by_symbol.THBD: THBD encodes thrombomodulin. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a cofactor for thrombin activation of protein C/PROC on the surface of vascular endothelial cells leading to initiation of the activated protein C anticoagulant pathway. It also accelerates the activation of the plasma carboxypeptidase B2/CPB2, which catalyzes removal of C-terminal basic amino acids from its substrates including kinins or anaphylatoxins leading to fibrinolysis inhibition.
function_by_symbol.TMEM147: TMEM147 encodes transmembrane protein 147. It forms part of the multi-pass translocon (MPT) complex that mediates insertion of multi-pass membrane proteins into the lipid bilayer of membranes. The MPT complex takes over after the SEC61 complex: following membrane insertion of the first few transmembrane segments of proteins by the SEC61 complex, the MPT complex occludes the lateral gate of the SEC61 complex to promote insertion of subsequent transmembrane regions. It also acts as a negative regulator of CHRM3 function, most likely by interfering with its trafficking to the cell membrane.
function_by_symbol.TMEM68: TMEM68 encodes DGAT1/2-independent enzyme synthesizing storage lipids. Based in part on similarity, it is a catalytic subunit of the alternative triglyceride biosynthesis pathway, which mediates formation of triacylglycerol from diacylglycerol and membrane phospholipids. It synthesizes triacylglycerol at the expense of membrane phospholipids, such as phosphatidylcholine (PC) and its ether-linked form (ePC), thereby altering the composition of membranes. The alternative triglyceride biosynthesis pathway is probably required to provide the energy required for rapid growth when fuel sources are limiting.
function_by_symbol.TNFAIP3: TNFAIP3 encodes tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3. It is an ubiquitin-editing enzyme that contains both ubiquitin ligase and deubiquitinase activities. It participates in immune and inflammatory responses signaled by cytokines, such as TNF and IL-1 beta, or pathogens via Toll-like receptors (TLRs) through terminating NF-kappa-B activity. It is an essential component of a ubiquitin-editing protein complex, comprising also RNF11, ITCH and TAX1BP1, that ensures the transient nature of inflammatory signaling pathways.
function_by_symbol.TNFRSF14: TNFRSF14 encodes tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 14. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor for four distinct ligands: The TNF superfamily members TNFSF14/LIGHT and homotrimeric LTA/lymphotoxin-alpha and the immunoglobulin superfamily members BTLA and CD160, altogether defining a complex stimulatory and inhibitory signaling network. It signals via the TRAF2-TRAF3 E3 ligase pathway to promote immune cell survival and differentiation. It participates in bidirectional cell-cell contact signaling between antigen presenting cells and lymphocytes.
function_by_symbol.TNFRSF1B: TNFRSF1B encodes tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 1B. It has high affinity for TNFSF2/TNF and approximately 5-fold lower affinity for LTA/TNFSF1. The TNF signaling pathway acts as a master regulator of the immune system, which either (1) promotes cell survival and inflammation by activating the canonical NF-kappa-B pathway or (2) trigger programmed cell death (apoptosis and necroptosis).
function_by_symbol.TOP1: TOP1 encodes DNA topoisomerase 1. Based in part on similarity, it releases the supercoiling and torsional tension of DNA introduced during the DNA replication and transcription by transiently cleaving and rejoining one strand of the DNA duplex. It introduces a single-strand break via transesterification at a target site in duplex DNA. The scissile phosphodiester is attacked by the catalytic tyrosine of the enzyme, resulting in the formation of a DNA-(3'-phosphotyrosyl)-enzyme intermediate and the expulsion of a 5'-OH DNA strand.
function_by_symbol.TOP2A: TOP2A encodes DNA topoisomerase 2-alpha. Based in part on similarity, it is a key decatenating enzyme that alters DNA topology by binding to two double-stranded DNA molecules, generating a double-stranded break in one of the strands, passing the intact strand through the broken strand, and religating the broken strand. May play a role in regulating the period length of BMAL1 transcriptional oscillation.
function_by_symbol.TOP2B: TOP2B encodes DNA topoisomerase II beta. It is a key decatenating enzyme that alters DNA topology by binding to two double-stranded DNA molecules, generating a double-stranded break in one of the strands, passing the intact strand through the broken strand, and religating the broken strand. It contributes to B-cell differentiation.
function_by_symbol.TOPBP1: TOPBP1 encodes DNA topoisomerase 2-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a scaffold protein that acts as a key protein-protein adapter in DNA replication and DNA repair. It is necessary for the loading of replication factors onto chromatin, including GMNC, CDC45, DNA polymerases and components of the GINS complex. It plays a central role in DNA repair by bridging proteins and promoting recruitment of proteins to DNA damage sites.
function_by_symbol.TP53BP1: TP53BP1 encodes TP53-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a double-strand break (DSB) repair protein involved in response to DNA damage, telomere dynamics and class-switch recombination (CSR) during antibody genesis. It contributes to the repair of double-strand DNA breaks (DSBs) in response to DNA damage by promoting non-homologous end joining (NHEJ)-mediated repair of DSBs and specifically counteracting the function of the homologous recombination (HR) repair protein BRCA1. It is required for immunoglobulin class-switch recombination (CSR) during antibody genesis, a process that involves the generation of DNA DSBs.
function_by_symbol.TPM3: TPM3 encodes tropomyosin alpha-3 chain. Based in part on similarity, it binds to actin filaments in muscle and non-muscle cells. It plays a central role, in association with the troponin complex, in the calcium dependent regulation of vertebrate striated muscle contraction. Smooth muscle contraction is regulated by interaction with caldesmon.
function_by_symbol.TPR: TPR encodes nucleoprotein TPR. It forms part of the nuclear pore complex (NPC), a complex required for the trafficking across the nuclear envelope. It acts as a scaffolding element in the nuclear phase of the NPC essential for normal nucleocytoplasmic transport of proteins and mRNAs, plays a role in the establishment of nuclear-peripheral chromatin compartmentalization in interphase, and in the mitotic spindle checkpoint signaling during mitosis. It negatively regulates both the association of CTE-containing mRNA with large polyribosomes and translation initiation.
function_by_symbol.TPSD1: TPSD1 encodes tryptase delta 1. Based in part on similarity, tryptase is the major neutral protease present in mast cells and is secreted upon the coupled activation-degranulation response of this cell type.
function_by_symbol.TRA: TRA is the T-cell receptor alpha locus, contributing the alpha chain of the alpha-beta receptor complex. The cell-surface receptor participates in peptide-antigen recognition and T-cell activation. TRA represents a receptor locus capable of generating a repertoire of antigen specificities, rather than a single fixed receptor directed at one particular antigen.
function_by_symbol.TRAF2: TRAF2 encodes TNF receptor-associated factor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that regulates activation of NF-kappa-B and JNK and plays a central role in the regulation of cell survival and apoptosis. It catalyzes 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitination of target proteins, such as BIRC3, IKBKE, MLST8, RIPK1 and TICAM1. Is an essential constituent of several E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes, where it promotes the ubiquitination of target proteins by bringing them into contact with other E3 ubiquitin ligases.
function_by_symbol.TRAF3: TRAF3 encodes TNF receptor-associated factor 3. It is a cytoplasmic E3 ubiquitin ligase that regulates various signaling pathways, such as the NF-kappa-B, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and interferon regulatory factor (IRF) pathways, and thus controls a lot of biological processes in both immune and non-immune cell types. It also acts as a constitutive negative regulator of the alternative NF-kappa-B pathway, which controls B-cell survival and lymphoid organ development. It is required for normal antibody isotype switching from IgM to IgG.
function_by_symbol.TRAF7: TRAF7 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase TRAF7. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin and SUMO-protein ligase that plays a role in different biological processes such as innate immunity, inflammation or apoptosis. It potentiates MAP3K3-mediated activation of JUN/AP1 and DDIT3 transcriptional regulators. It negatively regulates MYB transcriptional activity by sequestering it to the cytosol via SUMOylation.
function_by_symbol.TRAK1: TRAK1 encodes trafficking kinesin-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in the regulation of endosome-to-lysosome trafficking, including endocytic trafficking of EGF-EGFR complexes and GABA-A receptors. TRAK1 and RHOT form an essential protein complex that links KIF5 to mitochondria for light chain-independent, anterograde transport of mitochondria.
function_by_symbol.TRB: TRB is the T-cell receptor beta locus, containing variable, diversity, joining, and constant segments. During T-cell development, DNA rearrangement joins diversity and joining segments and then a variable segment; the constant region is incorporated by RNA splicing. Combinations of segments and junctional diversity help generate antigen specificity. The beta chain pairs with an alpha chain in the alpha-beta T-cell receptor.
function_by_symbol.TRG: TRG is the T-cell receptor gamma locus, containing variable, joining, and constant segments. Developing T cells join variable and joining segments by DNA rearrangement, while the constant region is incorporated by RNA splicing.
