Segment choice and junctional diversity contribute to receptor diversity. A functional gamma chain pairs with a delta chain, distinguishing this receptor type from alpha-beta T-cell receptors.
function_by_symbol.TRIM11: TRIM11 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase TRIM11. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that promotes the degradation of insoluble ubiquitinated proteins, including insoluble PAX6, poly-Gln repeat expanded HTT and poly-Ala repeat expanded ARX. It mediates PAX6 ubiquitination leading to proteasomal degradation, thereby modulating cortical neurogenesis. It may also inhibit PAX6 transcriptional activity, possibly in part by preventing the binding of PAX6 to its consensus sequences.
function_by_symbol.TRIM27: TRIM27 encodes zinc finger protein RFP. It is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination of various substrates and thereby plays a role in diffent processes including proliferation, innate immunity, apoptosis, immune response or autophagy. It functions as a regulator of retrograde transport: together with MAGEL2, mediates the formation of 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitin chains at 'Lys-220' of WASHC1, leading to promote endosomal F-actin assembly. It has a transcriptional repressor activity by cooperating with EPC1.
function_by_symbol.TRIM37: TRIM37 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase TRIM37. It is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase required to prevent centriole reduplication. It probably acts by ubiquitinating positive regulators of centriole reduplication. It mediates monoubiquitination of 'Lys-119' of histone H2A (H2AK119Ub), a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression: associates with some Polycomb group (PcG) multiprotein PRC2-like complex and mediates repression of target genes.
function_by_symbol.TRIM65: TRIM65 encodes tripartite motif containing 65. It is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that plays a role in several processes including innate immnity, autophagy or inflammation. It negatively regulates miRNAs by modulating the ubiquitination and stability of TNRC6A, a protein involved in RNA-mediated gene silencing by both micro-RNAs (miRNAs) and short interfering RNAs. This ubiquitination results in the suppressed expression of miR-138-5p leading to increased autophagy.
function_by_symbol.TRIP13: TRIP13 encodes pachytene checkpoint protein 2 homolog. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to chromosome recombination and chromosome structure development during meiosis. It is also needed for efficient completion of homologous synapsis by influencing crossover distribution along the chromosomes affecting both crossovers and non-crossovers pathways. It is also required for development of higher-order chromosome structures and is needed for synaptonemal-complex formation.
function_by_symbol.TRPS1: TRPS1 encodes zinc finger transcription factor Trps1. It binds specifically to GATA sequences and represses expression of GATA-regulated genes at selected sites and stages in vertebrate development. It regulates chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation. It executes multiple functions in proliferating chondrocytes, expanding the region of distal chondrocytes, activating proliferation in columnar cells and supporting the differentiation of columnar into hypertrophic chondrocytes.
function_by_symbol.TRUB1: TRUB1 encodes TruB pseudouridine synthase family member 1. It mediates pseudouridylation of mRNAs with the consensus sequence 5'-GUUCNANNC-3', harboring a stem-loop structure. It constitutes the major pseudouridine synthase acting on mRNAs. It also catalyzes pseudouridylation of some tRNAs, including synthesis of pseudouridine(55) from uracil-55, in the psi GC loop of a subset of tRNAs.
function_by_symbol.TSC1: TSC1 encodes hamartin. Based in part on similarity, the TSC-TBC complex acts as a GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for the small GTPase RHEB, a direct activator of the protein kinase activity of mTORC1. The TSC-TBC complex is inactivated in response to nutrients, relieving inhibition of mTORC1. It participates in microtubule-mediated protein transport via its ability to regulate mTORC1 signaling.
function_by_symbol.TSC2: TSC2 encodes tuberin. Based in part on similarity, it is the catalytic component of the TSC-TBC complex, a multiprotein complex that acts as a negative regulator of the canonical mTORC1 complex, an evolutionarily conserved central nutrient sensor that stimulates anabolic reactions and macromolecule biosynthesis to promote cellular biomass generation and growth. The TSC-TBC complex is inactivated in response to nutrients, relieving inhibition of mTORC1. It participates in microtubule-mediated protein transport via its ability to regulate mTORC1 signaling.
function_by_symbol.TSHR: TSHR encodes thyrotropin receptor. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor for the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) or thyrotropin. It also acts as a receptor for the heterodimeric glycoprotein hormone (GPHA2:GPHB5) or thyrostimulin. TSHR is coupled to G(s) proteins and mediates the activation of adenylate cyclase.
function_by_symbol.TUBGCP4: TUBGCP4 encodes tubulin gamma complex component 4. It forms part of the gamma-tubulin ring complex (gTuRC) which mediates microtubule nucleation. The gTuRC regulates the minus-end nucleation of alpha-beta tubulin heterodimers that grow into microtubule protafilaments, a critical step in centrosome duplication and spindle formation.
function_by_symbol.TUBGCP6: TUBGCP6 encodes tubulin gamma complex component 6. It forms part of the gamma-tubulin ring complex (gTuRC) which mediates microtubule nucleation. The gTuRC regulates the minus-end nucleation of alpha-beta tubulin heterodimers that grow into microtubule protafilaments, a critical step in centrosome duplication and spindle formation.
function_by_symbol.TYK2: TYK2 encodes non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase TYK2. It plays both structural and catalytic roles in numerous interleukins and interferons (IFN-alpha/beta) signaling. It associates with heterodimeric cytokine receptor complexes and activates STAT family members including STAT1, STAT3, STAT4 or STAT6. The heterodimeric cytokine receptor complexes are composed of (1) a TYK2-associated receptor chain (IFNAR1, IL12RB1, IL10RB or IL13RA1), and (2) a second receptor chain associated either with JAK1 or JAK2.
function_by_symbol.U2AF1: U2AF1 encodes a component of the U2 auxiliary splicing factor that contributes to recognition of 3′ splice sites during pre-mRNA processing. It contributes to both constitutive and enhancer-dependent splicing by mediating protein-protein interactions and protein-RNA interactions required for accurate 3'-splice site selection. It recruits U2 snRNP to the branch point. It directly mediates interactions between U2AF2 and proteins bound to the enhancers and thus may function as a bridge between U2AF2 and the enhancer complex to recruit it to the adjacent intron.
function_by_symbol.UBE2D3: UBE2D3 encodes ubiquitin conjugating enzyme E2 D3. It accepts ubiquitin from the E1 complex and catalyzes its covalent attachment to other proteins. It cooperates with the E2 CDC34 and the SCF(FBXW11) E3 ligase complex for the polyubiquitination of NFKBIA leading to its subsequent proteasomal degradation. It functions as an initiator E2, priming the phosphorylated NFKBIA target at positions 'Lys-21' and/or 'Lys-22' with a monoubiquitin.
function_by_symbol.UBE2T: UBE2T encodes ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 T. It accepts ubiquitin from the E1 complex and catalyzes its covalent attachment to other proteins. It participates in mitomycin-C (MMC)-induced DNA repair. It functions as a specific E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme for the Fanconi anemia complex by associating with E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase FANCL and catalyzing monoubiquitination of FANCD2, a key step in the DNA damage pathway.
function_by_symbol.UBR5: UBR5 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase UBR5. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase involved in different protein quality control pathways in the cytoplasm and nucleus. It forms part of the N-end rule pathway: ubiquitinates proteins bearing specific N-terminal residues that are destabilizing according to the N-end rule, leading to their degradation. It recognizes type-1 N-degrons, containing positively charged amino acids (Arg, Lys and His).
function_by_symbol.UBXN11: UBXN11 encodes UBX domain protein 11. Based in part on similarity, it may participate in the reorganization of actin cytoskeleton mediated by RND1, RND2 and RND3. It promotes RHOA activation mediated by GNA12 and GNA13.
function_by_symbol.UCHL1: UCHL1 encodes ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1. Based in part on similarity, it abrogates the ubiquitination of multiple proteins including WWTR1/TAZ, EGFR, HIF1A and beta-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1/BACE1. It regulates amyloid precursor protein/APP processing by promoting BACE1 degradation resulting in decreased amyloid beta production.
function_by_symbol.UIMC1: UIMC1 encodes BRCA1-A complex subunit RAP80. It specifically recognizes and binds 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitin. It plays a central role in the BRCA1-A complex by specifically binding 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitinated histones H2A and H2AX at DNA lesions sites, leading to target the BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer to sites of DNA damage at double-strand breaks (DSBs). The BRCA1-A complex also possesses deubiquitinase activity that specifically removes 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitin on histones H2A and H2AX.
function_by_symbol.UPF1: UPF1 encodes regulator of nonsense transcripts 1. Based in part on similarity, it is an RNA-dependent helicase required for nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of aberrant mRNAs containing premature stop codons and which modulates the expression level of normal mRNAs. It is an ATP-dependent 5'-3' helicase active on RNA:DNA substrates with a 5'-RNA extension. Phosphorylated UPF1 is recognized by EST1B/SMG5, SMG6 and SMG7 which are thought to provide a link to the mRNA degradation machinery involving exonucleolytic and endonucleolytic pathways, and to serve as adapters to protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), thereby triggering UPF1 dephosphorylation and allowing the recycling of NMD factors.
function_by_symbol.USP28: USP28 encodes ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase 28. It participates in DNA damage induced apoptosis by specifically deubiquitinating proteins of the DNA damage pathway such as CLSPN. It is also involved in G2 DNA damage checkpoint, by deubiquitinating CLSPN, and preventing its degradation by the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C).
function_by_symbol.USP6: USP6 encodes ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase 6. It promotes plasma membrane localization of ARF6 and selectively regulates ARF6-dependent endocytic protein trafficking. It is able to initiate tumorigenesis by inducing the production of matrix metalloproteinases following NF-kappa-B activation. It may act as a GTPase-activating protein for RAB3A.
function_by_symbol.USP8: USP8 encodes ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase 8. It converts both 'Lys-48' an 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitin chains. Catalytic activity is enhanced in the M phase.
function_by_symbol.VAV2: VAV2 encodes guanine nucleotide exchange factor VAV2. Based in part on similarity, it is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for the Rho family of Ras-related GTPases. It contributes to angiogenesis. Its recruitment by phosphorylated EPHA2 is critical for EFNA1-induced RAC1 GTPase activation and vascular endothelial cell migration and assembly.
function_by_symbol.VEGFA: VEGFA encodes vascular endothelial growth factor A, long form. Based in part on similarity, it induces endothelial cell proliferation, promotes cell migration, inhibits apoptosis and induces permeabilization of blood vessels. It binds to the FLT1/VEGFR1 and KDR/VEGFR2 receptors, heparan sulfate and heparin. It binds to the NRP1/neuropilin-1 receptor.
function_by_symbol.VGLL2: VGLL2 encodes transcription cofactor vestigial-like protein 2. It may act as a specific coactivator for the mammalian TEFs. May play a role in the development of skeletal muscles.
function_by_symbol.VIM: VIM encodes vimentin. Based in part on similarity, vimentins are class-III intermediate filaments found in various non-epithelial cells, especially mesenchymal cells. Vimentin is attached to the nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, and mitochondria, either laterally or terminally. It contributes to cell directional movement, orientation, cell sheet organization and Golgi complex polarization at the cell migration front.
function_by_symbol.VPS37B: VPS37B encodes VPS37B subunit of ESCRT-I. It forms part of the ESCRT-I complex, a regulator of vesicular trafficking process. It is required for the sorting of endocytic ubiquitinated cargos into multivesicular bodies. It may participate in cell growth and differentiation.
function_by_symbol.VSTM2A: VSTM2A encodes v-set and transmembrane domain-containing protein 2A. It contributes to the regulation of the early stage of white and brown preadipocyte cell differentiation. It promotes adipogenic commitment of preadipocytes by increasing gene expression of the transcription factor PPARG in a BMP4-dependent signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.WDR73: WDR73 encodes WD repeat domain 73. It forms part of a multiprotein complex required for the assembly of the RNA endonuclease module of the integrator complex. It associates with INTS9 and INTS11 in the cytoplasm, stabilizing the INTS9-INTS11 heterodimer and blocking the active site of INTS11.
function_by_symbol.WHR1: WHR1 encodes winged helix repair factor 1. It is a DNA-binding protein which is required for efficient transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (TC-NER). It functions as part of a TC-NER complex which assembles and interacts with RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) when it stalls at DNA lesions. TC-NER complex subunit UVSSA binds to the GTF2H1/p62 subunit of the TFIIH transcription factor complex, tethering TFIIH to the TC-NER complex.
function_by_symbol.WRN: WRN encodes WRN RecQ like helicase. Based in part on similarity, it also has 3'->5' exonuclease activity towards double-stranded (ds)DNA with a 5'-overhang. It has no nuclease activity towards single-stranded (ss)DNA or blunt-ended dsDNA.
function_by_symbol.WWTR1: WWTR1 encodes WW domain-containing transcription regulator protein 1. The core of this pathway is composed of a kinase cascade wherein STK3/MST2 and STK4/MST1, in complex with its regulatory protein SAV1, phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2 in complex with its regulatory protein MOB1, which in turn phosphorylates and inactivates YAP1 oncoprotein and WWTR1/TAZ. It contributes to coupling SMADs to the transcriptional machinery such as the mediator complex. It regulates embryonic stem-cell self-renewal, promotes cell proliferation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
function_by_symbol.XBP1: XBP1 encodes x-box-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it acts as a transcription factor during endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress by regulating the unfolded protein response (UPR). It is required for cardiac myogenesis and hepatogenesis during embryonic development, and the development of secretory tissues such as exocrine pancreas and salivary gland. It participates in terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes to plasma cells and production of immunoglobulins.
function_by_symbol.XPA: XPA encodes DNA repair protein complementing XP-A cells. It participates in DNA nucleotide excision repair (NER). It initiates repair by binding to damaged sites with various affinities, depending on the photoproduct and the transcriptional state of the region. It is required for UV-induced CHEK1 phosphorylation and the recruitment of CEP164 to cyclobutane pyrimidine dimmers (CPD), sites of DNA damage after UV irradiation.
function_by_symbol.XPC: XPC encodes DNA repair protein complementing XP-C cells. It participates in global genome nucleotide excision repair (GG-NER) by acting as damage sensing and DNA-binding factor component of the XPC complex. It has only a low DNA repair activity by itself which is stimulated by RAD23B and RAD23A. This feature is proposed to be related to a dynamic sensor function: XPC can rapidly screen duplex DNA for non-hydrogen-bonded bases by forming a transient nucleoprotein intermediate complex which matures into a stable recognition complex through an intrinsic single-stranded DNA-binding activity.
function_by_symbol.XPO1: XPO1 encodes exportin 1, a nuclear-export receptor that transports cargo proteins and RNA-associated complexes from the nucleus to the cytoplasm. It mediates the nuclear export of cellular proteins (cargos) bearing a leucine-rich nuclear export signal (NES) and of RNAs. The directionality of nuclear export is thought to be conferred by an asymmetric distribution of the GTP- and GDP-bound forms of Ran between the cytoplasm and nucleus. It participates in U3 snoRNA transport from Cajal bodies to nucleoli.
function_by_symbol.XRCC1: XRCC1 encodes DNA repair protein XRCC1. It is a scaffold protein involved in DNA single-strand break repair by mediating the assembly of DNA break repair protein complexes. It negatively regulates ADP-ribosyltransferase activity of PARP1 during base-excision repair in order to prevent excessive PARP1 activity. It recognizes and binds poly-ADP-ribose chains: specifically binds auto-poly-ADP-ribosylated PARP1, limiting its activity.
function_by_symbol.XRCC2: XRCC2 encodes DNA repair protein XRCC2. It participates in the homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway of double-stranded DNA, thought to repair chromosomal fragmentation, translocations and deletions. It forms part of the RAD51 paralog protein complex BCDX2 which acts in the BRCA1-BRCA2-dependent HR pathway. BCDX2 binds predominantly to the intersection of the four duplex arms of the Holliday junction and to junction of replication forks.
function_by_symbol.XRCC3: XRCC3 encodes DNA repair protein XRCC3. It participates in the homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway of double-stranded DNA, thought to repair chromosomal fragmentation, translocations and deletions. It forms part of the RAD51 paralog protein complex CX3 which acts in the BRCA1-BRCA2-dependent HR pathway. It forms part of a PALB2-scaffolded HR complex containing BRCA2 and RAD51C and which is thought to play a role in DNA repair by HR.
function_by_symbol.XRCC4: XRCC4 encodes DNA repair protein XRCC4. It functions as a scaffold protein that regulates recruitment of other proteins to DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs). It associates with NHEJ1/XLF to form alternating helical filaments that bridge DNA and act like a bandage, holding together the broken DNA until it is repaired. The XRCC4-NHEJ1/XLF subcomplex binds to the DNA fragments of a DSB in a highly diffusive manner and robustly bridges two independent DNA molecules, holding the broken DNA fragments in close proximity to one other.
function_by_symbol.XRCC5: XRCC5 encodes X-ray repair cross complementing 5. It is a DNA-binding protein critical for the DNA damage response, specifically in repairing double-strand breaks (DSBs) via the classical non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway. It forms a heterodimer with XRCC6 (Ku70), creating the Ku70:Ku80 heterodimer (Ku complex), which serves as a DNA end-binding complex. It primarily binds DSBs and recruits essential repair factors, assembling the core long-range NHEJ complex to facilitate the alignment and ligation of broken DNA ends.
function_by_symbol.XRCC6: XRCC6 encodes DNA repair protein Ku70. It is a DNA-binding protein critical for the DNA damage response, specifically in repairing double-strand breaks (DSBs) via the classical non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway. It forms a heterodimer with XRCC5 (Ku80), creating the Ku70:Ku80 heterodimer (Ku complex), which serves as a DNA end-binding complex. It primarily binds DSBs and recruits essential repair factors, assembling the core long-range NHEJ complex to facilitate the alignment and ligation of broken DNA ends.
function_by_symbol.YAP1: YAP1 encodes transcriptional coactivator YAP1. Based in part on similarity, the Hippo signaling pathway core involves a kinase cascade featuring STK3/MST2 and STK4/MST1, along with its regulatory partner SAV1, which phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2 in complex with their regulatory protein, MOB1. This activation leads to the phosphorylation and inactivation of the YAP1 oncoprotein and WWTR1/TAZ. The transcriptional regulation of gene expression requires TEAD transcription factors and modulates cell growth, anchorage-independent growth, and induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
function_by_symbol.YES1: YES1 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Yes. It is a non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase that is involved in the regulation of cell growth and survival, apoptosis, cell-cell adhesion, cytoskeleton remodeling, and differentiation. It participates in the phosphorylation of specific junctional components such as CTNND1 by stimulating the FYN and FER tyrosine kinases at cell-cell contacts. It participates in CD95L/FASLG signaling pathway and mediates AKT-mediated cell migration.
function_by_symbol.YLPM1: YLPM1 encodes YLP motif-containing protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to the reduction of telomerase activity during differentiation of embryonic stem cells by binding to the core promoter of TERT and controlling its down-regulation.
function_by_symbol.YWHAE: YWHAE encodes 14-3-3 protein epsilon. Based in part on similarity, it is an adapter protein implicated in the regulation of a large spectrum of both general and specialized signaling pathways. It binds to a large number of partners, usually by recognition of a phosphoserine or phosphothreonine motif. It positively regulates phosphorylated protein HSF1 nuclear export to the cytoplasm.
function_by_symbol.ZBTB7A: ZBTB7A encodes zinc finger and BTB domain-containing protein 7A. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that represses the transcription of a wide range of genes involved in cell proliferation and differentiation. It negatively regulates SMAD4 transcriptional activity in the TGF-beta signaling pathway through these two mechanisms. It collaborates with transcription factors like RELA to modify the accessibility of gene transcription regulatory regions to secondary transcription factors.
function_by_symbol.ZFHX3: ZFHX3 encodes zinc finger homeobox protein 3. Based in part on similarity, it inhibits the enhancer element of the AFP gene by binding to its AT-rich core sequence. It regulates the circadian locomotor rhythms via transcriptional activation of neuropeptidergic genes which are essential for intercellular synchrony and rhythm amplitude in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the brain.
function_by_symbol.ZNF516: ZNF516 encodes zinc finger protein 516. Based in part on similarity, may also play a role in the cellular response to replication stress.
function_by_symbol.ZNRF3: ZNRF3 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase ZNRF3. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by mediating the ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of Wnt receptor complex components Frizzled and LRP6. It acts on both canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
function_by_symbol.ZRSR2: ZRSR2 encodes a splicing factor important for recognition and processing of introns, particularly those handled by the minor spliceosome. It selectively interacts with the 3'-splice site of U2- and U12-type pre-mRNAs and promotes different steps in U2 and U12 intron splicing.
function_by_symbol.SPOP: SPOP encodes a substrate-recognition adaptor for a CUL3-based ubiquitin-ligase assembly. Its MATH domain recognizes short consensus sequences in protein substrates, while its BTB region and an adjacent helical structure support CUL3 binding. SPOP can form dimers, allowing multiple substrate-recognition sites to cooperate. This architecture connects selective substrate binding with ubiquitination, while distinguishing the adaptor from the catalytic functions of the complete ligase assembly.
